    Authoring Lessons Log¶

    Status: Accepted | Updated: 2026-07-25 Serves: A11 (structural quality tools across the corpus) Validated by: uv run python scripts/check_lessons_log.py

    Note on this first landing. The lessons below were learned building a three-book 16+ gamebook series (the Wyrmreach chain), and several Ref cells cite that series' spec, skeleton, and filled-story artifacts. Those artifacts are not part of this change: they land in a separate follow-up push so the process and tooling work can be reviewed on its own, alongside the other in-flight revisions to story development. Every lesson and every tooling change here stands without them; the story-dependent tests skip until they arrive (6 skips in the suite today), and the two Wyrmreach design and report documents are included because they are the evidence base each lesson cites.

    Every story development run appends here. The point is that a lesson learned once becomes a change to the tooling rather than folklore an author has to rediscover, so each row carries a proposed change and a status that tracks whether it landed.

    How to use this log¶

    When to append. At the end of any authoring run: a new story or series book, a skeleton promotion, a fill pass, or a validator/gate change made in service of authoring. If the run produced no lesson, append nothing; an empty run is a real outcome.

    What counts as a lesson. Something a future author or a future tooling change should act on. Three tests, any one of which qualifies it:

    1. It cost real iteration to discover (a rule interaction, a calibration, an ordering constraint).
    2. The tooling let a defect through, or reported it in a way that did not point at the cause.
    3. It would be re-learned from scratch by the next person, because nothing in the repo records it.

    A one-off typo is not a lesson. "The gate reports band membership, so the floor reads as a pass" is.

    Fields.

    Field Rule
    ID AL-NNN, sequential, never reused or renumbered.
    Date ISO date the lesson was recorded.
    Source The run that produced it (story slug, series book, or workstream).
    Category One of validator, tooling, authoring-craft, scale, metadata, process, docs, product.
    Lesson What is true, stated so it is actionable without reading the source run.
    Proposed change The change that would stop this recurring, or none (craft note) when the lesson is guidance rather than a code change.
    Status open, accepted, applied, rejected, or superseded.
    Ref Commit, PR, file, or doc. Required when status is applied, rejected, or superseded.

    Review cadence. Sweep the open rows whenever a phase is planned. An open row that has survived two phase boundaries is either genuinely low value (mark it rejected, with the reason in Ref) or it is real debt being avoided; either way, decide rather than let it sit.

    Status discipline. accepted means the change is agreed but unbuilt, and it must appear in a plan somewhere. applied means the change is merged and the Ref proves it. Nothing moves to applied on the strength of intent.

    Catalog counts inside a row are dated by that row's Date. A lesson that says "20 of 61 skeletons" records what a sweep returned on the day it ran, and is never rewritten when the catalog grows; current totals live in catalog-census.md (UW-G24).

    A count a row quotes from somewhere else keeps its own date, not the row's. A lesson that re-measures a prior claim carries two figures, and only the new one belongs to the row's Date. Give the quoted figure its source date inline, or mark it undated when the source never carried one. Without that, the rule above silently backdates the quoted figure to the day the row was written, which is the error the row exists to correct.

    AL-023 2026-07-25 wyrmreach b1-b3 tooling The shipped client never sends choice_path, so the server-side engine replay that exists to stop a forged current_node/var_state/path is dormant (api/reading.py carries the #ASSUME admitting it).     AL-024 2026-07-25 adversarial review tooling Committing a 746-node skeleton falsified the stated derivation of a resource cap without breaking anything. api/schemas.py:38-52 derives VISIT_SET_MAX_LENGTH from "the largest currently-authored skeleton is the-ashfall-expedition.json with 505 nodes ... so 505 is the exact real ceiling", and tells the reader not to invent numbers. The largest is now 746. Not a live bug: visit_set resets per read-through (player/engine.ts::start) and shrinks on undo (back() replays from the start), and book 3's depth is 74, so a real read never approaches 505. Nothing tests the constant against the catalog, so the false basis is invisible. Update the derivation and the number to the real largest skeleton, and add a lockstep test asserting the constant matches the largest production_eligible skeleton in skeletons/, so the next oversized book fails a test instead of quietly invalidating a comment. Raising an audit-derived (F8) cap wants the audit owner's sign-off, so recommend rather than change unilaterally. open api/schemas.py:38-52, tests/unit/test_schemas.py
    AL-025 2026-07-25 adversarial review process An adversarial review is only as good as its ability to finish. Four review agents died on a session limit having delivered no findings, and the only value recovered came from two half-formed leads left in their reasoning traces. The reasoning trace, not the final report, was the durable artifact. For any delegated review, ask for findings incrementally (highest-value first) rather than one report at the end, so a truncated run still yields something. Recover partial work from subagents/agent-*.jsonl rather than assuming a failed agent produced nothing. applied this review; leads chased manually and closed
    AL-026 2026-07-25 adversarial review authoring-craft Breadth built from terminating leaves halves the typical read. Reproduced with player/engine.StoryEngine over 3,000 condition-aware random reads: book 1 (305 nodes) has a median read of 11 pages / 650 words; book 3 (746 nodes) has a median of 5 pages / 302 words of a 42,085-word book. Termination density is identical (22.3% vs 22.5% of choices land straight on an ending), so the extra 441 nodes went into width made of failure leaves, not into reader-visible journey. 7 endings sit within two taps of the start, 3 decision nodes have every choice end the book, and 3,000 random reads reached only 94 of 232 endings. This qualifies AL-009: hanging rooms off an act hub does control depth, but paying for breadth in terminating leaves makes the book feel smaller the bigger it gets. Author breadth as reconvergent detours, not terminal leaves: a room should more often cost vigor and rejoin than end the run. PL-17's endings floor actively pushes toward terminal leaves at gamebook breadth, so the floor and this lesson are in tension and the floor's shape should be revisited. applied 45 shallowest failure leaves converted to vigor-costing pass-throughs; median read 5 -> 20 pages, endings reached 39% -> 56%; gate clean, chain clean, endings exactly on the 187 floor
    AL-027 2026-07-25 adversarial review validator Nothing constrains the typical path length. PL-20 floors only the fastest satisfying path (37 nodes for this cell), which book 3 satisfies at 52, while the median actual read is 5 pages. A book can pass every scale rule and still hand most readers a 90-second encounter. Add a scale advisory on expected read length over the walk machinery validator/walk.py already has: warn when the median uniform-walk playthrough falls below a per-cell page floor, or when more than ~20% of a node's choices terminate. Roughly 20 lines on existing infrastructure, and it would have caught AL-026 before the fill pass. open validator/walk.py, validator/policy.py
    AL-028 2026-07-25 adversarial review product K6's "found N of M endings" replay motivator inverts at large M. At M=232 a finished read reports "1 of 232" (0.4%), and EndingsBadge silently drops its dot row above MAX_DOTS = 10, removing the only kid-legible part of the mechanic precisely for the books that most need replay motivation. Part of the denominator is also effectively unreachable: 3,000 random reads found 94 of 232. Stop showing a raw denominator above a threshold: milestone framing ("3 new endings found, lots more to go") with a tier ladder, or scope the denominator to a curated signature-endings subset. EndingsProgress and EndingsBadge must share the threshold so the ending screen and the shelf never disagree. open frontend/src/reader/EndingsProgress.tsx:60-65, frontend/src/library/EndingsBadge.tsx:19-40
    AL-029 2026-07-25 adversarial review product The reader progress bar is visit_set.length / story.nodes.length, so it measures corpus coverage, not route progress. A median book-3 read shows 1% and then snaps to 100% at the ending screen; the bigger the book the more broken the signal. The numeric label is already suppressed as untrustworthy, but the aria-label still announces "5 of 746 pages explored". Make in-read progress route-relative (path length against distance-to-nearest-ending from the current node, precomputable from the walk the validator already does), or show "Page 5" for large books. Corpus coverage belongs on the shelf card, not in the reader chrome. open frontend/src/reader/readerProgress.ts:7-11, ReaderChrome.tsx:88
    AL-030 2026-07-25 adversarial review product Every page turn synchronously replays the entire read from page 1: canGoBack calls back(), which DFS-replays the recorded path, and discards everything but a boolean. Compounding it, nodeIndex rebuilds a 746-entry Map on every engine entry point, so a depth-71 replay performs ~285 rebuilds. Measured O(depth x nodes): 26 ms at depth 70 on a container CPU, and a BACK press pays it three times, so a phone plausibly freezes 300ms+ on the one control built for children who mis-tap. Cost grows with the depth the book is designed to reward. Memoize the node index and intBounds per Storybook in a WeakMap (story identity is stable for the reader's lifetime, satisfying the existing #ASSUME); stop canGoBack recomputing an answer it throws away; short-circuit the common "no" case off the render path. open frontend/src/player/engine.ts:17-19,325-347, reader/Reader.tsx:216, player/machine.ts:99-111
    AL-031 2026-07-25 adversarial review product No response compression is configured anywhere in the stack (no GZipMiddleware in app.py, nothing in either compose file), so a story download ships 405 KB instead of 107 KB and the 3-book series costs 750 KB instead of 202 KB. Separately, list_library and /v1/reading-history select(StorybookVersion) whole-row including the blob JSONB for every book, decoding 768 KB of prose per shelf render to produce three small cards; the reading-history call fires on every ending-screen mount, which at a 5-page median read is constantly. Add GZipMiddleware(minimum_size=1024), a one-line ~4x win on the one step where a child waits with nothing to do. Separately, denormalise title, node_count, ending_count and ending_node_ids onto StorybookVersion at publish time so the listing paths never load prose. applied GZipMiddleware(minimum_size=1024) in app.py; the listing-path denormalisation half stays open under this id
    AL-032 2026-07-25 adversarial review product Reconnecting mid-read can teleport a child backwards to an earlier page and remount the reader, from this device's own queued past. persist() updates revisionRef only on saved, never on queued, so after offline reading the live save carries a stale base revision; the replay-on-reconnect advances the server revision, the next tap 409s, and the 409 handler adopts the server row unconditionally and bumps readerKey to remount. The existing #ASSUME deliberately accepts losing position to another device, but explicitly reasons about "another device advanced this story's row" and does not contemplate this case. A 74-choice offline read queues 74 sequential writes, so the 409 window is proportional to how much the child read offline. Traced end to end, not executed. Collapse the offline queue to the newest state per (profile, storybook) before replay so 74 round-trips become 1; advance revisionRef on queued; and guard the adopt branch so a current_row that is a strict prefix of the local path is recognised as this device's own stale past and re-saved rather than adopted. open frontend/src/reader/ReaderPage.tsx:296,304-305,317-337, offline/sync.ts:277-325, api/reading.py:363-371
    AL-033 2026-07-25 adversarial review validator Safety hole. _screen_all_nodes calls the bright-line classifiers once per node in a sequential loop guarded by if openai_key and openai_reason is None, so the FIRST ClassifierUnavailable disables that classifier for every remaining node, with no retry and no per-node coverage record. At 746 nodes Stage 0 makes 1,492 sequential third-party calls, which is exactly the shape that trips a Perspective ~1 QPS quota or an OpenAI per-minute limit; a 429 at node 50 leaves 93% of the book unscreened for sexual/minors, self-harm/instructions and illicit/violent. The resulting report is indistinguishable from a fully-screened clean one apart from one whole-story ADVISORY, and summary.hard_block/soft_flag are unaffected, so submit and approve both pass. Verified by reading the loop; the docstring states the no-retry behaviour outright. Track per-node classifier coverage and emit a FLAG, not an advisory, naming the unscreened node count and ids, so the story cannot reach in_review clean. Add bounded retry with backoff plus a concurrency limit so a rate limit is absorbed rather than abandoning the book. Make submit/approve refuse a report declaring incomplete Stage-0 coverage. applied moderation/classifiers.py: per-node coverage, bounded retry, circuit breaker, and a gating classifier_coverage_incomplete FLAG; 6 new tests
    AL-034 2026-07-25 adversarial review scale One import of this book is ~2,986 strictly sequential provider round trips (2 classifier calls plus 2 review calls per node, plus 2 whole-story stages), with no gather, semaphore, batching or call budget, all inside one Postgres transaction that also holds SELECT FOR UPDATE on the Storybook row. That is a 40 to 100 minute idle in transaction session against a pooler configured for transaction mode, and any single failure discards the entire run with no checkpoint or resume. Bound the per-node stages with a concurrency semaphore and a per-story call/time budget that records an explicit "moderation incomplete" finding when exceeded. Split the import: commit the draft first, then moderate in short transactions, persisting findings incrementally so a retry re-screens only unscreened nodes. approve already refuses a version with no moderation report, so a committed unmoderated draft is safe to leave behind. open moderation/stages.py:196-268, pipeline.py:98, generation/import_cli.py:92-119
    AL-035 2026-07-25 adversarial review scale run_gate is a measured 3.72 second synchronous CPU burn on this book and is called inline from three async def handlers with no to_thread, so it stalls the whole event loop: every passage edit, an admin rescreen sweep, and validate_version, which is guardian-reachable and therefore a cheap self-DoS on the entire API. Wrap all three in anyio.to_thread.run_sync, cache the gate report per (storybook_id, version) so validate_version returns the stored report, and rate-limit it. applied anyio.to_thread.run_sync around run_gate in api/node_edit.py, api/generation.py, moderation/rescreen.py
    AL-036 2026-07-25 adversarial review product ADR-005 makes a human's recorded approval the only path to a child, and at 746 nodes that surface cannot deliver it: the review view ships the whole blob (measured 444 KB), renders all 746 passages, 232 ending badges and 1,030 choice rows unvirtualized in one DOM, and offers no pagination, no per-node reviewed state, no resume, and one Approve button at the bottom. A reviewer cannot read 42,085 words in one page load, so the recorded approval attests to far less than it claims. The queue and the guardian browse listing separately load every book's full blob to compute a title and a count. Add node-range pagination and stop echoing the whole blob; virtualize the read-through; persist per-node review progress keyed by (storybook_id, version, node_id, reviewer) so the approval record can state what fraction was actually read. Project listings in SQL or denormalise title/ending_count/flagged_count at publish time. open api/review_surface.py:100-117, api/approval.py:222-285, frontend/src/admin/ReviewDetailPage.tsx:534-565
    AL-037 2026-07-25 adversarial review tooling Import silently rewrites the authored series block. embed_series_block replaces the declared series_id, book_index, is_final and series_entry_node with DB-derived values, and nothing anywhere compares the declared book_index to the assigned one, so import order becomes chain order. carries_state is likewise taken from the Series row, whose value is derived from that row's own age band, so a mismatched row silently rewrites all three 16+ books to carries_state: false; SR-6 and SR-7 both still pass, and the campaign degrades to three episodic books with no error at import, approval, or read. --job (the only route that stamps skeleton_slug, runs the Stage 1 fidelity gate, and enables the leaf-diversity guard) and --series-id (the only route that links a series) are mutually exclusive, so no combination produces a correct Tier-2 series. Compare declared against assigned in embed_series_block and raise on mismatch rather than overwrite; preserve declared is_final; check Series.age_band and Series.family_id. Worst case rather than canonical case, because PL-26 is a CEILING and must fire when ANY equally fast walk is a corridor.     AL-126 2026-08-07 Wave-1 parallel agent dispatch, persistent-characters runtime plan (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime), Task 10's commit process Running pre-commit while other agents hold uncommitted, unstaged edits in the same shared worktree is unsafe, and not for the reason a "no concurrent git writes" rule protects against. pre-commit stashes unstaged changes before running its hooks and restores them afterward; a concurrent agent's write landing inside that stash/restore window can be silently reverted by the restore, with no error anywhere in the output, only a bland "Restored changes from ...patch..." line that reads exactly like success. The other agents' git-write prohibition protects the index; it does nothing for this hazard, since the stash is triggered by any pre-commit invocation, including one run by an agent that itself made no other git-write violation. Document in the parallel-dispatch coordination pattern (wherever concurrent-worktree agent rules are recorded) that pre-commit must not run while any other agent in the same worktree may still be mid-write; batch commits after every in-flight agent has reported, against a quiescent tree, one group at a time. open UW-C61
    AL-127 2026-08-07 Task 11 (promoting the-storm-chasers-club to Tier 2), persistent-characters runtime plan (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) validator Introducing a dedicated build node to set a character's archetype, with each of the six archetype choices converging on it, silently disqualifies the sorting_hat topology. validator/topology.py's sorting_hat admissibility check disqualifies any node with in-degree >= 2, and a build node fed by six archetype-setting choices has in-degree 6 by construction.     AL-129 2026-08-08 Task 12 (13-16 stat-envelope gamebook pilot; the pilot was withdrawn from the branch on 2026-08-08 and is preserved out of tree, so no skeleton path is cited here), persistent-characters runtime plan (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) validator A stat-envelope book (accepts_character declaring might/wits/nerve, each immutable per the design's "seeded, not built in-story" cost model) cannot gate a choice condition directly on a stat's threshold value without tripping a blocking L2-11 dead-branch error: validator/layer2.py::_check_dead_branches walks only the book's single declared-initial baseline configuration with zero accepts_character awareness, so a stat == 0 branch is unconditionally unreachable in baseline whenever the book's own declared initial is stat: 1, regardless of what the envelope proves reachable. CH-3a's union-quantified walk does not suppress this, because L2-11 is raised independently on the baseline walk itself. The design spec's section 4.3 "archetype = 0" build-node idiom is the analogous fix for the archetype variable, but does not transfer to stat books, which deliberately have no in-story mutating node (that absence is exactly what keeps the 27-state walk cheap per the design's section 4.5). Working fix (authoring-only, no validator or design-doc change): pair every stat-gated choice with an auxiliary ordinary (non-canonical) boolean resolve, reset by an unconditioned binary player choice immediately before the gate, and XOR-combine it with the stat threshold so the pair collapses to depend only on resolve at the fixed baseline value (both branches reachable via ordinary play, satisfying L2-11) while genuinely differentiating on the stat at other envelope states (for CH-3a/CH-3b/CH-4's per-state walks). Verified empirically: baseline walk 530 configs; all 27 envelope states also 530 configs each, zero per-walk size cost. The workaround is what killed the pilot, and that is the larger half of the lesson. Because the XOR pairing requires an unconditioned player choice able to flip the outcome immediately before every gate, the reader cannot perceive their stat deciding anything: the stat becomes a hidden modifier behind a coin flip the reader just made. Applied across a whole book it made all 14 stations mechanically identical, and the pilot read as scaffolding rather than a gamebook, so it was withdrawn from the branch on 2026-08-08 and preserved out of tree rather than shipped. A cost model that measures only configuration count therefore missed the cost that mattered: the workaround is free in walk time and expensive in reader-perceptible agency, and nothing in the gate could have reported the second. Two parts, and the second is the real decision. (1) Done on this branch, uncommitted: the L2-11-vs-immutable-stat interaction and the resolve/XOR pattern are now documented in the two docs an author actually reads, .claude/skills/cyo-author/reference/skeleton-format.md ("The stat-gate wall") and docs/architecture/story-skeletons.md, each stating plainly that the workaround leaves the reader unable to perceive the choice. The design spec is not the right home; authors do not read it. (2) Open and undecided: whether validator/layer2.py::_check_dead_branches should become envelope-aware, quantifying reachability over the entry states accepts_character declares instead of the baseline configuration alone. That would remove the need for the workaround and make a genuine stat gamebook authorable, but it is a validator change to a rule every skeleton in the catalog is already gated by, so its blast radius is catalog-wide and it needs a measured re-gate of the whole catalog before anyone commits to it. Not proposed as decided; proposed as the question to answer before another stat-envelope pilot is attempted. open UW-C64
    AL-130 2026-08-08 D-2 gate delivery (scripts/check_rad_citations.py), persistent-characters runtime plan (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) tooling A debt baseline generated from the working tree grandfathers the generating workstream's own new debt, and no amount of shrinking the baseline can surface it. rad-citation-baseline.toml was written by running --write-baseline over the tree as it then stood, which already contained src/cyo_adventure/validator/character.py, a file this workstream created. Its CH-2 #VERIFY cited test_canonical_bounds_are_read_by_the_validator, a test that never existed. The row was absorbed as pre-existing debt indistinguishable from the 122 genuine ones, the gate went green on its first live run, and the defect would have shipped inside the very commit that introduced the gate meant to catch it. Found only by intersecting the baseline's file list with the branch's changed-file list, which is not a check anything runs. The general shape: a grandfathering baseline defines "pre-existing" as "present when I looked", but the author is looking at a tree that already contains their own work, so the baseline's own generation is the moment the distinction is lost. Make --write-baseline refuse to add a row whose file is added or modified relative to origin/main, printing those citations as errors to fix rather than debt to inherit, so a baseline can only ever grandfather work that predates the branch writing it. Pair it with a CI assertion that the baseline never grows between origin/main and a PR head, which turns shrink-only from a comment in the file's header into something enforced. Until that lands, the manual check is the file-list intersection described above, and it belongs in the D-2 handoff as a step the receiving team repeats each time they regenerate. open UW-C65
    AL-131 2026-08-08 Final whole-branch review, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) validator The CH-* rules prove an envelope is declared and survivable, never that it is observable. the-storm-chasers-club's Tier 2 promotion passed all eight CH rules and the full gate while being behaviourally inert in two independent ways. Its single archetype-gated choice (r_a_fix/c_rafix_explain, condition {"==": [{"var": "archetype"}, 4]}) sits behind an only-inbound edge (c_rapick_window) whose effect sets archetype = 4, so the condition is unconditionally true for every one of the seven declared entry states; and its six archetype-setting choices are ungated with no bypass, which the same branch's skeleton-format.md explicitly forbids. CH-3b and CH-4 walk every entry state and correctly found all 121 nodes and all 25 endings reachable, which is precisely why they were silent: a tautology is maximally reachable, so a reachability rule reads a dead gate as a perfectly healthy one. The 13-16 stat pilot failed the same observability test through an unrelated mechanism (AL-129's XOR workaround), so two pilots built to the same spec were both imperceptible while both passing the gate. The promotion was withdrawn. Add a CH rule that fails a condition on a canonical character variable when every inbound path to the gate sets that variable to a value satisfying the condition, i.e. a gate whose truth is invariant across the declared envelope; and a companion rule that a book declaring accepts_character must have at least one condition whose truth varies across the declared entry states. Both are computable from the per-state walk validator/character.py already performs, so neither needs new traversal machinery. Until one of them exists, no gate run can distinguish a character-aware book from a book that merely says it is one, and the CH family's passing verdict should not be read as evidence of an observable envelope. open UW-C73
    AL-132 2026-08-08 Final whole-branch review fix wave, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) tooling A hand-maintained happy-path fixture turns adding a gated CI job into a multi-test breakage whose error names the shell instead of the cause. tests/unit/test_ci_gate_contract.py executes the extracted CI Gate script against a hardcoded ALL_SUCCESS dict holding one *_RESULT key per gated job. Adding the rad-citations job broke seven tests at once with bash: RAD_CITATIONS_RESULT: unbound variable under the script's set -u, so every assertion pointed at bash and none pointed at the missing entry. The tempting workaround, defaulting the variable inside the workflow with a :-success fallback, is worse than the breakage: it makes an absent job result read as a pass, which is precisely the issue #594 defect this gate exists to prevent. The fixture was data that had to track the job list, not a test to be relaxed, and the distinction is what makes the difference between updating it and weakening it. Derive the fixture from the workflow instead of hand-listing it. Applied: ALL_SUCCESS now spreads dict.fromkeys(RESULT_VAR_TO_JOB, "success"), reusing the mapping the module already parses out of the gate's own env: block, so any newly gated job joins the happy path automatically. RELEASE_PR stays hand-written on purpose, since it reads .outputs.release_pr rather than .result and so is deliberately outside that mapping. open UW-C74. The fix is written on the unmerged, unpushed branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime (tests/unit/test_ci_gate_contract.py, ALL_SUCCESS derived from RESULT_VAR_TO_JOB), so it is not applied: this log's own status discipline says applied means the change is merged and the Ref proves it, and nothing moves to applied on the strength of intent. Flip it on the squash SHA. Run context for the numbers, which were bare in an earlier revision of this row: the command is uv run pytest tests/unit/test_ci_gate_contract.py, the module holds 32 test functions as of commit d9a6a93e, and the comparison is before-fix versus after-fix on that same module: 25 passed and 7 failed before, 32 passed after.     AL-133 2026-08-08 Final whole-branch review fix wave, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) tooling An assertion that reads ordering out of source text is fooled by comments, because a comment that explains an ordering constraint has to name the later step first. A new test asserted that the CI step resolving a git ref runs git rev-parse before git cat-file -e, by finding each command's first occurrence in the extracted step body. It failed against the correct script: the step's own #CRITICAL comment names git cat-file -e while explaining why rev-parse must come first, so the explanation of the rule appeared earlier in the text than the code obeying it. The failure is the dangerous direction only by luck. Had the comment been phrased the other way round, the same assertion would have passed on a script with the calls in the wrong order, and a test asserting an ordering it cannot actually read is worse than no test. The general shape: source text is not the program, and any assertion that treats position-in-file as position-in-execution must first remove everything that is not executed. Strip comment lines before reading ordering or presence out of any extracted script body, and prefer asserting on the parsed step rather than on raw text wherever the harness already parses it. Applied on this branch in tests/unit/test_ci_gate_contract.py, which now filters comment lines out of the step body before locating either command. Worth generalising: the same module makes several presence assertions against raw workflow text, and every one of them can be satisfied by a mention in a comment rather than by real configuration. open UW-C75
    AL-134 2026-08-08 Final whole-branch review fix wave, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) tooling A FastAPI route docstring is published API surface, so documenting behaviour in one breaks the contract gate while changing nothing on the wire. FastAPI copies a route handler's docstring into the OpenAPI operation's description, and @hey-api/openapi-ts copies that verbatim into frontend/src/client/sdk.gen.ts, which is committed and drift-checked by the contract CI job. A fix wave documented the new character cap in create_character's docstring as an ordinary code comment would be, which would have failed contract on a change with no behavioural content, and the failure would have surfaced in CI as generated-client drift rather than as anything resembling its cause. This is the same channel as the already-known Pydantic model docstring path into types.gen.ts, reached from the route side instead of the model side, which is why knowing the first case did not prevent the second. Treat a route docstring as a contract edit, not a comment: either leave it byte-identical and put implementation notes in a call-site comment or a private helper's docstring, which is what this branch did, or change it deliberately and regenerate the client in the same commit. The verification that settles it in either direction is cheap and worth writing down: dump app.openapi() in-process and diff every operation description against the committed sdk.gen.ts, which reports drift locally instead of waiting for the contract job. Worth promoting into the contract-gate documentation so both channels, model docstrings and route docstrings, are named in one place. open UW-C76
    AL-135 2026-08-08 PR #649 CI, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) tooling A schema invariant recorded only as a RAD prose comment is enforced by nothing, so the branch that falsifies it finds out from a downstream job rather than from a test. scripts/reset_e2e_real_state.py issued a bare TRUNCATE TABLE reading_state under an #ASSUME stating that nothing declares a foreign key onto that table. This branch added character_book_completion with exactly such a foreign key, and the only thing that noticed was the real-backend Playwright job, which failed in its setup fixture with FeatureNotSupportedError: cannot truncate a table referenced in a foreign key constraint. Two compounding causes: the invariant lived in prose, which cannot fail; and the #VERIFY it cited, test_reset_e2e_real_state_truncates_reading_state, did not exist and was grandfathered in rad-citation-baseline.toml, so the new RAD citation gate correctly stayed silent. Note also that ondelete="CASCADE" does not rescue a TRUNCATE the way it rescues a DELETE, so a correctly declared foreign key still breaks the statement. Convert the prose invariant into a schema-derived test: list the truncated tables in one constant and assert, from live SQLAlchemy metadata, that every table with a foreign key onto a member of that set is itself a member. Done here as test_truncated_tables_cover_every_dependent_foreign_key, break-tested against the pre-fix single-table set (fails naming character_book_completion) and the fixed set (passes). Prefer naming each table explicitly over TRUNCATE ... CASCADE, which converts this loud Postgres error into silent data loss for the next foreign key someone adds. Generalises past this one script: any RAD comment that asserts a whole-schema property is a candidate for a metadata-derived test, and any grandfathered baseline citation is a claim currently proved by nothing. open UW-C77
    AL-136 2026-08-08 PR #649 CI, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) process A gate placed where the data was convenient rather than where the need is silently becomes a product-wide behaviour change, and a green unit suite cannot see it. KidShell already fetched the active character for the kid library route, so the first-run character gate was written there: with status === 'none' it rendered CharacterCreator instead of the library Outlet. That inverted the gate's scope from per-book to per-profile. Every existing child was hard-gated into creating a character before reaching their library, with no skip affordance, for a feature no catalog book can use, which also contradicted the branch's own stated posture that the chain merges enforced and unreached. Six unit tests covered the gate and all six passed, because each asserted the gate did what it was built to do; none could ask whether the scope was right. The only thing that caught it was the real-backend Playwright smoke, and it surfaced as a 30s timeout on getByRole('link', {name: 'The Tide Pool Mystery'}), a locator that says nothing about characters. Two changes. First, when a plan says "show X when Y has none", make it state the SCOPE explicitly, per book, per profile, or per route, because the implementer will otherwise put the check wherever the data already is, and that location silently sets the scope. Second, treat "changes what every existing user sees on next visit" as a distinct review question the diff cannot answer: a per-task reviewer reading only the gate sees a correct gate. Resolved here by exposing accepts_character on LibraryItem and deciding at the book, at click time, failing open on every non-'none' status since the backend already treats an unseeded read as normal. open UW-C78
    AL-137 2026-08-08 PR #649 CI, persistent-characters runtime (branch feat/persistent-characters-runtime) tooling A pull request that conflicts with its base runs ZERO GitHub Actions workflows, and the third-party app checks that remain make it read as green. pull_request workflows are evaluated against refs/pull/N/merge, a ref GitHub cannot create while the branch conflicts, so after origin/main moved under this branch the second push produced no runs at all. What gh pr checks then showed was four checks, all passing: CodeRabbit, GitGuardian, Socket Security, and qlty. Those post against the head SHA through the Checks API and are unaffected by the merge ref, so they keep reporting on a branch whose real CI never started. Nothing in that output says "conflicted" or "no runs"; the only tells are the context COUNT collapsing from ~30 to 4, and gh run list --branch <b> showing its newest head SHA behind the PR's. This is the same family as the existing roll-up traps (a skipped job renders green, a job with no runner renders red with steps: []), but strictly worse, because here the roll-up check does not exist at all rather than reporting the wrong colour. Never read gh pr checks alone as evidence that CI ran. Check gh pr view <n> --json mergeable,mergeStateStatus in the same call and treat CONFLICTING/DIRTY as "CI is not running", not as "merge later"; and cross-check the newest head SHA in gh run list --branch <b> against the PR head SHA, since a matching SHA is the only positive evidence the push was picked up. Worth folding into whatever check-verification helper the PR workflow settles on, as a precondition asserted before any check state is interpreted. open UW-C79
    AL-138 2026-08-09 PR #661 review, story-diversity checkers (branch feat/story-diversity-checkers) validator PL-24's gamebook winnability floor was changed from an absolute 3 to max(3, ceil(0.05 * total)), justified in a comment committed to validator/policy.py saying the absolute floor "had been calibrated below the whole corpus and was exercised only by unit test". Measuring the committed catalog falsifies both halves: the absolute floor already fired on 7 of 14 gamebooks, and the share floor fires on all 14. The cause is that winnable endings in this corpus are roughly constant rather than proportional to book size. Every gamebook carries between 2 and 5 positive endings whether it holds 74 endings or 209, so a 5% share demands 11 positive endings from the-tenfold-siege where the author wrote 2, and the highest positive count anywhere in the catalog is 5. An advisory that fires on 100% of one narrative style carries no information, and the false calibration claim now sits in production source where the next reader will trust it. Require any scaled or share-based floor to arrive at review with a measured distribution attached rather than a prose claim about one. Add a catalog measurement mode that reports a proposed floor's fire rate per narrative style and age band, so the corpus impact of a threshold change is computed rather than asserted. Separately, rule on which way this specific case cuts: gamebooks averaging 3 winnable endings out of roughly 130 may be a genuine design defect for a kids' reading app, in which case the floor is right and the catalog is the work. open
    AL-139 2026-08-09 PR #661 review, story-diversity checkers (branch feat/story-diversity-checkers) process A #VERIFY marker naming tests that do not exist reads as backed at the call site, because the thing that permits it lives in a file the reader never opens. scripts/check_fill_integrity.py carries a #CRITICAL: data-integrity block whose #VERIFY names test_check_fill_integrity_rejects_same_file and test_check_fill_integrity_rejects_a_skeleton_with_no_markers; neither exists. It scans scripts/, it knows both names are unresolved, and rad-citation-baseline.toml grandfathers them explicitly while --assert-no-growth blocks new ones. So the gate works as designed and the marker is still a claim proved by nothing. Verifying it cost a full round trip precisely because the marker's own prose warns that "a checker that cannot fail manufactures confidence", which reads as evidence of rigour rather than as an unbacked assertion. Same class as AL-135, one release later, in a different file, and reached by a reviewer rather than by a gate. Make the grandfathering visible where the claim is made, not only in the baseline: have check_rad_citations.py require an inline annotation on any baselined citation (for example #VERIFY(unproved): ...) so a reader of the marker can see it is currently proved by nothing without opening rad-citation-baseline.toml.     AL-140 2026-08-09 PR #661 review, story-diversity checkers (branch feat/story-diversity-checkers) tooling codecov/patch reported green on a pull request adding roughly 5,000 lines, about 4,900 of them under scripts/, while qlty coverage diff on the same diff reported "no coverage data for the files in this diff".     AL-141 2026-08-09 PR #661 review, story-diversity checkers (branch feat/story-diversity-checkers) validator The narrative contract sidecar declares safety obligations its checker never reads. check_narrative_contract.py's NC-0 registration loop covered only entry_state and establishes, so facts named in a node's forbids were never validated against the declared facts registry, and safety_envelope.forbidden_device_kinds appeared nowhere in the 489-line checker at all.     AL-142 2026-08-09 Pre-rebuild review, strict-mode implementation (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) tooling load_skeleton ran the full gate and then threw the ValidationReport away unless it blocked, so check_skeleton.py, the tool every authoring wave gates shells with, printed a clean ok for skeletons the gate had warned about.
