    AL-143 2026-08-09 Pre-rebuild review, strict-mode implementation (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) validator Arming the CG choice-grammar family on a skeleton shell revealed that CG-4 can never pass one: it checks content-word overlap between a choice label and the opening sentence of the target node's body, and on a shell every body is a <<FILL ...>> directive, so the overlap is empty by construction and CG-4 fires on every choice of every shell. The family was designed against filled stories and nothing documented which CG rules are shell-safe, so the first strict run failed the demo fixture on ten findings of which six were structurally meaningless. CG-1 (run cap), CG-2 (option bounds) and CG-3 (words per stop, which reads declared FILL word targets) are all shell-meaningful; only CG-4 requires prose. This is the same shape RL-13 hit before AL-006 taught it to skip FILL bodies. Applied: check_skeleton.py --strict escalates CG-1..CG-3 and deliberately excludes CG-4 with an in-code rationale; CG-4 belongs to the fill gate. When the grammar is armed for filled stories (UW-C24 flip), consider teaching CG-4 to skip FILL bodies outright, the AL-006 precedent, so a partially filled draft cannot fire it spuriously either. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-144 2026-08-09 Reconvergence hard-gate ruling implementation (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) validator A reconvergence cap designed from the aggregate (corpus mean max in-degree 7.79 vs the research anchor 1.5) would have banned two whole topology families, because the aggregate mixes two opposite mechanisms. Measured per topology before implementing: open_map hubs sit at median max in-degree 9 with one legitimate hub at 126 (the-blackwood-sanatorium, every room re-enters the hub by design) and loop_and_grow at 5, while the pathological corridor-collapse funnels live in the tree-like topologies (branch_and_bottleneck clone pair at 31, the-cinder-bazaar at 21). A blanket per-band cap tight enough to catch the funnels excludes every open map; one loose enough to admit open maps catches nothing. The gate had to be topology-aware to mean anything: cap branch_and_bottleneck/gauntlet/sorting_hat/time_cave at 4/4/6/6/8/8 by band, exempt the hub topologies whose re-entry is the design, and leave those to the SQ-15 per-path metrics. The general shape: a structural quality gate calibrated on a corpus-wide distribution silently encodes the assumption that one mechanism produced the distribution. Applied: topology-aware max in-degree hard cap in check_skeleton.py --strict with the exemption rationale in-code; when the strict checks are promoted into validator/ after the grandfathered catalog is removed, carry the topology awareness into the catalogued rule rather than flattening it to one number. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-145 2026-08-09 Strict-bar conformance census after the 2026-08-09 rulings (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) process An advisory rule family left inert since landing accumulates near-universal non-conformance, and the flip cost grows monotonically while nobody watches. Arming CG-1..CG-3 inside the strict bar and censusing the catalog showed 57 of 61 skeletons breach CG-2 and 48 breach CG-3: the entire catalog predates the grammar's own bar because enforce_grammar defaulted False from the day the family landed (UW-C24) and no production caller ever opted in, so every authoring wave since added non-conforming trees at zero visible cost. The full strict census passes 2 of 61, meaning the ruled bar implies a near-total rebuild; that number was invisible until the rules were armed against the corpus even once. The general shape: an inert gate is not a deferred decision, it is a debt meter running with the display off, and the census that reads the meter costs one afternoon against a rebuild-sized principal. Applied for this flip: the census ran before any removal and its numbers plus a remove-on-replacement sequencing recommendation are recorded in the 2026-08-09 review (Part 4 census section), so the removal wave is sized by data. Standing practice: before arming any long-inert rule, census the live corpus with the rule in report mode and record the count, so the flip cost is a number in a doc rather than a surprise in CI. open the code half merged with PR #661 (4e1a08bc, 2026-08-10), but this lesson's evidence is the 2026-08-09 review write-up on PR #662, which has not merged; it flips to applied on that merge SHA
    AL-146 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) tooling PL-23 only reveals the derived reading clock inside a failure message, so a declared estimated_minutes that is wrong but within the 25% tolerance never surfaces the true number, and every out-of-tolerance miss costs a full draft-gate iteration. Both large-cell pilot drafters independently reimplemented the fewest-words Dijkstra inside their generators purely to see the number the checker already computes. A subtlety the 3-5 draft exposed: PL-23 silently no-ops below 200 fastest-path words, so two structurally similar small skeletons get different effective rule sets and the author is never told which regime they are in. Applied: check_skeleton.py --headroom/--strict now always prints declared vs derived estimated_minutes via the canonical recompute_estimated_minutes. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-147 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, three cells with independent adversarial review process Strict-clean does not mean approvable, and the gap is systematic rather than incidental: three drafts in three different cells each passed check_skeleton --strict with zero findings at any severity, and each was independently REJECTED on adversarial review, on defects no deterministic layer measures (label laundering, positional fate bias, consequence-free choices, merge contradictions, quota-shaped design). The gate verifies topology, budgets, and quota arithmetic; the rejections were all about outcomes, consequences, and continuity. Second half of the lesson: both large-cell drafters concluded a hand-author cannot hold the coupled global constraints at 180+ nodes, and each built an ad-hoc structural generator replicating the strict rule set; the only one-shot passes came from that method. Make adversarial critique a mandatory stage of the rebuild drafting workflow (draft, strict gate, in-cell audits, adversarial review, then promotion PR), and ship the structural generator harness as a first-class authoring aid instead of expecting every wave to rebuild it ad hoc. open UW-C84
    AL-148 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, adversarial critiques of all three drafts validator The outcome gates read kind/valence tags, not outcomes, so a draft can satisfy PL-24, the walk floor, and the outcome-spread audit purely by tag distribution over scenes the tags misdescribe. All three pilot drafts did it, two of them unconsciously: the 3-5 draft narrates one identical terminal scene under four kind/valence combinations, one tag contradicting its own beats; the 10-13 draft tags a full mission success neutral and ten failures as discovery; the 13-16 draft has sixteen everyone-survives rescues tagged negative setback and twelve off-page abandonments tagged neutral, plus role= derived mechanically from valence so twelve endings instruct the fill to write a discovery where nothing is discovered. Every headline economy number that passed the gates was a tag artifact. Build the tag-honesty audit: extend scripts/audit_ending_valence.py with an outcome-keyed rubric (goal delivered, goal lost, goal deferred) checked against ending beat text, flag valence/kind contradictions and same-terminal-event ending sets (high pairwise beat similarity across endings), decouple role= from valence, and wire the audit beside the outcome-spread check in the drafting loop. open UW-C85
    AL-149 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, adversarial critiques of the two large drafts validator Choice-level fairness and consequence are invisible to every current metric, and generated drafts fail both by construction. Position bias: in the 10-13 draft the third option leads to an ending 77% of the time and the first option never does; in the 13-16 draft always-pick-option-1 walks to the single best ending with zero risk, because the generator ordered options safe-first in every fan. Consequence: 25 decision nodes in the 10-13 draft have sibling choices with byte-identical reachable-ending sets, and staged merges collapse 98 ancestors into one node while never exceeding direct in-degree 5, laundering exactly the funnel the in-degree cap was ruled to stop. Add computable consequence checks to the strict bar: per-position ending-kind distribution with a skew ceiling plus an argmax-position walk that must not reach a positive ending unscathed; flag sibling choices with identical reachable-ending sets; extend the reconvergence gate with a k-hop ancestor-funnel metric. Generators must seeded-shuffle option order. open UW-C86
    AL-150 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, adversarial critiques of the two large drafts validator Merge-node beat contradictions, the known the-hollow-lighthouse defect class, are reproduced systematically by generation rather than occasionally by hand: eight hard upstream-vs-beat contradictions in each large draft, including endings narrating scenes from choices the reader explicitly declined, characters referenced at merges who are introduced only on other routes, gear appearing from nowhere, and one terminal beat hedging 'whichever stranger you trusted' because the generator knew its parents disagreed. Tier-1 has no state, so every fact a merge-node beat presupposes must hold on every inbound path, and nothing checks it. Give in-degree >= 2 nodes a machine-checkable contract: lint each merge node's presupposed facts (objects, characters, terrain, time of day) against the union of beats on every inbound simple path, flag hedging disjunctions in terminal beats, and until that exists require human beat-vs-parents review of every shared ending in the drafting workflow. open UW-C87
    AL-151 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, 3-5 adversarial critique tooling The drafting loop's gate and the catalog's admission audits are disjoint, so a strict-passing draft can be inadmissible three separate ways and nobody sees it until commit: the 3-5 pilot draft was structural distance 0.065 from puddle-jumping-day (second-closest pair in the whole catalog), its outcome economy survived the spread audit only by one dubious tag, and it was a slotless, contract-less shell with production_eligible: true, which exits the strict gate cleanly and would silently take the legacy free-text fill path in production matching (load_contract_for returns None). Wire check_incell_clones.py and check_outcome_spread.py into the drafting workflow with the candidate temporarily placed in its target cell, and make --strict fail a production_eligible shell that has no slot surfaces and contract sidecar. open UW-C88
    AL-152 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, both large-cell drafters' friction logs validator Several strict constraints are individually reasonable but couple destructively, and the couplings, not the values, dictated the drafts' shape: CG-3's stop ceiling equals roughly two to three nodes at the band words mean (a lone corridor node at the 10-13 mean is already illegal before a normal-weight successor; at 13-16 every checkpoint merge lives within ten words of the wall), so both drafts near-eliminated corridors and one emitted stops at 148-150 of the 150 cap, leaving zero fill headroom; CG-2's exact (3,3) at 8-13 bans the binary dilemma and forces a third strategy at every one of 100+ decisions, which is where template-sameness pressure originates; the 25% gamebook endings fraction makes terminal leaves the only legal padding, pushing toward the shallow-ending sprawl other rules exist to prevent; PL-26's gamebook ceiling of 4.0 is unmotivated by its own comment yet strict-blocking; PL-24's 60% kind ceiling quantizes harshly at four or fewer endings, silently raising the real endings floor for small kid books. Calibration review before rebuild wave 1, deciding each coupling explicitly: exempt the terminal node from CG-3 composition or raise the prose stop ceiling; widen CG-2 to (2,3) at 8-13; key the endings floor to distinct outcome identities or lower the gamebook fraction toward 0.20; anchor or drop PL-26's gamebook 4.0; make PL-24's ceiling count-aware below five endings. Also adopt the headroom discipline: generators target at most 90% of any hard cap, and strict warns at 98%. open UW-C89
    AL-153 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, all three drafters' friction logs docs The authoritative spec for newly drafted skeletons lives in a CLI script's docstring and constants, and the authoring-facing docs either omit or contradict it: skeleton-format.md never mentions CG-3 or its stop-composition rule (the single rule every grandfathered 10-13 medium skeleton fails), the strict topology constraints, or the FILL grammar's actual quoting behavior (apostrophes inside beats='...' are folklore learned from an exemplar); the word 'satisfying' names two different sets (success/completion kinds in PL-20, positive-or-neutral valence in the walk floor) with no doc distinguishing them; ending role= vocabulary is unvalidated folklore; and both pilot briefs drifted from the code because they were hand-copied (one mis-stated PL-26's gamebook ceiling as 6.0 against the code's 4.0). Write the strict-bar authoring reference: a new-skeleton section in the cyo-author skill generated from band_profile.py/choice_grammar.py values rather than hand-copied, covering the five strict policies, CG-3 composition, the two 'satisfying' senses, FILL quoting, and the role vocabulary decision; generate per-cell drafting briefs from code the same way. Applied in 177a4c6: scripts/generate_drafting_brief.py emits the per-cell constraint set from the enforced sources, and skeleton-format.md carries the corrected word table, the strict-bar section (incl. both 'satisfying' senses), the slot/contract grammar with the quoting note, and an honest role= description; the residual (wave-1 briefs actually produced by the generator) rides UW-C90. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-154 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, all three drafting subagents independently process The authoring-lessons mandate collides with subagent authoring runs: CLAUDE.md requires appending lessons at the end of any authoring run, but a scratchpad-scoped subagent cannot discharge it (repo-mutating MUST, feature-branch and signing rules, UW register cross-reference for open lessons), so all three pilot drafters and all three critics correctly declined to write the log and returned candidate lessons to the orchestrator instead. The mandate as written does not say who lands lessons from delegated runs, and six agents each spent tokens re-deriving the same conclusion. Amend the authoring-lessons section of CLAUDE.md: a delegated authoring run returns candidate lessons to its orchestrator, and the orchestrator (the session that can branch, sign, and validate) is responsible for landing them; a subagent must not edit the log. open UW-C91
    AL-155 2026-08-09 Same-skeleton diversity experiment: three isolated fills of the-lost-mitten under maximally different theme bindings (review Part 6) validator A same-skeleton story pair has a perceived-similarity floor of 0.50 before any prose exists (PS weights 0.5 leaf + 0.3 structural + 0.2 theme; structural is 1.0 for a same-tree pair by construction and theme was 1.0 because binding never re-themes metadata.themes), and the empirical best case, three independent authors filling three maximally different bindings with near-minimal leaf similarity (0.18-0.20, body trigram Jaccard 0.026-0.029), landed at PS 0.59-0.60 against the 0.70 repeat threshold. Meanwhile the qualitative verdict on the same triple was 'one story, three costumes': identical search-strategy menus, clue mechanics, gag, and punchline, with two of three ending titles string-identical. So a beat-identical triple sails under every lexical gate while fill quality has almost no room to move the metric: slot granularity, not prose, is the diversity bottleneck, which is direct experimental evidence for the SQ-11 beat-variant ADR (gate OG3). Add a structural signal to the family-scoped anti-repeat guard: skeleton id plus beat-variant fingerprint, never serving the same combination twice to one family (cheapest intervention, pure policy); adopt variant beat pools on high-salience nodes (the clue mechanics, the twist ending, the set-piece gag) per SQ-11, which this experiment sizes at roughly 2-3x beat authoring on 4 of 11 nodes with zero topology or validator changes; frame same-skeleton siblings honestly as a series in the product. open UW-C92
    AL-156 2026-08-09 Same-skeleton diversity experiment (review Part 6) tooling Theme binding rewrites the three slotted surfaces but leaves metadata.themes untouched, so a beach book and a meadow book both shipped tagged 'winter'. The stale tags are kid- and guardian-facing library metadata, they feed skeleton matching, and they feed the perceived-similarity theme axis, where they pin 0.20 of PS at maximum for every same-skeleton pair regardless of how different the bound themes actually are. render_bound_skeleton (or the binding pipeline around it) must re-derive or strip metadata.themes at binding time, with the contract carrying per-binding theme tags; add a binding acceptance check that no legacy-theme tag survives into a bound skeleton's metadata. open UW-C93
    AL-157 2026-08-09 Same-skeleton diversity experiment (review Part 6) process Beats encode world facts the slot system does not govern, and the fill contract's reskin rule is ambiguous enough that three independent authors resolved the same conflicts three different ways: the skeleton's un-slotted snow was imported into an autumn park by one author and reskinned to dew by another; 'one bare hand is cold' was inverted to a hot bare head because the bound item was a sunhat; and one binding produced 'fireflies chirped' because the beat verb belonged to the legacy birds, a world-consistency defect no gate catches. Divergent resolutions mean fidelity review cannot tell a faithful fill from a drifted one on exactly these beats. Slot or neutralize world-fact surfaces in beats during parameterization (weather, anatomy tied to the item, helper-species verbs and time of day), add a binding-consistency lint that checks bound helper species and setting against beat verbs, and sharpen the fill contract's reskin-versus-uphold rule with the three observed cases as worked examples. open UW-C94
    AL-158 2026-08-09 Opus pipeline analysis for the narrative redesign (review of every FILL-directive consumer) tooling Every consumer of the FILL directive fails open on a parse miss: binding.py, fidelity.py, fidelity_review.py, and slotted_surfaces.py all skip the node when the anchored regex does not match, and three more private regex copies live in mutation/bundle.py, mutation/operators.py, and parameterize_skeleton.py. A future format change the regex does not match would therefore silently disable slot substitution, word-count fidelity, semantic fidelity, theme-leak scanning, and slot-set equality simultaneously, with zero findings anywhere. The consumers were each individually reasonable; the cascade is the defect, and it is invisible until the first format evolution, which the narrative redesign now schedules. Make the parse total before any format work: a body starting with the FILL marker that does not parse becomes a blocking L1 finding; add a lockstep test enumerating every directive consumer and asserting each reports rather than skips on an unparseable directive; collapse the three private regex copies onto storybook/slotted_surfaces.py. Prerequisite 1 of the narrative redesign proposal. open UW-C95
    AL-159 2026-08-09 Opus format-design analysis, re-expressing the-lost-mitten node by node validator A node with an in-edge from its own descendant is re-rendered verbatim on every loop, and nothing tells the prose author: the-lost-mitten's three abandon-the-lead choices all target n_start, whose beat stages the loss as fresh news, so all three experiment fills wrote a discovery beat and a child who loops back reads the oh-no moment again on every return. The defect is prose tense inside a beat, so no graph, budget, or fidelity check can see it, and it generalizes to every skeleton with hub re-entry (loop_and_grow and open_map are built on it). Derive a reentrant flag from the graph (any node reachable from its own successors), have the validator REQUIRE the flag rather than trust the author, and carry a reentry contract into the fill prompt (write established fact, not fresh news). Cheap, graph-derived, and worth shipping ahead of the wider redesign; folded into the proposal's ship-regardless stage. open UW-C96
    AL-160 2026-08-09 Narrative-redesign pilot, scene-inventory and recognition ratings over nine fills of one skeleton (proposal section 10) validator Pairwise distinctness margins can be passed while every story shares an attractor vocabulary, because free LLM invention diversifies pairwise and converges collectively: the three fully-free arm C authors, working in isolation, independently produced the same false-clue retcon in 3 of 3 fills, the same nudge-and-catch retrieval in 3 of 3, the same cozy-container napping reveal in 3 of 3, a near-verbatim 'boing boing' eyewitness in 2 of 3, and regressed the choice-label surface to the control template including three verbatim label collisions with a different arm. The dominant residual recognition leaks after devices vary are ritual phrases in labels and dialogue ('Team time', 'One, two, three, reach it together'). Neither class is visible to pairwise device margins, lexical similarity gates, or the perceived-similarity metric. Add two sibling-scoped checks to the drafting loop: a convergence check flagging any device that appears in 2 or more sibling fills of one skeleton, and an n-gram overlap check over choice labels and quoted dialogue against sibling fills; both complement rather than replace the pairwise margins. open UW-C97
    AL-161 2026-08-09 Narrative-redesign pilot, arm B twist-margin failure (proposal section 10) validator Locking an ending's outcome propositions locked its MECHANISM too, and mechanism-sameness is what a reader recognizes: all three arm B twists shared the carried-all-along reveal because locked_outcome pinned it, differing only by concealment prop, and the rater scored the twist margin 0 of 3 under the noun-swap rule while the one mechanism-changed twist in the pilot (arm C's third-party recovery) was the only twist no reader predicted. The contract's own premise.resolution_space already enumerated three mechanisms; nothing selected among them. Make the ending mechanism a per-request selection drawn from the contract's resolution_space (a selection-vector entry with the same seeded, family-steered discipline as device selection), with locked_outcome locking kind, valence, and affect envelope only. open UW-C98
    AL-162 2026-08-09 Narrative-redesign pilot, arm B clue-margin failure (proposal section 10) tooling Bible authoring converges exactly the way fill authoring does, and a converged bible caps the format's diversity from upstream: bibles a and c were written with near-identical device kinds (flattened grass vs parted clover; yarn strand vs wool wisp), so the a-c pair collapsed to noun-swap on 2 of 3 clue nodes and failed the pre-registered margin even though the obligation format delivered everything else. Device distinctness must be enforced where devices are chosen, not hoped for at fill time. Bible generation enforces cross-binding device-kind diversity: compute Mechanic Divergence against the family's (and the cell's recent) prior bibles at bind time and re-draw below threshold, backed by a wider per-category device-kind taxonomy so re-draws have somewhere to go. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-163 2026-08-09 Higher-difficulty B-plus pilot on the-clocktower-cipher (proposal section 11) validator The obligation contract is itself a shared prompt across every fill of its skeleton, and anything concrete in it becomes the new frozen armature: scene devices written into constraints (the seize-then-lubricate remedy, the noise-trap safeguard, the preserved-loft adoption) produced a single scene-device inventory under rotated props in all three isolated fills (clue-analog margin 1 of 3 for every pair), and contract vocabulary seeded convergent prose ('stepped out for tea thirty years ago' verbatim in two books, 'Knowing when not to is a skill' in all three, ten-plus cross-book phrase templates). The sibling-gram check surfaced the leaks but its budget of 8 was calibrated on 500-word fills and reads 95 at 3.1k words, so it cannot yet gate. Contract hygiene: obligation strings must be device-abstract, every recurring set-piece becomes an invention slot over a bible category with real kind freedom, and the sibling-gram check gains a length-normalized budget (per thousand leaf words) and joins the fill loop as a gate. open UW-C100
    AL-164 2026-08-09 Higher-difficulty B-plus pilot, theme-authoring agent measurement (proposal section 11) tooling Contract-forced device kinds consume the Mechanic Divergence budget invisibly: kind_must_be specs froze most category multisets at pairwise Jaccard 1.0, leaving roughly 0.07 of headroom over the tau, so the MD gate passed while the frozen-kind categories stayed frozen and the room hint-carriers scored 0-2 of 4 distinct per pair downstream. The theme agent could only discover this by reading the checker's source and doing the arithmetic by hand. check_bible_diversity reports per-category Jaccard with forced-by-contract categories marked, so authors and generators see real headroom; world recipes minimize kind_must_be to what safety genuinely requires, and a contract whose forced kinds leave less than a floor of free MD headroom fails NC review. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-165 2026-08-09 Higher-difficulty B-plus pilot, recognition rating at 10-13 (proposal section 11) validator The reader surfaces the contract cannot vary are the strongest recognition channels, and their strength grows with band: same-order same-function choice menus landed the same-book verdict at node 2 of 26 for a pattern-sharp 10-13 reader, five of eight ending titles were unslotted and therefore byte-identical across books, and one slotted title named a prop the selection had assigned to a room off that title's reaching path. The overall score fell to 2.0 against the 3-5 pilot's 2.5 despite better device work, because recognition capability rises with age while the diversity margins stayed constant. Generate all ending titles under the title contract with none unslotted, add a selection-time check that a title's named props lie on the reaching path, add a label-surface diversity directive with a menu-surface margin to the pilot protocol, and scale distinctness margins and gram budgets with band. open UW-C102
    AL-166 2026-08-09 Third pilot, sibling-gram trace and scene-rater convergence list (proposal section 12) authoring-craft Same-model idiom convergence is a distinct channel from spec leakage: three isolated authors with device-abstract inputs produced identical staging idioms at the same beats ("a door stood ajar on a room that smelled of", "stepped out for tea", "the climb was shorter than it looked") that appear in no input file, and after a token-level revision round all five watched idiom families reappeared in paraphrases below the 4-gram floor ("corkscrewed" stairs, the "come back by daylight, and knock" closing beat in all three books). The n-gram check catches token identity, not idiom identity, so a revision pass defeats the metric more thoroughly than the phenomenon. Add an idiom-family layer to the sibling check: a curated watch list of staging tropes matched by stem or embedding rather than exact tokens, or a rater-in-the-loop sample on the convergence list; budget it per band. open UW-C103
    AL-167 2026-08-09 Third pilot, first-pass gram failure root cause (proposal section 12) authoring-craft Fact description strings are shared prompt surface exactly like constraints and hints: the hygiene pass abstracted constraints and beat hints but left rooms_mapped naming the spiral stair and pendulum ledge, cipher_decoded saying "substitution cipher" against a freed cipher-form slot, and vault_contents_known enumerating slot-supplied contents, and all three seeded cross-book prose or contradicted selections. Extend the contract-hygiene rule to every prose-bearing string in the contract (facts, merge notes, reentry contracts), and have NC review scan fact strings for device-category kind tokens and slot-supplied nouns. open UW-C104
    AL-168 2026-08-09 Third pilot, menu-frame check and both raters (proposal section 12) validator Per-binding label styles close the menu-surface channel cheaply: with a label_style drawn per selection and validated by NC-7, shared menu frames went from the pilot-2 recognition driver to 0 deterministic overlaps, and the scene rater scored the label voices 3.0 ("non-interchangeable, not template rewording"). Styling does not vary meaning, so the semantic fingerprint remains (AL-170), but the surface channel is closed. None further; adopt label_style as a standard selection field for every contract. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-169 2026-08-09 Third pilot, revision round (proposal section 12) tooling The gate-revise-regate fill loop works agentically in one round: feeding the deterministic shared-gram list back to each isolated author (revise only your own colliding sentences, in your binding's voice) moved 20.4 shared grams per 1000 to 1.2 against a 4.0 budget with integrity and the full gate still green, no human repair. This is the production shape for every deterministic diversity check. Wire check_sibling_fills (and the title and menu checks) into the generation fill loop as a blocking gate with an automated revision pass, capped at N rounds before flagging for review. open UW-C105
    AL-170 2026-08-09 Third pilot, recognition rating (proposal section 12) authoring-craft With devices, prose, menus, and titles all varied, recognition still lands at node 4 (2.5 against a 2.0 baseline, margin failed) and the residual channels are the skeleton's identity itself: choice-menu SEMANTICS (same options, same meanings, same order at every fork, visible through any label styling) and scene-function order, plus beat-identical emotional payoffs at same-mechanism-family endings. Sibling fills of one skeleton are structurally a "same adventure, new world" series, and downstream hygiene cannot change that. Owner decision: frame same-skeleton bindings as an explicit series (assignment policy: at most one binding of a skeleton per reader, or market the format honestly), and/or fund per-fork semantics pools rotated at selection time as the mechanism treatment applied to decisions; catalog-level diversity comes from more skeletons, not more hygiene. open UW-C106
    AL-171 2026-08-09 Model-tier study, Haiku fill of the clocktower contract (proposal section 13) validator Declared node obligations are proved coherent but never verified against the prose that fills them: a Haiku fill decoded the cipher at n_open, whose contract declares forbids: [inside_access, cipher_decoded, keeper_met], voiding the entire "solve the cipher" branch because n_note then re-presented the same decode as a discovery. It passed fill integrity, the full Layer 1 and Layer 2 gate, and every NC check, because the NC checks run BEFORE prose exists and no later check reads a node's body against its establishes and forbids sets. A stronger author was papering over the hole, so it becomes load-bearing exactly when a cheaper model is introduced. Add a fill-vs-contract fact audit as a review-panel stage (per node: does the prose establish anything in forbids, and does it establish everything in establishes), since it needs a semantic judgment rather than a token metric; wire it into the automated adversarial panel of proposal section 9 rather than the deterministic gate. open UW-C107
    AL-172 2026-08-09 Model-tier study, blind three-tier prose comparison (proposal section 13) product Model tier moves prose quality but not sameness: across nine books from one skeleton, blind craft scores ran 4.9 (frontier), 4.0 (Sonnet), 2.2 (Haiku) with ship verdicts of as-is, light-edit, and do-not-publish, while the recognition score was 2.5 for BOTH the frontier and Haiku tiers with the same drivers named independently (keeper-plus-maker pair, four-exit hub menu). Diversity is a property of the skeleton and contract; prose is a property of the author; they are close to orthogonal. Separately, convergence was not monotonic in capability, with Sonnet the most convergent tier (29.7 shared grams per 1000) and Haiku the least (8.5), each converging its own way: Haiku near-quotes contract strings, Sonnet reaches for stock genre idioms. Treat the catalog-diversity work and the fill-model cost decision as independent choices; set the fill model on prose grounds (Sonnet floor, with a reading-level directive for its systematic upward drift at mean FK 9.17) and use Haiku for mechanical roles it passed cleanly: selection derivation, deterministic-finding revision rounds, first-pass triage. open UW-C108
    AL-173 2026-08-09 Model-tier study, comparative vs isolated rating of the same books (proposal section 13) process Absolute quality judgments are systematically more forgiving than comparative ones: the same three Haiku books scored 2.2 with a rewrite verdict from a rater holding all nine books side by side, and 3.0 with a one-editing-pass verdict from a rater holding only those three. This is the project's single-reviewer problem measured directly, and it means a reviewer approving one story in isolation will pass work that a side-by-side comparison rejects. Show a sibling fill alongside the story under review in the approval surface, and give the automated review panel a comparative rather than absolute rubric; treat isolated-rating scores as an upper bound. open UW-C109
    AL-174 2026-08-09 Model-tier study, deterministic battery across three tiers (proposal section 13) validator Gate-clean does not mean publishable: all nine books across three model tiers cleared fill integrity, the full validator gate, safety, topology, word bands, and title contracts on the first pass, and three of them were judged unpublishable by a blind rater for tense instability including breaks inside a single paragraph, a central puzzle that is asserted rather than performed ("the digits spell out language"), and narrator moral tags closing nearly every ending. None of those three defect classes is visible to any existing check. Add deterministic prose-craft detectors for tense stability, narrator moral tags, and told-emotion density, calibrated so they separate the observed tiers; and state plainly in the authoring docs that the gate certifies validity, not quality. applied PR #661 squash-merged to main 2026-08-10 as 4e1a08bc; the earlier branch SHAs lived only on a scratch branch that never merged
    AL-175 2026-08-09 Prose-craft detector calibration (proposal section 13, commit 4b93b97) validator The prose-craft detectors separate publishable from unpublishable books perfectly, but the separation is IN-SAMPLE by construction: every threshold (--max-unstable-nodes 0, --min-tense-cues 6, --max-node-mix 0.34, --max-moral-tags 0, --max-told-per-1000 0.5) was tuned against the same nine books it is reported to separate, so the result measures fit rather than predictive power. Two thresholds are already known to be fragile: the told-emotion rate ranks one unpublishable book (0.31 per 1000) BELOW one shippable book (0.35), so that detector cannot rank those two and the book is caught only by the other two detectors; and the moral-tag budget of zero is unfalsifiable on a corpus where every shippable book scored zero. Validate out of sample before wiring the detectors into any blocking gate: score a held-out set of books that had no part in calibration, ideally from a different skeleton and band, and re-tune on the union; until then run the detectors as advisory-only and report their findings to the author rather than blocking on them. open UW-C111
    AL-176 2026-08-09 Per-child sibling-exposure analysis (scripts/analyze_sibling_exposure.py, skeleton-free alternatives proposal section 2b) product The unit of story-sameness exposure is the CHILD, not the family, and the system has no per-child skeleton history at all: Storybook carries only family_id and personalization_subject_profile_id, and both reads of prior skeleton_slug (skeleton_match.py:587, diversity/history.py) filter on family with a 20-row window. Family scoping alone triples the second-request repeat rate (0.09 to 0.29 from one child to three) while a child-scoped counterfactual reproduces the single-reader curve, and the shared window hides 81% of a child's own band reading in a three-child household. StoryRequest.profile_id and StorybookAssignment.child_profile_id already carry the needed evidence. Scope the anti-repeat history and weighting to the requesting child rather than the family, widen or drop the 20-row window, and close the visibility='catalog' leak where a cross-family read is invisible to recency. Recovers 25 to 30% of the required catalog for no new content. open UW-C112
    AL-177 2026-08-09 Per-child sibling-exposure analysis (proposal section 2b) product A skeleton is consumable within a child but reusable across children, and nothing in the code contradicts that (no global or cross-family anti-repeat exists; visibility='catalog' actively amortizes one fill across families). Required catalog therefore scales with per-child lifetime consumption inside a band, roughly tenure x rate spread over that band's cells, and is INDEPENDENT of user count, which makes catalog growth a bounded one-time capital cost rather than a cost that grows with the business. Measured need is about 130 skeletons at 0.5 stories per child per month, 408 at 1, and 816 at 2, against 57 production-eligible today. Treat catalog build as bounded capital and size it against measured demand; instrument per-child stories per month per band, which is the single number that sets the target and is not measured in this deployment. open UW-C113
    AL-178 2026-08-09 Per-child sibling-exposure analysis (proposal section 2b) scale Every populated production cell holds 3 or 4 skeletons across all six bands, so a child exhausts a cell by their 4th request in it and every later story in that cell is with certainty a tree they have already read; a repeat is more likely than not by request 3 or 4, and rotating across a band's length cells buys about two extra requests rather than an order of magnitude. This, not the skeleton format, is the measured driver of the sameness the three diversity pilots characterized, and it retires the case for replacing the skeleton architecture. Fund catalog depth and per-child scoping ahead of any pipeline replacement; keep the skeleton-free alternatives as a designed option set to revisit only if those two fixes fail to clear the problem. open UW-C114
    AL-179 2026-08-09 Adversarial review of the skeleton-free alternatives proposal validator SAFE-14 (validator/safety.py:41) is a Phase-2 stub returning an empty report unconditionally, so safety_flagged cannot take a non-false value, yet "zero safety flags" was reported as evidence of safety seven times across pilots 1 to 3 and the model-tier study. The real deterministic pre-LLM denylist floor on untrusted brief material is validator/slots.py, whose only caller is the theme-binding path, so it runs for skeleton fills only and a skeleton-free story has no pre-LLM denylist gate. Separately, the gate is provenance-agnostic but not format-agnostic: PL-19, PL-23, CG-3, and RL-13 each parse the <<FILL words=N>> grammar, and enforce_grammar defaults off so generated stories never run CG-1 through CG-4 at all. Stop reporting safety_flagged as a measured outcome until SAFE-14 is implemented, and mark it explicitly as a stub in any results table; document that the gate's strictness is caller-parameterized so cross-path comparisons state their scale and enforce_grammar settings. open UW-C115
    AL-180 2026-08-09 Adversarial review, strict-bar measurement across the catalog validator The --strict authoring bar passes 2 of 61 catalog skeletons (0 of 11 at 10-13), because it gates newly drafted skeletons while the shipped catalog is grandfathered. Two consequences were being missed: a proposal pre-registered "strict bar: pass by construction" for the baseline, which is false 97% of the time, and the pilots' own control skeleton the-clocktower-cipher is the catalog's single non-production-eligible (10-13, None, None) row, so it is never served to a child and, declaring no length or style, is held to band budgets rather than the ADR-011 cell budgets every production 10-13 skeleton faces. Every pilot baseline number was measured on it. Decide explicitly whether the strict bar is the intended production bar (promoting it as a blocking rule would retire 97% of the catalog, a product decision); and re-baseline future diversity work on a production-eligible skeleton in a real cell. open UW-C116
    AL-181 2026-08-09 Length-demand catalog sizing (scripts/analyze_sibling_exposure.py, proposal section 2b.3a) scale Story-length demand is not flat within a band and the catalog is: every populated cell holds 3 to 4 skeletons while demand concentrates on medium. Because skeleton_matches_cell treats only a NULL length as a wildcard and 0 of 58 production-eligible skeletons declare one, cells are hard partitions, so surplus in the short and long cells is stranded capital that can never serve a medium request. Peaking demand leaves the band TOTAL essentially unchanged (one child's band-lifetime consumption however it splits) but raises the SHORTFALL by 23 to 32% and moves the binding constraint to the medium cell in every band, pulling the first likely repeat forward about one request (P(repeat by request 4) at 8-11 rises from 0.386 flat to 0.647 strongly-medium-weighted). Author against the demand curve rather than filling cells evenly: put the first 6 to 12 skeletons of each band's budget entirely into that band's medium cell, which buys 0.8 to 2.2 more requests before a repeat than an even split; short and long earn marginal skeletons only past roughly request 17 to 20. Measure the real length distribution to replace the assumed regimes. open UW-C117
    AL-182 2026-08-09 Length-demand analysis, intake trace (proposal section 2b.3a) product Kid auto-approve hardcodes length=Length.SHORT band-agnostically (api/story_requests.py:508), which steers exactly the requests where nobody is choosing into the thinnest-demand tier, and for the teen bands it is an outright production bug: 13-16 and 16+ have no short cell by ADR-011 design and hold no short skeletons, so candidates_for_cell returns empty and the authoring plan 422s every time for a teen-band child with auto-approve enabled. Separately, ADR-011's band-by-length rule is enforced nowhere in the request path (the approve body validates band against style only, and both length selectors render all three lengths for every band), so a guardian can approve a long 3-5 book or a short 13-16 book and hit the same empty-cell failure later. Make the auto-approve length band-aware (reuse the _length_of teen fallback rather than a constant) and default it to the demand-weighted tier rather than short; add band-by-length validation to the approve and authored-create bodies and gate the frontend length options by band, so an unservable cell is rejected at intake rather than 422ing at planning time. open UW-C118
    AL-183 2026-08-09 Per-request mutation pilot on the-midnight-museum (alternatives proposal section 11.5.1) scale Bounded mutation of a single parent is not a catalog multiplier, and the reason generalizes: every accepted mutant preserved 100% of the parent's <<FILL>> beat directives (95 of 95 nodes and beats across all three mutants), so mutation moves the graph while recognition is driven by the scene content and decision semantics that live in the beats. Shape-preserving operators scored structural distance exactly 0.0000 (M1 on all five swap pairs tried, including cross-act), the shape-changing M4 reconvergence variant reached 0.0038, and a maximum-length chain using only the parent's own material reached 0.0064, all below the committed TAU_CELL of 0.05, while hand-authored same-cell siblings sit at a median of 0.390. A rater landed the same-book verdict at reading position 3 (score 2.0) with the structural difference invisible until position 8. Applicability was not the constraint: M4 had 2,201 eligible sites. Withdraw per-request mutation as a diversity lever and fund catalog depth instead; if a structural multiplier is still wanted, test cross-skeleton recombination (M3 graft) separately, since the only mutant to clear the floor did so by importing 32 nodes from a different skeleton, which scales with pairs of existing skeletons rather than replacing the need for them. open UW-C119
    AL-184 2026-08-09 Per-request mutation pilot, deterministic bench (alternatives proposal section 11.5.1) validator structural_distance and the committed TAU_CELL floor were vindicated on this evidence rather than refuted: the floor rejected exactly the mutants the reader rejected, and the metric's ordering matched the reader's ordering. The metric's known order-blindness and self-declared topology weighting did not bite because no bounded mutant came within an order of magnitude of the threshold. This is not a general exoneration, since the failure mode it cannot see (identical scene function at identical position) is precisely what a mutant preserves. Keep TAU_CELL as the anti-clone gate for catalog-time work, and continue to treat structural_distance as unsuitable for judging perceived diversity between artifacts that already share authored content; revisit only if a candidate approaches the threshold. open the code half merged with PR #661 (4e1a08bc, 2026-08-10), but this lesson's evidence is the 2026-08-09 review write-up on PR #662, which has not merged; it flips to applied on that merge SHA
    AL-185 2026-08-09 Per-request mutation pilot, sibling-fill measurement (alternatives proposal section 11.5.1) process A sibling-convergence measurement is invalid when one author writes both arms: the second book's first draft was a sentence-level world swap of the first at 302 shared grams per 1000, and two deliberate de-convergence passes only brought it to 70.4, still an order of magnitude above the 4.0 budget and roughly three times the worst previously measured arm. The number therefore measures the author's de-convergence effort rather than the condition under test. Separately, the recognition rating could not be run in an isolated agent in this environment, so it is author-scored rather than blind. Require an independence protocol for any sibling-fill arm: one isolated author per arm with no sight of the other arms, and a rater that has not seen the generation plan. Where isolation is impossible, report the measurement as author-scored and treat it as an upper bound on distinctness. open UW-C120
    AL-186 2026-08-10 PR #662 review fix, band-median re-measurement process Three of the six uniform-random-walk band medians reported in the 2026-08-09 review (5-8, 13-16, 16+) did not reproduce on re-measurement, and the review recorded the gap as unexplained. The cause was not a measurement error: the band work was done in a local working directory and never committed, so only the resulting numbers reached the document while the script, its inputs and its metric choice were left behind. A figure whose producer is uncommitted cannot be re-derived, cannot be re-checked when a rule changes underneath it, and forces a later reader to treat honest drift as an unexplained contradiction. Any quantitative figure quoted in a review or proposal cites a committed producer: a script under scripts/ plus the exact invocation, or a committed output artifact. Where the measurement is one-off, commit the script that produced it in the same PR as the document that quotes it, even if it is never run again. open UW-C124
    AL-187 2026-08-10 PR #662 review fix, strict-census re-measurement in a fresh worktree tooling A git worktree does not share the primary tree's virtualenv, and uv run creates a bare one rather than failing, so the strict census re-run reported 0 of 61 skeletons passing. That reads as a dramatic regression against the recorded 2 of 61, but every one of the 61 runs had died at import on ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'sqlalchemy' before the checker executed a single rule. The tell is that every input failed identically: a catalog-wide measurement that returns the same verdict for every member is an environment fault, not a finding, and a census loop that only records pass/fail cannot tell the two apart. Have the census path distinguish 'the checker did not start' from 'the skeleton failed the bar': catch the non-rule exit separately and abort the whole run rather than scoring it as a failure. Add to the worktree instructions that uv sync --all-extras is required before any measurement run, not only before tests. open UW-C125
    AL-188 2026-08-09 Pre-rebuild review, strict-mode implementation (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) tooling load_skeleton ran the full gate and then threw the ValidationReport away unless it blocked, so check_skeleton.py, the tool every authoring wave gates shells with, printed a clean ok for skeletons the gate had warned about. A warning-visible sweep found 40 of 61 catalog skeletons carrying hidden advisories: 37 PL-23 clock drifts up to 125%, 25 PL-24 ending-mix breaches including 7 below the winnability floor, 4 L2-13 and 2 PL-26. None of these was visible in any authoring log because the loader dropped the report on the floor; the script even re-implemented one warning (below-cell-min) by hand, which made the omission of the other nine look deliberate. The general shape: a loader that validates and returns only the payload converts every advisory the validator produces into silence, and the tooling downstream inherits that silence as a clean bill of health. Applied: load_skeleton takes an optional report_sink callback receiving the full GateResult before the block decision, plus an enforce_grammar passthrough; check_skeleton.py prints every finding at every severity and gains --strict, the newly-drafted-skeleton bar that escalates the PL-19/23/24/25/26 and L1-7 advisories, enforces CG-1..CG-3, and requires a band-scaled random-walk satisfying-outcome floor. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-189 2026-08-09 Pre-rebuild review, strict-mode implementation (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) validator Arming the CG choice-grammar family on a skeleton shell revealed that CG-4 can never pass one: it checks content-word overlap between a choice label and the opening sentence of the target node's body, and on a shell every body is a <<FILL ...>> directive, so the overlap is empty by construction and CG-4 fires on every choice of every shell. The family was designed against filled stories and nothing documented which CG rules are shell-safe, so the first strict run failed the demo fixture on ten findings of which six were structurally meaningless. CG-1 (run cap), CG-2 (option bounds) and CG-3 (words per stop, which reads declared FILL word targets) are all shell-meaningful; only CG-4 requires prose. This is the same shape RL-13 hit before AL-006 taught it to skip FILL bodies. Applied: check_skeleton.py --strict escalates CG-1..CG-3 and deliberately excludes CG-4 with an in-code rationale; CG-4 belongs to the fill gate. When the grammar is armed for filled stories (UW-C24 flip), consider teaching CG-4 to skip FILL bodies outright, the AL-006 precedent, so a partially filled draft cannot fire it spuriously either. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-190 2026-08-09 Reconvergence hard-gate ruling implementation (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) validator A reconvergence cap designed from the aggregate (corpus mean max in-degree 7.79 vs the research anchor 1.5) would have banned two whole topology families, because the aggregate mixes two opposite mechanisms. Measured per topology before implementing: open_map hubs sit at median max in-degree 9 with one legitimate hub at 126 (the-blackwood-sanatorium, every room re-enters the hub by design) and loop_and_grow at 5, while the pathological corridor-collapse funnels live in the tree-like topologies (branch_and_bottleneck clone pair at 31, the-cinder-bazaar at 21). A blanket per-band cap tight enough to catch the funnels excludes every open map; one loose enough to admit open maps catches nothing. The gate had to be topology-aware to mean anything: cap branch_and_bottleneck/gauntlet/sorting_hat/time_cave at 4/4/6/6/8/8 by band, exempt the hub topologies whose re-entry is the design, and leave those to the SQ-15 per-path metrics. The general shape: a structural quality gate calibrated on a corpus-wide distribution silently encodes the assumption that one mechanism produced the distribution. Applied: topology-aware max in-degree hard cap in check_skeleton.py --strict with the exemption rationale in-code; when the strict checks are promoted into validator/ after the grandfathered catalog is removed, carry the topology awareness into the catalogued rule rather than flattening it to one number. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-191 2026-08-09 Strict-bar conformance census after the 2026-08-09 rulings (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) process An advisory rule family left inert since landing accumulates near-universal non-conformance, and the flip cost grows monotonically while nobody watches. Arming CG-1..CG-3 inside the strict bar and censusing the catalog showed 57 of 61 skeletons breach CG-2 and 48 breach CG-3: the entire catalog predates the grammar's own bar because enforce_grammar defaulted False from the day the family landed (UW-C24) and no production caller ever opted in, so every authoring wave since added non-conforming trees at zero visible cost. The full strict census passes 2 of 61, meaning the ruled bar implies a near-total rebuild; that number was invisible until the rules were armed against the corpus even once. The general shape: an inert gate is not a deferred decision, it is a debt meter running with the display off, and the census that reads the meter costs one afternoon against a rebuild-sized principal. Applied for this flip: the census ran before any removal and its numbers plus a remove-on-replacement sequencing recommendation are recorded in the 2026-08-09 review (Part 4 census section), so the removal wave is sized by data. Standing practice: before arming any long-inert rule, census the live corpus with the rule in report mode and record the count, so the flip cost is a number in a doc rather than a surprise in CI. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-192 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot (branch claude/skeleton-story-review-3zy6tq) tooling PL-23 only reveals the derived reading clock inside a failure message, so a declared estimated_minutes that is wrong but within the 25% tolerance never surfaces the true number, and every out-of-tolerance miss costs a full draft-gate iteration. Both large-cell pilot drafters independently reimplemented the fewest-words Dijkstra inside their generators purely to see the number the checker already computes. A subtlety the 3-5 draft exposed: PL-23 silently no-ops below 200 fastest-path words, so two structurally similar small skeletons get different effective rule sets and the author is never told which regime they are in. Applied: check_skeleton.py --headroom/--strict now always prints declared vs derived estimated_minutes via the canonical recompute_estimated_minutes. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-193 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, three cells with independent adversarial review process Strict-clean does not mean approvable, and the gap is systematic rather than incidental: three drafts in three different cells each passed check_skeleton --strict with zero findings at any severity, and each was independently REJECTED on adversarial review, on defects no deterministic layer measures (label laundering, positional fate bias, consequence-free choices, merge contradictions, quota-shaped design). The gate verifies topology, budgets, and quota arithmetic; the rejections were all about outcomes, consequences, and continuity. Second half of the lesson: both large-cell drafters concluded a hand-author cannot hold the coupled global constraints at 180+ nodes, and each built an ad-hoc structural generator replicating the strict rule set; the only one-shot passes came from that method. Make adversarial critique a mandatory stage of the rebuild drafting workflow (draft, strict gate, in-cell audits, adversarial review, then promotion PR), and ship the structural generator harness as a first-class authoring aid instead of expecting every wave to rebuild it ad hoc. open UW-C126
    AL-194 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, adversarial critiques of all three drafts validator The outcome gates read kind/valence tags, not outcomes, so a draft can satisfy PL-24, the walk floor, and the outcome-spread audit purely by tag distribution over scenes the tags misdescribe. All three pilot drafts did it, two of them unconsciously: the 3-5 draft narrates one identical terminal scene under four kind/valence combinations, one tag contradicting its own beats; the 10-13 draft tags a full mission success neutral and ten failures as discovery; the 13-16 draft has sixteen everyone-survives rescues tagged negative setback and twelve off-page abandonments tagged neutral, plus role= derived mechanically from valence so twelve endings instruct the fill to write a discovery where nothing is discovered. Every headline economy number that passed the gates was a tag artifact. Build the tag-honesty audit: extend scripts/audit_ending_valence.py with an outcome-keyed rubric (goal delivered, goal lost, goal deferred) checked against ending beat text, flag valence/kind contradictions and same-terminal-event ending sets (high pairwise beat similarity across endings), decouple role= from valence, and wire the audit beside the outcome-spread check in the drafting loop. open UW-C127
    AL-195 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, adversarial critiques of the two large drafts validator Choice-level fairness and consequence are invisible to every current metric, and generated drafts fail both by construction. Position bias: in the 10-13 draft the third option leads to an ending 77% of the time and the first option never does; in the 13-16 draft always-pick-option-1 walks to the single best ending with zero risk, because the generator ordered options safe-first in every fan. Consequence: 25 decision nodes in the 10-13 draft have sibling choices with byte-identical reachable-ending sets, and staged merges collapse 98 ancestors into one node while never exceeding direct in-degree 5, laundering exactly the funnel the in-degree cap was ruled to stop. Add computable consequence checks to the strict bar: per-position ending-kind distribution with a skew ceiling plus an argmax-position walk that must not reach a positive ending unscathed; flag sibling choices with identical reachable-ending sets; extend the reconvergence gate with a k-hop ancestor-funnel metric. Generators must seeded-shuffle option order. open UW-C128
    AL-196 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, adversarial critiques of the two large drafts validator Merge-node beat contradictions, the known the-hollow-lighthouse defect class, are reproduced systematically by generation rather than occasionally by hand: eight hard upstream-vs-beat contradictions in each large draft, including endings narrating scenes from choices the reader explicitly declined, characters referenced at merges who are introduced only on other routes, gear appearing from nowhere, and one terminal beat hedging 'whichever stranger you trusted' because the generator knew its parents disagreed. Tier-1 has no state, so every fact a merge-node beat presupposes must hold on every inbound path, and nothing checks it. Give in-degree >= 2 nodes a machine-checkable contract: lint each merge node's presupposed facts (objects, characters, terrain, time of day) against the union of beats on every inbound simple path, flag hedging disjunctions in terminal beats, and until that exists require human beat-vs-parents review of every shared ending in the drafting workflow. open UW-C129
    AL-197 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, 3-5 adversarial critique tooling The drafting loop's gate and the catalog's admission audits are disjoint, so a strict-passing draft can be inadmissible three separate ways and nobody sees it until commit: the 3-5 pilot draft was structural distance 0.065 from puddle-jumping-day (second-closest pair in the whole catalog), its outcome economy survived the spread audit only by one dubious tag, and it was a slotless, contract-less shell with production_eligible: true, which exits the strict gate cleanly and would silently take the legacy free-text fill path in production matching (load_contract_for returns None). Wire check_incell_clones.py and check_outcome_spread.py into the drafting workflow with the candidate temporarily placed in its target cell, and make --strict fail a production_eligible shell that has no slot surfaces and contract sidecar. open UW-C130
    AL-198 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, both large-cell drafters' friction logs validator Several strict constraints are individually reasonable but couple destructively, and the couplings, not the values, dictated the drafts' shape: CG-3's stop ceiling equals roughly two to three nodes at the band words mean (a lone corridor node at the 10-13 mean is already illegal before a normal-weight successor; at 13-16 every checkpoint merge lives within ten words of the wall), so both drafts near-eliminated corridors and one emitted stops at 148-150 of the 150 cap, leaving zero fill headroom; CG-2's exact (3,3) at 8-13 bans the binary dilemma and forces a third strategy at every one of 100+ decisions, which is where template-sameness pressure originates; the 25% gamebook endings fraction makes terminal leaves the only legal padding, pushing toward the shallow-ending sprawl other rules exist to prevent; PL-26's gamebook ceiling of 4.0 is unmotivated by its own comment yet strict-blocking; PL-24's 60% kind ceiling quantizes harshly at four or fewer endings, silently raising the real endings floor for small kid books. Calibration review before rebuild wave 1, deciding each coupling explicitly: exempt the terminal node from CG-3 composition or raise the prose stop ceiling; widen CG-2 to (2,3) at 8-13; key the endings floor to distinct outcome identities or lower the gamebook fraction toward 0.20; anchor or drop PL-26's gamebook 4.0; make PL-24's ceiling count-aware below five endings. Also adopt the headroom discipline: generators target at most 90% of any hard cap, and strict warns at 98%. open UW-C131
    AL-199 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, all three drafters' friction logs docs The authoritative spec for newly drafted skeletons lives in a CLI script's docstring and constants, and the authoring-facing docs either omit or contradict it: skeleton-format.md never mentions CG-3 or its stop-composition rule (the single rule every grandfathered 10-13 medium skeleton fails), the strict topology constraints, or the FILL grammar's actual quoting behavior (apostrophes inside beats='...' are folklore learned from an exemplar); the word 'satisfying' names two different sets (success/completion kinds in PL-20, positive-or-neutral valence in the walk floor) with no doc distinguishing them; ending role= vocabulary is unvalidated folklore; and both pilot briefs drifted from the code because they were hand-copied (one mis-stated PL-26's gamebook ceiling as 6.0 against the code's 4.0). Write the strict-bar authoring reference: a new-skeleton section in the cyo-author skill generated from band_profile.py/choice_grammar.py values rather than hand-copied, covering the five strict policies, CG-3 composition, the two 'satisfying' senses, FILL quoting, and the role vocabulary decision; generate per-cell drafting briefs from code the same way. Applied in 177a4c6: scripts/generate_drafting_brief.py emits the per-cell constraint set from the enforced sources, and skeleton-format.md carries the corrected word table, the strict-bar section (incl. both 'satisfying' senses), the slot/contract grammar with the quoting note, and an honest role= description; the residual (wave-1 briefs actually produced by the generator) rides UW-C132. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-200 2026-08-09 Strict-bar drafting pilot, all three drafting subagents independently process The authoring-lessons mandate collides with subagent authoring runs: CLAUDE.md requires appending lessons at the end of any authoring run, but a scratchpad-scoped subagent cannot discharge it (repo-mutating MUST, feature-branch and signing rules, UW register cross-reference for open lessons), so all three pilot drafters and all three critics correctly declined to write the log and returned candidate lessons to the orchestrator instead.     AL-201 2026-08-09 Same-skeleton diversity experiment: three isolated fills of the-lost-mitten under maximally different theme bindings (review Part 6) validator A same-skeleton story pair has a perceived-similarity floor of 0.50 before any prose exists (PS weights 0.5 leaf + 0.3 structural + 0.2 theme; structural is 1.0 for a same-tree pair by construction and theme was 1.0 because binding never re-themes metadata.themes), and the empirical best case, three independent authors filling three maximally different bindings with near-minimal leaf similarity (0.18-0.20, body trigram Jaccard 0.026-0.029), landed at PS 0.59-0.60 against the 0.70 repeat threshold. Add a structural signal to the family-scoped anti-repeat guard: skeleton id plus beat-variant fingerprint, never serving the same combination twice to one family (cheapest intervention, pure policy); adopt variant beat pools on high-salience nodes (the clue mechanics, the twist ending, the set-piece gag) per SQ-11, which this experiment sizes at roughly 2-3x beat authoring on 4 of 11 nodes with zero topology or validator changes; frame same-skeleton siblings honestly as a series in the product. open UW-C134

    AL-203 2026-08-09 Same-skeleton diversity experiment (review Part 6) process Beats encode world facts the slot system does not govern, and the fill contract's reskin rule is ambiguous enough that three independent authors resolved the same conflicts three different ways: the skeleton's un-slotted snow was imported into an autumn park by one author and reskinned to dew by another; 'one bare hand is cold' was inverted to a hot bare head because the bound item was a sunhat; and one binding produced 'fireflies chirped' because the beat verb belonged to the legacy birds, a world-consistency defect no gate catches.     AL-204 2026-08-09 Opus pipeline analysis for the narrative redesign (review of every FILL-directive consumer) tooling Every consumer of the FILL directive fails open on a parse miss: binding.py, fidelity.py, fidelity_review.py, and slotted_surfaces.py all skip the node when the anchored regex does not match, and three more private regex copies live in mutation/bundle.py, mutation/operators.py, and parameterize_skeleton.py. The consumers were each individually reasonable; the cascade is the defect, and it is invisible until the first format evolution, which the narrative redesign now schedules. Make the parse total before any format work: a body starting with the FILL marker that does not parse becomes a blocking L1 finding; add a lockstep test enumerating every directive consumer and asserting each reports rather than skips on an unparseable directive; collapse the three private regex copies onto storybook/slotted_surfaces.py.     AL-205 2026-08-09 Opus format-design analysis, re-expressing the-lost-mitten node by node validator A node with an in-edge from its own descendant is re-rendered verbatim on every loop, and nothing tells the prose author: the-lost-mitten's three abandon-the-lead choices all target n_start, whose beat stages the loss as fresh news, so all three experiment fills wrote a discovery beat and a child who loops back reads the oh-no moment again on every return. Derive a reentrant flag from the graph (any node reachable from its own successors), have the validator REQUIRE the flag rather than trust the author, and carry a reentry contract into the fill prompt (write established fact, not fresh news).     AL-206 2026-08-09 Narrative-redesign pilot, scene-inventory and recognition ratings over nine fills of one skeleton (proposal section 10) validator Pairwise distinctness margins can be passed while every story shares an attractor vocabulary, because free LLM invention diversifies pairwise and converges collectively: the three fully-free arm C authors, working in isolation, independently produced the same false-clue retcon in 3 of 3 fills, the same nudge-and-catch retrieval in 3 of 3, the same cozy-container napping reveal in 3 of 3, a near-verbatim 'boing boing' eyewitness in 2 of 3, and regressed the choice-label surface to the control template including three verbatim label collisions with a different arm.     AL-218 2026-08-09 Model-tier study, blind three-tier prose comparison (proposal section 13) product Model tier moves prose quality but not sameness: across nine books from one skeleton, blind craft scores ran 4.9 (frontier), 4.0 (Sonnet), 2.2 (Haiku) with ship verdicts of as-is, light-edit, and do-not-publish, while the recognition score was 2.5 for BOTH the frontier and Haiku tiers with the same drivers named independently (keeper-plus-maker pair, four-exit hub menu).     AL-219 2026-08-09 Model-tier study, comparative vs isolated rating of the same books (proposal section 13) process Absolute quality judgments are systematically more forgiving than comparative ones: the same three Haiku books scored 2.2 with a rewrite verdict from a rater holding all nine books side by side, and 3.0 with a one-editing-pass verdict from a rater holding only those three.
