    AL-221 2026-08-09 Prose-craft detector calibration (proposal section 13, commit 4b93b97) validator The prose-craft detectors separate publishable from unpublishable books perfectly, but the separation is IN-SAMPLE by construction: every threshold (--max-unstable-nodes 0, --min-tense-cues 6, --max-node-mix 0.34, --max-moral-tags 0, --max-told-per-1000 0.5) was tuned against the same nine books it is reported to separate, so the result measures fit rather than predictive power. Two thresholds are already known to be fragile: the told-emotion rate ranks one unpublishable book (0.31 per 1000) BELOW one shippable book (0.35), so that detector cannot rank those two and the book is caught only by the other two detectors; and the moral-tag budget of zero is unfalsifiable on a corpus where every shippable book scored zero. Validate out of sample before wiring the detectors into any blocking gate: score a held-out set of books that had no part in calibration, ideally from a different skeleton and band, and re-tune on the union; until then run the detectors as advisory-only and report their findings to the author rather than blocking on them. open UW-C153
    AL-222 2026-08-09 Per-child sibling-exposure analysis (scripts/analyze_sibling_exposure.py, skeleton-free alternatives proposal section 2b) product The unit of story-sameness exposure is the CHILD, not the family, and the system has no per-child skeleton history at all: Storybook carries only family_id and personalization_subject_profile_id, and both reads of prior skeleton_slug (skeleton_match.py:587, diversity/history.py) filter on family with a 20-row window. Family scoping alone triples the second-request repeat rate (0.09 to 0.29 from one child to three) while a child-scoped counterfactual reproduces the single-reader curve, and the shared window hides 81% of a child's own band reading in a three-child household. StoryRequest.profile_id and StorybookAssignment.child_profile_id already carry the needed evidence. Scope the anti-repeat history and weighting to the requesting child rather than the family, widen or drop the 20-row window, and close the visibility='catalog' leak where a cross-family read is invisible to recency. Recovers 25 to 30% of the required catalog for no new content. open UW-C154
    AL-223 2026-08-09 Per-child sibling-exposure analysis (proposal section 2b) product A skeleton is consumable within a child but reusable across children, and nothing in the code contradicts that (no global or cross-family anti-repeat exists; visibility='catalog' actively amortizes one fill across families). Required catalog therefore scales with per-child lifetime consumption inside a band, roughly tenure x rate spread over that band's cells, and is INDEPENDENT of user count, which makes catalog growth a bounded one-time capital cost rather than a cost that grows with the business. Measured need is about 130 skeletons at 0.5 stories per child per month, 408 at 1, and 816 at 2, against 57 production-eligible today. Treat catalog build as bounded capital and size it against measured demand; instrument per-child stories per month per band, which is the single number that sets the target and is not measured in this deployment. open UW-C155
    AL-224 2026-08-09 Per-child sibling-exposure analysis (proposal section 2b) scale Every populated production cell holds 3 or 4 skeletons across all six bands, so a child exhausts a cell by their 4th request in it and every later story in that cell is with certainty a tree they have already read; a repeat is more likely than not by request 3 or 4, and rotating across a band's length cells buys about two extra requests rather than an order of magnitude. This, not the skeleton format, is the measured driver of the sameness the three diversity pilots characterized, and it retires the case for replacing the skeleton architecture. Fund catalog depth and per-child scoping ahead of any pipeline replacement; keep the skeleton-free alternatives as a designed option set to revisit only if those two fixes fail to clear the problem. open UW-C156
    AL-225 2026-08-09 Adversarial review of the skeleton-free alternatives proposal validator SAFE-14 (validator/safety.py:41) is a Phase-2 stub returning an empty report unconditionally, so safety_flagged cannot take a non-false value, yet "zero safety flags" was reported as evidence of safety seven times across pilots 1 to 3 and the model-tier study. The real deterministic pre-LLM denylist floor on untrusted brief material is validator/slots.py, whose only caller is the theme-binding path, so it runs for skeleton fills only and a skeleton-free story has no pre-LLM denylist gate. Separately, the gate is provenance-agnostic but not format-agnostic: PL-19, PL-23, CG-3, and RL-13 each parse the <<FILL words=N>> grammar, and enforce_grammar defaults off so generated stories never run CG-1 through CG-4 at all. Stop reporting safety_flagged as a measured outcome until SAFE-14 is implemented, and mark it explicitly as a stub in any results table; document that the gate's strictness is caller-parameterized so cross-path comparisons state their scale and enforce_grammar settings. open UW-C157
    AL-226 2026-08-09 Adversarial review, strict-bar measurement across the catalog validator The --strict authoring bar passes 2 of 61 catalog skeletons (0 of 11 at 10-13), because it gates newly drafted skeletons while the shipped catalog is grandfathered. Two consequences were being missed: a proposal pre-registered "strict bar: pass by construction" for the baseline, which is false 97% of the time, and the pilots' own control skeleton the-clocktower-cipher is the catalog's single non-production-eligible (10-13, None, None) row, so it is never served to a child and, declaring no length or style, is held to band budgets rather than the ADR-011 cell budgets every production 10-13 skeleton faces. Every pilot baseline number was measured on it. Decide explicitly whether the strict bar is the intended production bar (promoting it as a blocking rule would retire 97% of the catalog, a product decision); and re-baseline future diversity work on a production-eligible skeleton in a real cell. open UW-C158
    AL-227 2026-08-09 Length-demand catalog sizing (scripts/analyze_sibling_exposure.py, proposal section 2b.3a) scale Story-length demand is not flat within a band and the catalog is: every populated cell holds 3 to 4 skeletons while demand concentrates on medium. Because skeleton_matches_cell treats only a NULL length as a wildcard and 0 of 58 production-eligible skeletons declare one, cells are hard partitions, so surplus in the short and long cells is stranded capital that can never serve a medium request. Peaking demand leaves the band TOTAL essentially unchanged (one child's band-lifetime consumption however it splits) but raises the SHORTFALL by 23 to 32% and moves the binding constraint to the medium cell in every band, pulling the first likely repeat forward about one request (P(repeat by request 4) at 8-11 rises from 0.386 flat to 0.647 strongly-medium-weighted). Author against the demand curve rather than filling cells evenly: put the first 6 to 12 skeletons of each band's budget entirely into that band's medium cell, which buys 0.8 to 2.2 more requests before a repeat than an even split; short and long earn marginal skeletons only past roughly request 17 to 20. Measure the real length distribution to replace the assumed regimes. open UW-C159
    AL-228 2026-08-09 Length-demand analysis, intake trace (proposal section 2b.3a) product Kid auto-approve hardcodes length=Length.SHORT band-agnostically (api/story_requests.py:508), which steers exactly the requests where nobody is choosing into the thinnest-demand tier, and for the teen bands it is an outright production bug: 13-16 and 16+ have no short cell by ADR-011 design and hold no short skeletons, so candidates_for_cell returns empty and the authoring plan 422s every time for a teen-band child with auto-approve enabled. Separately, ADR-011's band-by-length rule is enforced nowhere in the request path (the approve body validates band against style only, and both length selectors render all three lengths for every band), so a guardian can approve a long 3-5 book or a short 13-16 book and hit the same empty-cell failure later. Make the auto-approve length band-aware (reuse the _length_of teen fallback rather than a constant) and default it to the demand-weighted tier rather than short; add band-by-length validation to the approve and authored-create bodies and gate the frontend length options by band, so an unservable cell is rejected at intake rather than 422ing at planning time. open UW-C160
    AL-229 2026-08-09 Per-request mutation pilot on the-midnight-museum (alternatives proposal section 11.5.1) scale Bounded mutation of a single parent is not a catalog multiplier, and the reason generalizes: every accepted mutant preserved 100% of the parent's <<FILL>> beat directives (95 of 95 nodes and beats across all three mutants), so mutation moves the graph while recognition is driven by the scene content and decision semantics that live in the beats. Shape-preserving operators scored structural distance exactly 0.0000 (M1 on all five swap pairs tried, including cross-act), the shape-changing M4 reconvergence variant reached 0.0038, and a maximum-length chain using only the parent's own material reached 0.0064, all below the committed TAU_CELL of 0.05, while hand-authored same-cell siblings sit at a median of 0.390. A rater landed the same-book verdict at reading position 3 (score 2.0) with the structural difference invisible until position 8. Applicability was not the constraint: M4 had 2,201 eligible sites. Withdraw per-request mutation as a diversity lever and fund catalog depth instead; if a structural multiplier is still wanted, test cross-skeleton recombination (M3 graft) separately, since the only mutant to clear the floor did so by importing 32 nodes from a different skeleton, which scales with pairs of existing skeletons rather than replacing the need for them. open UW-C161
    AL-230 2026-08-09 Per-request mutation pilot, deterministic bench (alternatives proposal section 11.5.1) validator structural_distance and the committed TAU_CELL floor were vindicated on this evidence rather than refuted: the floor rejected exactly the mutants the reader rejected, and the metric's ordering matched the reader's ordering. The metric's known order-blindness and self-declared topology weighting did not bite because no bounded mutant came within an order of magnitude of the threshold. This is not a general exoneration, since the failure mode it cannot see (identical scene function at identical position) is precisely what a mutant preserves. Keep TAU_CELL as the anti-clone gate for catalog-time work, and continue to treat structural_distance as unsuitable for judging perceived diversity between artifacts that already share authored content; revisit only if a candidate approaches the threshold. open delivered on the story-diversity work, currently OPEN on PR #661; the earlier SHAs live only on a scratch branch that will never merge, so this flips to applied on the merge commit
    AL-231 2026-08-09 Per-request mutation pilot, sibling-fill measurement (alternatives proposal section 11.5.1) process A sibling-convergence measurement is invalid when one author writes both arms: the second book's first draft was a sentence-level world swap of the first at 302 shared grams per 1000, and two deliberate de-convergence passes only brought it to 70.4, still an order of magnitude above the 4.0 budget and roughly three times the worst previously measured arm. The number therefore measures the author's de-convergence effort rather than the condition under test. Separately, the recognition rating could not be run in an isolated agent in this environment, so it is author-scored rather than blind. Require an independence protocol for any sibling-fill arm: one isolated author per arm with no sight of the other arms, and a rater that has not seen the generation plan. Where isolation is impossible, report the measurement as author-scored and treat it as an upper bound on distinctness. open UW-C162
    AL-232 2026-08-10 Obligation-variance experiment, contract variant review (docs/planning/evidence/obligation-variance/) process An admissibility bar that enumerates fields silently exempts every field it omits. The bar for a contract variant required divergence in 2 of establishes, choice_semantics, affect, and function; two variants passed it at 26/26 nodes on all three pairs while their beat_hint strings were the shipped contract's sentences with single nouns swapped, byte-identical at n_end_library across all three variants, at or above 0.85 similarity at 10 of 26 nodes against v1, and above 0.60 at 22 of 26. beat_hint is the most direct instruction a fill agent reads, so the intervention the experiment exists to test was largely undelivered; because a null result was the expected outcome, the run would have been uninterpretable, since "obligation variance does not work" could not have been separated from "the obligations were never varied." Gate variant admissibility with check_variant_divergence.py --check, which adds a beat_hint similarity ceiling (0.60 difflib) against every other variant including the shipped one. More generally, when a bar enumerates fields, state which fields it does NOT cover, so an exemption is a decision rather than an oversight. open UW-C166
    AL-233 2026-08-10 Obligation-variance experiment, blind recognition rating (spec section 12) product Obligation variance is refuted as the diversity lever, and the refutation identifies the actual fingerprint: recognition landed at position 2 against a pre-registered margin of past position 5, with distinctness 2.0 against the control's 2.5, while all six quality guards passed. Both contracts varied choice_semantics completely at the landing nodes, yet the blind rater recorded the same fork in the same order at position 2 and the same four-room fan at position 5, because a choice's DESTINATION is graph structure rather than contract content: choice 1 still leads to the note-decoding scene, and both authors must still write a stair, a study, a catwalk, and a basement. This unifies the prior nulls rather than adding one, since devices change the nouns in the rooms, prose the wording, model tier the quality, and obligations why the rooms matter, while none of them changes the rooms. Stop searching for a format fix inside a single graph; treat single-use per child as inherent to a shared armature. Fund catalog depth per cell and evaluate cross-skeleton recombination, the only mechanism that ever cleared the anti-clone floor. Record in the drafting guide that per-node obligations cannot vary what a reader perceives at a fork. open UW-C167
    AL-234 2026-08-10 Obligation-variance experiment, residual menu-frame collision (spec section 12.5) validator Unslotted choice labels are a recognition channel no check covers. 13 of the clocktower skeleton's 35 choice labels carry no slot token (Climb the spiral stair., Spin the hands at random and hope.), so they are byte-identical across every binding; NC-8 warns about unslotted ENDING titles and is silent on choice labels, even though choice-menu semantics was already named as the residual leak in AL-216. Observed live: two isolated authors on different contracts and different settings both rewrote Climb the spiral stair. to Head up the spiral stair., because the fixed destination noun left only the verb free. Extend the NC-8 unslotted warning from ending titles to choice labels, and add a per-binding label-divergence check so a label whose destination noun is frozen is flagged at contract time rather than discovered by a sibling-gram round. open UW-C168
    AL-235 2026-08-10 Obligation-variance experiment, device collision the bench missed (spec section 12.5) validator Mechanic Divergence is category-scoped and blind to cross-category device collisions. MD scored the two arms' bibles 0.978 against tau 0.34 with no within-category kind overlap, while arm C's cipher_hint_carriers/pattern_in_mechanism ("long, long, short") and arm D's cipher_forms/rhythm_code ("read each pull as long or short") are the same device; the blind rater caught it unaided ("the two books' secret codes are the same code"). A metric that compares multisets within a category cannot see a device that moved category. Add a cross-category pass to check_bible_diversity: compare every category of one bible against every category of the other for semantic collision, or at minimum flag shared distinctive tokens across category boundaries, so MD cannot certify 0.978 for two books sharing a cipher. open UW-C169
    AL-236 2026-08-10 Obligation-variance experiment, sibling-gram guard misfire (spec section 12.2) process A calibrated budget carries a protocol stage with it, and comparing across stages manufactures a false failure. The 4.0 shared-grams-per-1000 budget is calibrated on POST-revision output because the control pair went through a gate-revise-regate round (AL-215); gating un-revised treatment output against it reported a guard failure at 6.4 when the matched-stage comparison was control 9.0 pre-revision against treatment 6.4 pre-revision, so the treatment pair actually started LESS convergent than the control. Separately, check_sibling_fills --check gates on grams only, so the spec's margin of 0 menu frames was going unenforced entirely.     AL-237 2026-08-10 Obligation-variance experiment, arm C isolation disclosure and arm D discretion (spec section 12.6) process Isolation between parallel authoring agents leaks through the shared filesystem, and identical briefs still produce asymmetric effort. Arm C ran ls on the shared work directory and saw the other arm's filenames before writing (a tool-call audit confirmed it read no content, and the brief had already disclosed a second author, so the exposure was immaterial); more consequentially, arm D volunteered a sentence-splitting pass that cut its reading-level warnings from 19 to 2 while arm C left its 20 standing, so the two books differ in sentence rhythm for reasons unrelated to the treatment.     AL-238 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, blind relabelling (docs/planning/decision-variance-experiment-spec-2026-08-10.md section 8.2) process A metric computed from self-declared labels cannot be measured by the party declaring the labels. An author asked to minimise decision overlap, scored on a signature block it also authored, moved tradeoff reuse from 0.929 to 0.179 and passed every gate; an independent annotator applying one written principle to the same two artifacts scored the identical pair at 1.000. Inspection showed the drop came from relabelling rather than rewriting: n_clockface's four choices read "answer the test on its own terms" against "set the levers on the board's own terms", the same four decisions with different nouns, while c_face_random was reclassified PHYSICAL_RISK to MORAL and c_face_panel INFORMATION to CRAFT. The author was not cheating, it was optimising what it was scored on. Annotation must be independent of authoring for any signature-based diversity metric. Applies directly to the externally proposed decision-program compiler, which would both emit DecisionSignatures and be scored on them; that design needs a separate scorer or a derived-from-artifact labelling step. open UW-C172
    AL-239 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, instrument construction (spec section 8.2) validator A free-text action field makes an exact-repetition bar vacuous, because the surface changing while the decision does not IS the defect being measured. Two contracts scored 0 of 35 identical action strings while a blind annotator judged 34 of 35 the same decision: set_the_dial_deliberately against set_the_levers_deliberately is one act and two strings. Separately, six of eighteen nodes offered a single option; a one-option node is a page turn rather than a decision, and including them pulled the aggregate family rate to 0.486, inside its 0.6 ceiling, while n_vault and n_setjam sat at 1.00 and the three principal forks at 0.67 to 0.75.     AL-240 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, two authoring attempts on a fixed graph (spec section 8.3) product Decisions appear to be pinned by the graph together with fact-graph closure, not merely by authorial habit. Two attempts to author genuinely different decisions over one unchanged 26-node graph in one unchanged world, the second explicitly instructed to move tradeoff and consequence rather than the verb and iterated against a metric, produced 28 of 28 options that a blind annotator called the same decision. The single fork that did move, n_open, is the one with no incoming constraint. The mechanism is that each fork's children must deliver what their own descendants require and merge closure propagates those requirements backward, so the kind of thing a branch accomplishes is fixed even when every prop and sentence changes. Treat the verifiability/freedom tension as evidenced rather than hypothetical: a shape-only skeleton is decision-free only if its entry and exit facts are also free, and free facts cannot be merge-verified before prose. A decision-program compiler must therefore generate the fact graph and the decisions together rather than assigning decisions onto a fixed fact skeleton. Retest on a production-eligible graph before treating the magnitude as settled. open UW-C174
    AL-241 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, run termination (spec sections 8, 8.5) process Terminating an experiment at the point the intervention cannot be constructed is cheaper and more informative than running it to a rating. This run stopped before any fill because blind annotation showed the treatment was not delivered, which saved two fills and a rating and produced a sharper finding than a null rating would have: not that varying decisions fails to help, but that varying them on a fixed graph is much harder than assumed. A null rating would have been uninterpretable in exactly the way AL-232 describes. Add a delivery check to every intervention spec: an independent verification, before any measurement is spent, that the intervention actually differs from the control on the dimension it claims to vary. Make it a standing precondition rather than a per-experiment afterthought. open UW-C175
    AL-242 2026-08-10 Metric build, retention exemption review (supabase/migrations/20260810000000_*, publishing/state_machine.py) tooling A docstring's claim about the codebase rots, and reasoning from it silently produced a wrong production predicate. publishing/state_machine.py said the draft --auto_reject--> needs_revision hop "has no slice-1 caller"; slice 2 landed and moderation/pipeline.py drives it on a classifier hard BLOCK. An agent building a data-retention exemption read that docstring, concluded needs_revision implies a human send-back, and wrote a predicate that would have preserved every machine-rejected story's raw LLM output indefinitely: widening ADR-007's retention window with no human decision to justify it, and filling the calibration corpus it existed to build with rows carrying no reviewer judgment. The correct key is the SENT_BACK pipeline event, which only the human path writes. Fixed the docstring and keyed the exemption on the event. More generally, a docstring asserting that something has no caller is a claim that must carry a #VERIFY and be re-checked by grep before anything is built on it; prefer keying policy on an event that only the intended actor emits rather than on a status any actor can reach. open UW-C176
    AL-243 2026-08-10 Metric build, inter-annotator agreement measurement (docs/planning/decision-signature-labelling-principle.md) process Independent annotation of decision signatures is reliable, which corrects the diagnosis implied by AL-238. Two annotators given only a contract and a written convention, with no knowledge of what was being compared, reached Fleiss' kappa 0.796 on action_family, 0.816 on target_role, and 0.758 on both tradeoff and consequence over 35 choices, all clearing the 0.60 floor. The earlier 0.179-versus-1.000 swing was therefore never annotator unreliability; it was one annotator having authored the artifact and being scored on the result. As a free by-product, both annotators independently raised the same three vocabulary gaps (no family separating searching a mechanism from reading a document, no public-versus-private tradeoff axis, and consequence: LOCATION doing double duty for arrival and progress), which is stronger evidence for a v2 vocabulary than either alone. Invest in independence and a versioned written convention rather than in a richer vocabulary or a stronger annotator model, and treat the externally proposed signature architecture as viable on that condition.     AL-244 2026-08-10 Metric build, branch-obligation checker (scripts/check_branch_obligations.py) tooling A deterministic property of the plan reproduced two results that had each cost a full measurement round. Comparing, per branch, the facts a destination presupposes that its fork does not already guarantee, the checker scores same-shape rate 1.000 on the pair a blind annotator judged 28 of 28 identical decisions, and 1.000 again on the earlier pair a human rater put at recognition position 2. It also surfaces the mechanism, seven one-for-one fact renames such as past_the_seal to past_the_barred_door. It needs no model, no annotation and no prose, so it runs in milliseconds before a fill is committed. Its limits are real: it was validated on two known-bad pairs with no known-good example, so it is a screen rather than an arbiter and its threshold is uncalibrated. Run the deterministic screen before spending any measurement on an artifact, and look for a computable-from-the-plan proxy before commissioning a fill or a rating in future experiments. Calibrate the threshold once a genuinely divergent contract exists, and keep independent annotation as the arbiter. open UW-C178
    AL-245 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, v5 arm fill shell (docs/planning/decision-variance-experiment-spec-2026-08-10.md section 9) tooling A fill shell that pre-binds choice labels hands the author the previous book's vocabulary, and the author stays inside it while rewriting every word. Because 13 of 35 skeleton choice labels carry no slot token (AL-234), binding produced clocktower-dial wording in a salvage story, and the author changed 35 of 35 labels yet still wrote "Force the hands into place instead" and "Spin the hands and hope for the best" against the shell's "Force the hands by guesswork" and "Spin the hands at random and hope". Every deterministic guard passed while sibling grams hit 28.8 per 1000, the highest ever measured, with 4 shared menu frames. A shell handed to a fill agent must express every author-controlled string as a FILL directive and carry no skeleton prose at all.     AL-246 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, v5 arm rating (spec section 9) tooling Device collision between two books in one world dominates a reader's verdict and can invalidate a whole measurement round. Only 6 of the 14 sat at the same node; the other 8 were the same props relocated, which a same-slot diff scores as fresh and which a rater described unprompted as variety fork by fork but pure rearrangement at the book level. Sharing a world is the series contract and must never be penalised; sharing the props inside it reads as the same book. Built scripts/check_device_collision.py, which compares every prop against every prop rather than slot against slot, so relocation is caught, and flags rare shared vocabulary so a device reworded into another category is caught too (it fires on the AL-235 rhythm pair that check_bible_diversity certified at 0.978).     AL-247 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, v5 contract (spec section 9) validator The branch-obligation screen has a measured false negative, which corrects the framing in AL-244. A third contract over the same graph, written to break the obligation structure, scored same-shape rate 0.000 with zero one-for-one renames, meaning the fact graph was rebuilt rather than repainted. Blind independent annotation of that contract against the original still returned 28 of 28 options asking the same decision, with action-family, tradeoff, consequence and ordered-sequence rates all 1.000, worst fork n_backpanel. A high same-shape rate is therefore strong evidence the decisions repeat; a low one is no evidence at all that they differ. This also refutes the fact-graph-closure explanation in AL-240: closure was broken and the decisions did not move. Treat the screen as one-way, for cheap rejection only, and never as a delivery certificate; independent annotation stays the only delivery check for a decision-variance intervention. Docstring corrected in place.     AL-248 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, rating instrument (spec section 9) process The five-question instrument is mostly dead weight on a shared skeleton, and two blind raters found the same missing question without conferring. Q1 (same kinds of actions) and Q4 (repeated sequence) both saturated at 5 for both pairs, because with one node skeleton across all three books those answers are fixed before a word is read; Q2 came out a wash or mildly against the eventual verdict, leaving the whole judgement resting on Q3. Both raters independently proposed the same sixth item, whether solving the first book gives you the answer to the second, and both said it would have separated the pairs immediately. One reported having to smuggle it into Q3. Add a solution-transfer question to the instrument and treat it as the primary item, since it is the only one that discriminated.     AL-249 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, rating instrument (spec section 9) product Two blind raters independently reported a per-book defect that the pair framing structurally hides: the n_inside four-room fork has no consequence in any of the three books, every room yields the same pattern and every road reconverges at n_clockface, and roughly seven of nine forks on this pilot graph either do not branch or reconverge one node later. Because the defect is identical in all three books it scores the same everywhere and cancels out of every pairwise comparison, so a diversity programme measuring only pairs can run indefinitely without seeing it. Both raters then attached a product judgment to that structural fact, calling it illusory choice and a likely threat to the reading experience. The owner rejected that judgment: reconverging exploration paths are a convention of the form. The lesson is therefore about raters over-reaching from an accurate structural observation into a product call that is not theirs, which is the same class of error as the earlier misreading of the central defect. Add a per-book illusory-choice check before any pair comparison: flag every fork whose branches reconverge with no difference in what they deliver, computable from the contract as branches whose obligations are equal and whose subgraphs rejoin within N nodes. Report it per book, never per pair. rejected owner ruling, decision-variance-experiment-spec-2026-08-10.md section 9.9: loop-back exploration is a convention of the form, not a flaw, on the tabletop analogy that sweeping every room is the play. The structural observation stands; the defect framing does not, and no gate will be built.
    AL-250 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, second attempt (docs/planning/decision-variance-experiment-spec-2026-08-10.md section 9.5) validator The decision-signature instrument ranks two book pairs in the opposite order from readers, on every axis. One blind annotator labelling all three plans scored the control pair 24 of 28 same decisions (family 0.929, tradeoff 0.893, sequence 0.909) against the treatment pair's 28 of 28 and 1.000, while two blind raters in counterbalanced order both judged the treatment pair the LESS decision-repetitive of the two. Replicated: two further independent annotators put the control at 24 and 23 of 28. Unreliability does not explain it, since kappa between annotators on the same artifacts is 0.961 and 0.962 on action_family and 1.000 on consequence. AL-243 established reliability; this establishes that reliability was not sufficient. Stop treating any v1 signature field as decision-carrying: report only, route nothing, until a vocabulary is validated against reader judgement rather than against another annotator.     AL-251 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, signature diff (spec section 9.6) validator The inversion has an exact and fixable cause, and it runs in both directions at once. Deaf where it counts: at the three forks both raters independently named decisive (n_clockface, n_vault, n_setjam), all three plans carry identical signatures choice for choice, because "compute a value and dial it" and "match a shape against a full-size drawing and seat the part" are one signature and two kinds of thinking.     AL-252 2026-08-10 Decision-variance experiment, rating (spec sections 9.3, 9.4) product Varying the act a choice asks for does reduce perceived decision repetition, thinly, and the reader-invented question is what detects it. Two blind raters in counterbalanced order both chose the control pair as more decision-repetitive, agreeing exactly on Q2 (5,5 against 4,4), Q3 (2,2 against 3,3) and Q6 (4,4 against 3,3), and both named the same three decisive forks. The result holds against a stacked deck: the treatment shares the base book's entire world while the control changes world wholesale, and one rater noted the verdict would flip if shared world counted, which the owner's definition says it must not. Q6, solution transfer, was proposed independently by both raters of the discarded round and on first use discriminated cleanly while Q1 and Q4 saturated at 5 for both pairs exactly as they predicted. Both raters called the effect thin: three re-skins of one graph, separation resting on three forks of eleven. Treat solution transfer as the primary construct for the diversity programme rather than action-family overlap, and retest on a production-eligible graph before treating the magnitude as real. Separate the two changes the treatment bundled, different decision content and four rooms yielding distinct components, since one rater credited the latter explicitly and they are confounded here. open UW-C183
    AL-253 2026-08-10 Diversity test register, D-3 (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) validator The signature instrument was annotating the wrong artifact, which is a layer error rather than a vocabulary error. Adding reasoning_kind and stake to the annotation of the contracts fixed nothing: reasoning_kind inverted the reader ordering exactly as action_family had (control 0.929 against treatment 1.000) and stake tied at 1.000, with zero of six fields ordering the pairs as readers did. The reason is verifiable without any annotator: the contracts describe the decisive fork as "answer the test on its own terms, set it deliberately" and "fit the piece the way the diagram shows, deliberately", which Rule 2 of the labelling principle correctly calls one decision. The distinction both raters named, adding two numbers and carrying against holding a part against its outline, lives in the binding (clock_arithmetic, rhythm_code, pictogram_code), not in the contract. This also partly retracts AL-251: the vocabulary was not deaf at the climax, the contract was silent there and the vocabulary reported that silence faithfully. The scenery-leakage half of AL-251 stands. Annotate contract plus binding rather than contract alone, and re-specify any architecture that plans decision variety at the contract layer. Three of the proposed architectures (reviewer 2's decision-program compiler, reviewer 1's decision-first abstract routing, and the in-house decision-axis scheduling) schedule decisions in a representation that provably omits the property readers respond to, which is a defect in those designs and not only in our instrument. open UW-C184
    AL-254 2026-08-10 Diversity test register, D-3b and D-3c (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) validator Annotating the binding alongside the contract recovers the property readers respond to, and the recovery is real but fragile. With each plan's bound devices attached, reasoning_kind becomes the only field of six that orders the two book pairs as readers did, and the pre-registered primary (that field over the six forks the book's code runs through) passed under both annotators, as did the prediction that the entry forks would invert. But the magnitude collapsed on replication, 1.000 against 0.000 for one annotator and 0.333 against 0.167 for the other, and over the full option set the second annotator ties. The cause is one underspecified vocabulary boundary: kappa on reasoning_kind is 1.000 on the arithmetic plan and 0.919 on the pictogram plan but 0.719 on the rhythm plan, because decoding a symbolic notation sits between COMPUTE and MATCH and the definitions do not say which. That single call decides whether the control's two books share a reasoning kind. Write the COMPUTE/MATCH boundary explicitly for symbolic decoding, and treat the rewrite as a reliability fix only. Re-scoring these same three plans under a sharpened rule cannot re-confirm the hypothesis, because the sharpening determines the decisive item by construction and a motivated author would choose the direction that rescues the result. Validity has to be retested on artifacts the vocabulary has never seen. open UW-C185
    AL-255 2026-08-10 Diversity test register, commit 2b854d5 process Chaining a file edit and a git commit in one shell invocation lets a failed edit commit anyway, and the commit message then describes content that is not in the diff. A Python heredoc doing the edit raised AssertionError on an anchor that no longer matched; because the commit was a separate command in the same invocation rather than chained to the edit's exit status, it ran and pushed three label files under a message claiming to record a result and pre-register the follow-up analysis, neither of which was present. Caught on the next read of the file, corrected by a follow-up commit rather than a history rewrite, since the bad commit was already pushed. Never chain an edit and its commit in one invocation. Verify the staged diff against the intended message before committing, and make anchor-based edits fail loudly enough to stop the sequence. This matters more than ordinary commit hygiene here because these commits are the evidence record for experiments whose results nobody can reproduce from memory. open UW-C186
    AL-256 2026-08-10 D-2 fills, arm P (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) process The presence of an agent's output file is not evidence the agent has finished, and acting on one mid-run silently corrupts the work. Arm P's filled_P.json existed on disk and parsed cleanly, so it was read, verified, and character-renamed; the author then kept working and rewrote the same path four minutes later, making the renamed copy a derivative of a draft that no longer existed (10,608 words against the final 10,504). The author's own report flagged the orphan file it had not created, which is how it was caught. It was also reported upward as "all three fills are in" while one was still writing. Wait for the completion notification before reading, verifying or transforming any agent artifact, and never infer completion from a file existing. Where a derived copy is made, record the source's modification time alongside it so staleness is detectable rather than invisible. applied rename redone against the final files; renamed_P.json rebuilt and verified structurally identical to the shell
    AL-257 2026-08-10 D-2 fills, cross-arm convergence (register, D-2 section) product Same-model idiom convergence reaches proper nouns and titles, not just phrasing, and it survives strict isolation. Three authors in separate directories, given one device-agnostic contract and three deliberately non-colliding bindings, all named the companion Teo (38, 61 and 47 uses), two named the protagonist Nora, and all three titled the book identically. Three ending titles collided across arms, one of them (Goodnight Through the Door) in all three at the same node. Grepping every input file confirmed Teo and Nora appear in none of them, so the name convergence has no leak to explain it. The title convergence does: the shell still carried the skeleton's id, sk_midnight_frequency, which every author read and named its book from. Neutralise every identifying field in a fill shell, not just the prose fields: id, title, metadata and slugs all leak. Treat cross-arm name and title collision as a measurable convergence signal in its own right and check it before rating, since it is invisible to the shared-gram measure that is supposed to catch convergence. open UW-C187
    AL-258 2026-08-10 D-2 guard battery (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product Sharing one narrative contract across books makes the contract's own wording the fingerprint. Three isolated authors writing from one contract and three non-colliding bindings produced 653 and 717 shared 4-grams per pair, 59.2 and 63.8 per 1000 words against a budget of 4.0, and 51 and 41 identical choice-menu openings out of 131. The pilot, whose books scored 1.8 to 2.7 per 1000 and zero shared menus, differed in exactly one respect: its arms read different contracts, whose choice_semantics were 0 of 35 identical, where D-2's three arms read 131 of 131 identical. The first diagnosis, that the contract was lexically over-prescriptive, was tested and refuted: labels reuse a distinctive word from their own semantics at 46.6 percent in D-2 against 54.3 percent in the pilot, so per-book reuse is higher in the non-converging case. It is sharing, not prescriptiveness. Any architecture that reuses one plan across many books must treat the plan's own prose as a convergence source and either neutralise choice_semantics wording, generate it per book, or require authors to diverge from it explicitly. This bears directly on every proposed architecture built on a reusable plan object. For D-2 specifically the arm design was wrong: it mirrored the pilot's arm structure while varying only bindings, where the pilot varied contracts. open UW-C188
    AL-259 2026-08-10 D-2 guard battery, reading level validator Reading level degrades badly at production scale and the gate cannot stop it, because every finding is advisory. All three 101-node books landed at whole-book Flesch-Kincaid 8.14 to 8.41 against a 5.5 target with 1.5 tolerance, with only 16 to 20 of 101 nodes inside the band and 81 to 85 RL-13 warnings each, yet all three returned blocked=False. The pilot's 26-node books ranged 4.99 to 7.45 on the same measure. Model tier is a candidate but not established: one pilot book written on the stronger tier also sat out of band at 7.45, so length and node count are confounded with tier. Make aggregate reading level a blocking condition rather than 85 advisory warnings nobody reads: a book with four fifths of its nodes outside the band is not age-appropriate whatever the per-node rule says. Separately, test tier against scale directly before attributing this to the cheaper model. applied scripts/check_reading_level.py
    AL-260 2026-08-10 D-4, scripts/check_solution_transfer.py validator A rarity threshold calibrated on a large corpus silently inverts when applied to a subset. The device-collision check treats a word used by at most two props as rare, calibrated over 24-prop bindings. Reused inside a 6-prop and then a 2-prop solution chain, the corpus shrinks to four props and very nearly every content word qualifies, so the signal fires on everything. It reported three plainly different waypoint marks, a scratched star, a painted spiral and an inked triangle, as the same device, on the shared words logbook's, mark and margins, which are the contract's own framing for that slot rather than any book's device. Judge rarity over the whole artifact a threshold was calibrated on, never over the subset being scored, and state the corpus explicitly in any measure that inherits a calibrated threshold. Audit every other measure that reuses a calibrated constant on a filtered input. open UW-C190
    AL-261 2026-08-10 D-4, operation tiers against the 101-node bindings validator A word-list classifier for "what kind of thinking does this puzzle ask" ranks on the artifacts it was written from and collapses on any other. It reproduced three known reader rankings on the pilot, then classified 2 of 6 chain props on an unseen contract. Two failure modes, neither fixable by adding words: no negation, so "a page of small hand-drawn icons instead of numbers" scores as arithmetic; and polysemy, so "a short tail" on a drawn symbol scores as rhythm. The one cross-arm match it did report was an artifact of the slot, since every waypoint mark in that world is a drawn symbol. This is the second measure in this programme good enough to rank and not good enough to gate, after the fill-fidelity triage. Stop building lexical proxies for semantic properties in this programme; the expected outcome is now a ranking aid, not a gate. Where a property must be checkable, declare it as a field in the narrative contract rather than inferring it from the prose: the plan schema needs an explicit operation field. open UW-C191
    AL-262 2026-08-10 D-6 rig construction (docs/planning/evidence/d6-contract-sharing/build.py) product Choice semantics cannot be neutralised mechanically from the fact graph, because the fact graph does not contain the decision. Deriving each branch's semantics from the facts its destination presupposes needs no author and so cannot smuggle in a voice, which is why it was tried first. It also destroys the fork: at the pilot's central four-way decision, answering the code, forcing the dial, going round the back and guessing at random all own exactly the same obligation and flatten to one identical sentence. This is AL-247 reached from the opposite direction, and it means the D-2 repair that looked cheapest and most objective is unavailable. Any "flatten the plan's wording" repair must be authored under a stated rule and treated as itself under test, not derived. More generally, stop proposing fact-graph derivations for properties that D-3 and AL-247 have already located above the fact layer. open UW-C192
    AL-263 2026-08-10 Q-1 catalog count (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) process The catalog's depth was being counted in the wrong unit, and nobody had counted either. 61 skeletons over 17 band-by-length cells, 13 of them holding four or fewer, so the exhaustion premise holds. But 2 of 61 skeletons carry a narrative contract, which is the artifact every measure in this programme and every proposed architecture actually needs, at roughly 1.7KB per node of hand authoring. Whether that cost is per skeleton or per book is decided by AL-258, so a research result decides which capital purchase this is. Track narrative-contract coverage as a first-class catalog metric alongside skeleton count, and do not scope any depth purchase until the contract-sharing question is settled. open UW-C193
    AL-264 2026-08-10 D-6 (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product Contract sharing is confirmed as a cause of cross-book convergence, and neither cheap repair fixes it. Holding graph, bindings, model and isolation constant, moving two arms from separate contracts to one moves shared 4-grams from 2.9 to 17.2 per 1000 against a budget of 4.0. The "changing only" framing this row originally used is withdrawn (2026-08-12): two separate contracts differ in premise, obligations and fact set as well as in document count, so the 5.9x measures sharing a plan as a bundle rather than the document-sharing channel alone, and the 2.9 is the pilot's rig rather than a fourth D-6 arm. The cause claim survives; only the isolation claim was too strong. Flattening the shared wording reaches 11.8 and instructing authors to diverge from it reaches 13.6, both still around three times budget; at one pair per condition their ordering flips depending on whether labels are counted, so neither is better, both are insufficient. Figures corrected 2026-08-11: published as 16.9, 11.4 and 12.9, re-derived from the frozen artifacts at body-only scope as 17.2, 11.8 and 13.6, with the 2.9 control reproducing exactly. See AL-296 and the research brief's 16g.1 correction block; the conclusion is unchanged. Treat AL-258 as established and stop proposing wording-level repairs as sufficient. The third repair is no longer untested and the prediction held. D-7 generated everything below a shared stratum per book, the decisional stratum included, and landed at 13.6, still more than three times budget; D-7b then showed the operative variable was the prose in the shared half rather than what was generated per book, reaching 2.3 by deleting 422 words and changing nothing else (AL-282, and AL-284 for the correction to its stated mechanism). Per-book generation of the decisional stratum is therefore ruled out as sufficient on its own, and the open question moved to which shared prose matters. Do not reopen this row's prediction as pending work; the successor experiment is the third arm named in AL-284. open UW-C194
    AL-265 2026-08-10 D-6 gram attribution (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product The convergence leak has at least four channels and choice_semantics is not the main one. Tracing shared grams to the contract field they draw on: choice_semantics under half, beat_hint similar, premise as much or more, and about a quarter tracing to no contract field at all, which is same-model idiom (AL-257) that no plan-level intervention reaches. Categories overlap, so this is indicative rather than a partition. Two consequences: a reusable plan that shares the dramatic question is already sharing the largest traceable channel, and there is an idiom floor bounding what a shared-language guard can ever certify. Move premise into the per-book stratum alongside choice_semantics and beat_hint, and set the shared-gram budget for reusable-plan architectures with the idiom floor measured rather than assumed. Amend the architecture re-specification, which put the premise on the shared side. open UW-C195
    AL-266 2026-08-10 D-6 confound check process A cross-experiment comparison inherited a second difference that nearly invalidated it, and the check that saved it was cheap. The pilot's shells shipped draft choice labels, 13 of 35 identical across its arms, where D-6's authors wrote every label from scratch, so the baseline and the treatment differed in two ways rather than one. Splitting the measure by prose part settled it in one run: labels contribute zero shared 4-grams in every condition including the pilot, so the whole signal is in bodies, which were authored from scratch throughout. Before comparing a new run against a historical baseline, diff the two authoring tasks and not only the artifacts, and where a confound is found try to partition the measure rather than caveating the result. open UW-C196
    AL-267 2026-08-10 D-6 addendum, generator idiom floor product The shared-gram budget of 4.0 was never validated against what the generator can actually achieve, and it turns out to be just above it. Measured on book pairs sharing nothing but the model and the age band (different graph, different contract, different world), the floor is 3.3 shared 4-grams per 1000, range 1.9 to 5.0. Two consequences neither of which was known: the budget is reachable, so no architecture fails it on a technicality; and the pilot's one-contract-per-book design scores 2.9, indistinguishable from books sharing nothing, so not converging is already a solved problem and the only open question is whether reuse can be bought back. D-6's repairs sit at 3.6 times the floor, so they failed with a factor of three of headroom unclaimed rather than against a hard limit. The floor also corroborates the D-6 gram attribution independently: a quarter of 17.2 is 4.3, against a directly measured 3.3. (Both figures were restated on 2026-08-11 from 3.5 and "a quarter of 16.9 is 4.2": the original counts joined each book's bodies into one string and so counted 4-grams straddling body boundaries, which do not exist in any body. The conclusion is unchanged and the direction of the error was to overstate convergence.) Record 3.3 as the measured floor beside the 4.0 budget wherever the budget is cited, and re-measure it whenever the generation model changes, since it is a property of the model rather than of any architecture. open UW-C197
    AL-268 2026-08-10 M-2 deterministic pre-test (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product The catalog's large graphs are linear-with-decorations, not worlds, and it shows in their shape rather than in any reading. Removing the hub from each of the 21 graphs at 200-plus nodes and taking the components of the remainder: 18 have one spoke holding nearly every node (the 677-node graph puts 656 of 677 in a single mass) with the rest being 1-to-4-node early exits, so there is no second region from which to cut a disjoint tour. Only the-skyrail-heist (10-13, 246 nodes, spokes of 83/82/77), the-year-of-four-banners and the-tricameral-city are genuinely world-shaped. A first attempt using max-flow node-disjoint paths returned 1 for all 21 and looked like a total refutation; the single cut node is the hub at depth 1 to 5 in every case, which is what a hub-and-spoke world should have, so strict node-disjointness was the wrong requirement. Scope M-2 to the three named graphs rather than to "the largest", and add spoke-balance to the catalog metrics so world-shaped graphs are identifiable without re-deriving it. When a graph-theoretic test returns a uniform extreme across every input, check what the cut object is before reporting the result. open UW-C198
    AL-269 2026-08-10 Q-3 skeleton-free generation (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product An unaided model builds structurally sound story graphs, and fails only the rules nobody gave it. Six authors with no skeleton, no example story and no validator in the loop produced 6 of 6 graphs with zero dangling targets, unreachable nodes, sinks or trapped cycles, at 27 to 35 nodes. All six were then blocked by the project gate, and every blocking finding violates a constraint absent from the brief: branch-depth budget (4 of 6), first-decision floor (2 of 6), ending-object schema (2 of 6). The brief stated the structural rules and the model met all of them. State the band budgets, the opening floor and the ending schema in any generation brief, then re-run to test whether the gap closes; the current result cannot distinguish model incapacity from an incomplete brief, and the brief is the cheaper thing to fix first. open UW-C199
    AL-270 2026-08-10 Q-3 convergence, read against D-6 product Removing the shared plan entirely does not vary the premise, because the model converges there unaided. Six stories sharing no plan sit at the idiom floor on average (3.5 per 1000 against a floor of 3.3), which is the cleanest evidence that D-2 and D-6's convergence came from the shared contract rather than from the model. But 4 of 15 pairs breach the 4.0 budget, and the worst pairs are premise twins: two coastal lost-signal mysteries, two woodland camp discoveries, and all six are 'children find a thing left by an older person and follow clues to it'. D-6 identified premise as the largest traceable leak channel and concluded a reusable plan must vary it per book; Q-3 shows sharing less does not achieve that. Vary the premise with something that actively repels, not by withholding a shared plan and not by instruction. This is the concrete requirement R1-3's repulsion term should be pointed at, alongside the bound solution chain. open UW-C200
    AL-271 2026-08-10 M-4 contract authoring, first attempt (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) process Instructing an author to write independently produces the surface markers of independence and not the substance. A contract briefed with wording-independence as a hard, itemised experimental constraint came back structurally excellent (26 nodes, 52 facts, zero fact-closure violations under an independent reimplementation) with a different world, a different slug and zero fact-name overlap, and at 126.7 shared 4-grams per 1000 with its reference: beat_hint 260.3, world_recipe+safety_envelope 127.5, choice_semantics 96.2. For scale, D-6's worst fill condition was 17.2 (restated 2026-08-11 from 16.9, per the per-body-unit recount noted on AL-267) and the generator floor is 3.3. This is D-6's diverge condition one layer up and far worse: at fill time the same instruction cut traceable grams 45 percent, at contract-authoring time it achieved essentially nothing. The checkable markers were all satisfied while the property was not. Enforce independence by what the author is not shown, not by instruction: supply the format as a written schema and withhold the reference artifact. Note the consequence for R1-3, whose promotion rested on generating a fresh contract per book: fresh-per-book is not independent-per-book. open UW-C201
    AL-272 2026-08-10 M-4 contract authoring, controlled comparison (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product Independence comes from what an author is not shown, not from what it is told. Same task, same shell, same requirement, one variable: with the reference contract visible plus an itemised instruction to diverge from it, a fresh contract shares 126.7 4-grams per 1000 with that reference; with the reference withheld and the format supplied as a written schema instead, 1.0. A 127-fold reduction. Both artifacts are structurally sound on the same independent checks. Instructing divergence is close to useless at the plan-authoring layer and is the intervention every proposal reaches for first. But the premise converged anyway: the withheld-reference author independently chose a clock tower against the reference's clocktower, so withholding closes the wording channel completely and the premise channel not at all (AL-270 a third time). Generate each book's decisional stratum from the structural stratum alone, never from a sibling book, and treat that as the implementable form of AL-258's third repair. Name it explicitly in the architecture re-specification and in R1-3. Handle the premise with a separate repulsion mechanism, since withholding provably does not touch it. open UW-C202
    AL-273 2026-08-10 M-4 confound check (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product Cross-book convergence does not scale with plan similarity; the threshold is sentence identity. Checking a new contract's similarity to the base before using it as an arm turned up that the pilot's two contracts are 118.4 shared 4-grams per 1000, almost exactly as similar as an attempt discarded as unusable at 126.7, and their fills sat at the floor, 2.9. They share vocabulary heavily while sharing 0 of 35 choice_semantics strings. Two authors handed the same sentence converge on it; two handed different sentences sharing vocabulary do not, even at 118 per 1000. This refutes the proportional reading of AL-258, which was mine, and makes the repair far cheaper: a per-book decisional stratum needs only to be separately written, not independent of its siblings. Limit: the pilot's contracts also differ in premise, so sentence-difference and premise-difference are bundled in the one available comparison. Amend the AL-258 and AL-272 guidance to require separate generation rather than independence, and run the disambiguating test: two contracts sharing a premise but not a sentence, filled and measured. That is the cheapest open question in this line. open UW-C203
    AL-274 2026-08-10 M-4 guard battery, scripts/check_fill_integrity.py validator Every shell in this programme now defers the book title, and the fill-integrity checker fails on that by default. Since AL-257, where a shell id leaked one title into three arms, shells carry <<FILL book_title>>, so a filled title necessarily differs from its shell. check_fill_integrity.py counts the top-level title as non-fillable unless --allow-title-rewrite is passed, and reports FAIL structure: filled story differs from skeleton outside node bodies and choice labels (ids, choices, targets, endings, variables, or metadata), which reads like a serious structural defect and is not one. Verified across D-2 arm P, three D-6 fills and the M-4 arm: all fail without the flag, all pass with it, and an independent graph-level comparison confirms the title is the only difference every time. The flag exists for exactly this case per AL-211; the trap is that its default became wrong once title deferral became standard. Teach the checker to treat any field the shell wrote as a <<FILL ...>> directive as fillable, which removes the flag and cannot drift as more fields are deferred. Until then name the flag in the guard-battery runbook. applied scripts/check_fill_integrity.py
    AL-275 2026-08-10 M-4 rating round 1 (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) process A treatment arm's label_style encoded the treatment, making the book identifiable from its labels alone. The stake-economics contract offered name the cost before the reward among its label_styles; the author picked it and all 35 labels began with the word "Spend", against comparison books using neutral styles (terse imperatives, first-person plural resolves). The first blind rater named it unprompted as "the single most distinctive authorial signature among the three texts" and cited it in the forced comparison, so its verdict cannot separate priced-failure-in-the-fiction from a label template. This is AL-245 in a new place: contamination entering through a field nobody was watching, here one I introduced by letting the treatment contract author its own label styles. Hold label_style constant across arms, or draw it from a shared neutral pool, and never let a treatment contract supply style options that name the treatment. Add a first-word-concentration check to the guard battery: no more than about a sixth of labels sharing an opening word. applied scripts/check_label_template.py
    AL-276 2026-08-10 M-4 rating round 1, blinding procedure process Blinding renamed the files and left the provenance inside them. The two books from the older shells carry "id": "sk_clocktower_cipher" and the new arm carries "id": "d6", and the second blind rater found it unaided and called it "the single most concrete signal in the whole set", explicitly noting it traces two of the three books to one shared origin object. This is AL-257 a second time (a shell id leaking, there into titles, here into a rating) and it biases the comparison in the direction of the observed result. Blinding must normalise every provenance-bearing field, not just the filename: id, metadata, version, and anything else that is not prose the reader would see. Write it as a reusable blinding step rather than doing it by hand per round, since it has now failed twice. applied scripts/blind_books.py
    AL-277 2026-08-10 M-4 rating round 1, rater finding on filled_D product A choice label promises one thing and its destination depicts another, in an artifact used as a control in three rating rounds. The option reads "Call the risk not worth it", which in the other two books resolves as declining the crossing; in this book the text has the character attempt it and slip ("Sam's foot went out from under him on the second plank... Idris's hand closed hard on his sleeve"). A child choosing the cautious option gets a near-fall anyway. Found by a blind rater, not by any guard, and it has survived every battery this book has been through. Add a label-to-destination consistency check to the review surface, at minimum for the decline/retreat family where the mismatch is most legible. Note that this is a model-judgement check, not a lexical one, per the Q-5 and AL-261 pattern. applied scripts/build_prose_review_worklist.py
    AL-278 2026-08-10 M-4 rating round 1, rater finding on filled_costly validator Fact-graph closure can hold in the contract and be violated by the prose, and nothing checks that direction. The contract passed a closure walk under two independent implementations, yet the merge node's prose reads "Priya reads the first lever's knot, matches it to the pattern from the loft... Dez does the second, checking it against the ledger's margin notes", naming clues from two of the four rooms when a reader visits exactly one. check_fill_fidelity.py asks whether a node delivered its obligations; nothing asks whether a node assumed more than its entry_state guarantees. This is the mirror image of Q-5's logic_earned finding and is invisible to every guard in the battery. Add an over-assumption check at merge nodes: a model pass asking whether the prose references any fact the node's entry_state does not guarantee. Merge nodes are few (three in this graph) so the cost is bounded, and they are exactly where the error is structurally likely. applied scripts/build_prose_review_worklist.py
    AL-279 2026-08-10 M-4 rating round 2, rater finding traced to the contracts validator A choice promises an object, and the fact representing it survives only on the branch that declines it. At the crossing fork, c_pendulum_oil reads "cross with care and claim the maker's set-aside reward" and its destination carries only the puzzle facts, dropping reward_glimpsed entirely; c_pendulum_giveup ("decline it") is the branch whose destination does carry it. The claiming branch has no fact representing possession, so no author can write the payoff, and none did. A blind rater found the resulting hole in all three books unprompted: "the label promises an object; the text simply drops it", quoting all three. The pattern reproduces in contract_v2, contract_v3 and contract_costly, three independently authored contracts, one of which was written without sight of the others, so it is an error the graph shape invites rather than one author's slip. It is invisible to fact-graph closure, which only forbids assuming too much and treats dropping a fact as always safe, and invisible to check_branch_obligations.py, which computes what a branch owes rather than what it silently drops. Add an asymmetric-drop check at forks: a fact established at a fork and carried by one branch but not another is a candidate defect, and one whose dropping branch's choice_semantics name that fact's subject is a confirmed one. Cheap, deterministic, and it catches a class three guard batteries missed. applied scripts/check_promise_discharge.py
    AL-280 2026-08-10 M-4 rounds 1 and 2 (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product A rating effect that two blind raters agreed on disappeared entirely once two contaminations were removed. Round 1: both raters, opposite orders, ranked the free-failure control pair more decision-repetitive, Q6 gap one point. The arm carried a label template (35 of 35 labels opening "Spend") and a provenance leak (id shared by two of three books), both found and cited by the raters themselves. Round 2, same books with a neutral label style and tool-based blinding: raters split, both call it close, Q6 ties at 5,5, and M-4's own falsifier fires. The caveated version of round 1 would have been reported as a positive with a footnote. Note a residual handicap that runs the other way: M-4's "same goal" requirement forces the treatment arm to share the base's premise engine while the control does not, so the null may understate the effect. Treat agreement between blind raters as necessary and not sufficient; a contaminated round can produce unanimity. Keep AL-241's rebuild-rather-than-caveat rule and cite this as the case that justifies it. Where a design requires holding a variable constant, check whether that constant is itself a similarity channel before reading a null. open UW-C210
    AL-281 2026-08-10 Instrument audit across three rating rounds (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) process One item of the six-question instrument has never varied, and the only item that ever carried a result has now saturated too. Across the three rounds with recorded per-question scores, twelve cells each: Q4 (sequence repeats) is 5 in 12 of 12 and separated the pairs in 0 of 3 rounds; Q3 never leaves a two-point band at the bottom; and Q6 (solution transfer), which carried every earlier result, tied at 5,5 in the one uncontaminated round. Two raters recommended retiring Q4 unprompted after the D-5 round and the recommendation was recorded and never acted on. The consequence is concrete: D-1, which proposes three more arms rated on this graph with this instrument, would spend three contracts and three fills to produce a null that is an instrument artifact rather than a finding. Drop Q4 from the scored instrument and keep it as a description of the condition. Do not schedule another rating round on this graph until either the graph varies its central puzzle structurally between arms, which is why Q6 saturates, or a discriminating measure exists that is not at ceiling. Audit instrument ceilings from accumulated cells before commissioning a round, which costs nothing and would have saved this one. open UW-C211
    AL-282 2026-08-11 D-7 and D-7b (docs/planning/diversity-test-register.md) product A plan can be shared across books without them converging, but the prose the shared half carries has to be the right kind. This row originally read "no prose at all"; AL-284 measured the passing arm and found 473 words of free text still in it, so read that row before acting on this one. D-7 shared a stratum of topology, obligations, fact names and 32 one-line fact glosses, generating everything else per book: 13.6 shared 4-grams per 1000 against a budget of 4.0, exactly where D-6's diverge landed. D-7b removed the glosses and changed nothing else, verified byte-identical on every other key: 2.3, under budget and below the 3.3 generator floor. 422 words of prose in the shared artifact was the difference between 13.6 and 2.3. Two corrections, both 2026-08-11. This row first read 12.9 and 3.2, the label-inclusive pair; the body-only scope the programme standardised on gives 13.6 and 2.3, and the effect is unchanged (see AL-284). It also asserted "62 percent of shared grams tracing to the glosses"; that figure is retracted in the research brief, which re-traces it strictly as 5 of 40, or 12.5 percent, and withdraws rather than repairs it because the original method was never recorded. The retraction does not touch the deletion's effect, which is what this lesson rests on: the glosses were still the only thing that differed, and the mechanism the re-trace supports is convergent elaboration rather than copying. The stratification proposed in the architecture re-specification is therefore sound and its contents were wrong: I classified prose glosses as structure. Define the shareable stratum by exclusion rather than enumeration: it may contain identifiers, relations and enumerated categories. Do not state the exclusion as "no free text of any kind"; AL-284 measured 473 words of free text in the arm that passed, so that form of the rule describes no artifact we have built. Scope it to prose attached to the fact vocabulary the nodes reference, which is what the deletion removed; prose instructing the binding process was present in both arms and is not implicated at this volume. Keep the exclusion form, because enumerating prose fields has now missed some twice (constraints and mechanisms in AL-265's follow-up, then facts). Amend the architecture re-specification's section 2 table accordingly. open UW-C212
    AL-283 2026-08-11 D-7b fact readings product Bare fact names bind two independent authors to the same obligation without a gloss. The worry was that stripping definitions would make the shared plan too vague to be a plan. Measured: two authors given only names, node function and their own binding wrote 0 of 32 identical reading sentences and 0 of 35 identical choice semantics, chose different engines, and agreed in meaning on every fact sampled (logic_earned as "one real, usable piece of the tide arithmetic needed to set the dial" against "one working piece of the peal-cipher's logic, enough to actually attempt a setting"). A name plus a node function plus a binding is a sufficient specification. Drop fact glosses from the shared stratum as standard, and require each book's plan to record its own fact_readings, which makes interpretation drift measurable per book instead of assumed away. open UW-C213
    AL-284 2026-08-11 Second external review, question on device categories, checked against the D-7b artifact process We published a rule describing an artifact we had not measured, and the artifact contradicts it. D-7b was reported as sharing a plan with "no free text at all". Measured directly: the shared kernel still carries 473 words of free text (world_recipe binding notes, per-node invention notes, eight title_contract.must_not clauses, the affect ceiling), which is more than the 422 words the experiment deleted (895 to 473). The measured result is unaffected and still holds at the corrected body-only scope, 13.6 to 2.3, but the stated mechanism cannot be right: "no free text at all" is not what the passing arm implements. The reviewer reached the same objection from the document alone, by reasoning that device categories carry no prose yet still steer the puzzle; the artifact was worse than their inference. Note this also weakens AL-282, whose figures are the superseded mixed-scope pair and whose "no free text of any kind" rule this corrects. State the rule as: free text attached to the fact vocabulary nodes reference drove convergence; free text instructing the binding process did not, at this volume. Whether the operative variable is what the text describes or how often it is re-read is open and settled by a third arm that deletes the 473 and keeps the 422. Standing process change: before publishing any claim of the form "the shared artifact contains no X", assert it programmatically against the artifact rather than against the build script's intent. open UW-C214
    AL-285 2026-08-11 Second external review, question 1 on rater provenance process The brief calls model raters "human". Section 14 reads "a deterministic decision-overlap score on top of blind human annotation". Every rater, annotator and "blind reader of the finished books" in Parts I and II was an LLM agent instance; no human and no child has read any book in this programme for rating purposes, and the reported Fleiss kappas (0.96, 1.00) are inter-model agreement. Part I's methods appendix says "a rater agent" correctly, so the document contradicts itself, and every other use of "rater", "annotator" and "reader" is unqualified and therefore ambiguous. An external reviewer had to ask which it was before they could weight any result, which is the cost. Correct section 14, and add one provenance statement covering every rated result in both parts, stating that rater verdicts are hypotheses about reader response rather than reader evidence. Adopt as a standing rule: name the rater's nature at every site where a verdict is reported, never once in an appendix. open UW-C215
    AL-286 2026-08-11 Fourth external review, A1.1 attack on 16l, run rather than argued product The 16l pair passes every lexical gate and sits at the top of our observed range on shared cognitive operation. A reviewer objected that 16l measures verbatim overlap while the defect is decision repetition, and that the pair had never been measured for the second. Run on the existing artifacts, so the cost was zero generations: solution transfer over the shared chain gives answer 0.167 (passes the tier-1 gate), operation 0.500, solution 0.467. Correction, same day: my first reading of this was wrong and the known-bad battery caught it. The operation tier is not monotone with badness, because the tiers are exclusive and the strongest wins: a prop matching by answer never counts as an operation match, so a literally identical binding scores operation 0.000. Ranking must use the composite. On the composite solution_transfer, scored against a battery built for this purpose, the ordering is: identical binding 1.000, same-chain-different-dressing 1.000, the known-contaminated pair 1.000, relocated chain 0.700, the 16l pair 0.467, most distinct real pair 0.225. So the 16l pair is mid-range, not the worst we hold: four of its six chain props transfer at some tier, which is materially short of clean and well short of catastrophic. Separately, on aligned choice positions in the two filled books: zero identical labels and 11 of 35 sharing their first content word, several of them the same act with a swapped noun ("Turn Back Together" against "Turn back now"; "Stay and Read" against "Stay and read the logs"). Caveat that must travel with this: the operation tier is advisory and was not the tier that reproduced rater orderings in D-4, only tier 1 was, and n is 6 chain props on one contract. Stop reporting 16l as a distinctness result. It is a convergence result, and the first cheap test of the property 1.3 actually defines comes back unfavourable. Add a decisional sibling to the exclusion rule: sharing a structural kernel must also schedule the reasoning kind per fork, not merely leave it to the binding. Validate the operation tier against a constructed known-bad battery before it is allowed to gate anything, and never quote 0.500 as a gate result. open UW-C216

A skeleton is structurally valid by construction, so the gate certifies it and the outcome is status='passed', error=None, with the input handed back as the output. That totality is the tell that a seed fallback rather than a partial write produced the artifact, but it does not rule out truncation upstream: a completion cut off mid-JSON does not parse at all, so it yields current_doc = None and therefore a perfectly empty book by exactly this path. A fill that never produced a parseable document must terminate as failed, whatever the gate later says about the fallback artifact, because the gate is being asked about a document the model never wrote. Do not seed a repair loop with the unfilled input: repairing a skeleton toward validity is a no-op that consumes the budget and ends in a false pass; seed from the last document the model actually produced, or refuse to enter the loop. The error is one-directional and worst exactly where retries are most likely, because a starved reasoning model burns the full cap and delivers nothing.
