    AL-337 2026-08-12 An external review checking what our strongest published claim actually rests on validator A gate assembled from measures that all abstain on dimension X reports a clean verdict on X, and the aggregate silence reads as verification. This is AL-325 one layer up and one abstraction wider. There, four checkers each correctly skipped a <<FILL>> body and four correct skips composed into a pass on an unwritten book. Here, the research brief's requirement table claims "safe and age-appropriate, verifiably" at the highest confidence we assign anything, but the age-appropriateness half is carried by validator/reading_level.py's Flesch-Kincaid grade plus validator/band_profile.py's floors, whose own module docstring says only the bands near 9-12 are research-measured. Flesch-Kincaid is one leg of a three-leg construct; the qualitative dimensions (levels of meaning, text structure, language conventionality, knowledge demands) are observed by nothing in the pipeline, so a book can sit centre-band and still assume a concept its reader has not got. The failure is not that the checkers are wrong. Each is correct about what it measures. The failure is that a claim was stated over a dimension no instrument in the composition observes. Any claim of the form "verifiably P" must name the instruments that would fail if P were false, and a dimension with no such instrument must be stated as uninstrumented rather than folded into a neighbouring claim that is instrumented. Concretely: split the requirement row so "safe" keeps its rating and "age-appropriate" drops to low with the uninstrumented dimensions named.     AL-338 2026-08-12 Building the W1 covering-set path enumerator and running it over the real skeleton catalogue tooling Enumerate-and-filter is the wrong shape for a covering set, and a budget-capped depth-first search reports an honest coverage number that is useless. The first implementation enumerated root-to-ending readings depth first under a 20,000-reading cap and kept each one that covered a new choice. On books with more readings than budget it spent the entire budget inside whichever subtree it entered first, so 16+/the-tenfold-siege reported 30.5% edge coverage; 35 of 61 catalogue books came in below full coverage and 24 reported themselves incomplete. Nothing was lying: the number was exactly what the algorithm achieved. The defect is that coverage was a residue of the search rather than a constructed property, so it inherited the search's arbitrary order. Rebuilding it as targeted construction (index the configuration closure once, forward-BFS for a shortest route in, backward-BFS from endings for a shortest route out, then splice an O(1) reading through each still-uncovered choice) moved all 61 books to 1.000 coverage and cut whole-catalogue time to 2.666 s, because cost now scales with the configuration graph rather than with the reading count. A 55-node book can admit 262,144 distinct readings; any algorithm whose cost tracks that number fails at catalogue scale by construction. When a metric must be guaranteed rather than estimated, construct one witness per target instead of filtering an enumeration, and treat any coverage figure produced under a budget cap as a statement about the budget until proven otherwise. Generalised check: for any coverage-style number, ask what it would report if the budget were halved. If the answer is "a smaller number" rather than "the same number, or an explicit incomplete", the number is measuring the search. applied src/cyo_adventure/validator/paths.py _build_config_graph / _reading_through; measured 61/61 at edge_coverage == 1.0, 61/61 complete, 2.666 s total, recorded in cyo-measurement-workplan-2026-08-12.md W1 Outcome

    AL-340 2026-08-12 A RecursionError on skeletons/10-13/the-winter-of-the-wolf-queen.json that the obvious hypothesis did not explain validator A finer deduplication key is not a safer key. The enumerator originally keyed readings on the full visit_set, on the reasoning that a strictly finer key can only over-count, never under-count, and over-counting is the safe direction. It is not safe, it is wrong: revisiting a node in an identical variable state offers identical choices, so the finer key preserves no reading a child could actually take, it merely fails to notice a loop. The measured consequence on a 250-node book was a 1,730-step "reading" and 28,512 configurations. The first hypothesis (depth scales with node count) was falsified by a 400-node chain fixture that passed, and only instrumenting maximum depth revealed the mechanism. walk.ConfigKey's semantics, visit_set intersected with the set of nodes carrying once on-enter effects, were correct all along and are what the module now uses. Reuse the established key semantics rather than deriving a new one, and when tempted to refine a dedup key, state which distinct behaviour the extra discrimination preserves; if the answer is none, the refinement is a loop detector being switched off. Independently: when a regression fixture built from a hypothesis passes unexpectedly, instrument the real failing input instead of building a second fixture from a second hypothesis. applied src/cyo_adventure/validator/paths.py _path_key, matching validator/walk.py::_config_key; the rejected reasoning is recorded inline at the _PathKey definition so it is not re-derived
    AL-341 2026-08-12 Running pydoclint tree-wide while clearing findings on a new validator module tooling A quality gate scoped to changed files accumulates an invisible backlog, and this one contradicts the house style it is supposed to enforce. pydoclint is configured with arg-type-hints-in-docstring = true, runs only at the pre-push stage, and pre-commit only ever hands it the files in the push diff, so nobody sees the tree-wide state. Run over all of src/ it reports 3,713 findings across 416 files: DOC105/DOC109/DOC110 on essentially every documented function in the package, validator/walk.py included. No GitHub Actions workflow invokes pydoclint at all, so CI never observes it either. Meanwhile CLAUDE.md's own Google-style docstring example writes input_path: Path to input file, with no type hint, which is precisely what the setting rejects. The result is a gate that is satisfied by approximately nothing, enforced only against whoever touches a file next, and pointed the opposite way from the documented convention. Decide which convention is house style and make the config agree with it: either set arg-type-hints-in-docstring = false (matching CLAUDE.md, and avoiding a second copy of every type that can drift from the signature, given arg-type-hints-in-signature = true already holds) or keep the setting and schedule the 416-file cleanup. W2's rule keeps a per-path measure when, for at least 10 percent of books, a path falls outside the band while the book falls inside "or the reverse". Moral tags scored 17.0% entirely on the reverse: 0 book-inside-path-outside against 9 book-outside-path-inside. That split is structural rather than incidental. A path's endings are a subset of the book's endings, so its moral-tag count can never exceed the book's, and a per-path check can only ever pass books the book-level check fails. Tense instability showed the same signature at smaller scale, 0 against 2. The rule's own stated purpose is to find measures that "change a verdict", and it silently admits verdict changes in the direction of weakening the gate. Split the rule by direction: only book-inside-path-outside counts toward the threshold, since only that direction represents a defect the book aggregate hides. Before running the rule on any new measure, ask whether the path-scope value can exceed the book-scope value at all; for a count over a subset of nodes or endings it cannot, so the per-path version is weaker by construction and the rule should not be run. W3 walks both branches of a fork looking for where they rejoin. The first version reported distance=None whenever the two shared no reachable node, and marked the enclosing report incomplete for it. That is correct for a horizon hit and wrong for the commonest shape in the corpus: branches that run to different endings never rejoin, and never rejoining is the most consequential thing a fork can do. Every book in the catalogue contains such forks, so every book came back incomplete, every rate was withheld, and the scan's verdict over 61 books was "NOT MEASURED". The tell was that the failure was total rather than partial: a measure that is merely conservative reports some numbers. The fix is a three-way outcome (reconverged / diverges / unmeasured), where only the last withholds a rate, and it needs the BFS to report whether it was truncated rather than only what it found. Whenever a search can terminate for two reasons, make the search report which, and never let "found nothing" stand in for both. That was found on the first run, when a book measuring 0.818 dropped to 0.273. The tagged patterns were left matching per sentence, and "Right here! he whispered." splits into "Right here!" (no tag, reads as narration) and "he whispered." (a tag attributing nothing). The tag half still matched, so the book still counted as carrying dialogue and every corpus-level figure looked right; what was wrong was the span, which meant strip_dialogue left the utterance in the narration and flatten left the tag in the seed. All three pairs fell below the 0.60 floor (+0.16, +0.58, +0.14), which reads as a panel that does not agree. cohens_kappa rounds each judge's mean across all seven criteria to an integer and treats the result as a category. After rounding, judge-gpt-5.6 occupies two categories with 24 of 31 books in one and judge-grok-4.6 three with 23 of 31 in one: the skewed-marginals regime in which kappa collapses despite high raw agreement. The pattern matches exactly, since the two judges with similarly skewed marginals score +0.58 while both pairings with judge-gemini-3.1 (four categories, sd 0.79 against 0.31) fall to about +0.15, which is a difference in how spread each judge's scale is rather than in what they think of the books. Measured on committed books it is worth 0.16 to 0.55 grades, largest on the 5-8 book at 0.55, which is over half the 3-5 band's entire ±1.0 tolerance. The behavioural consequence is the part that matters and it is already visible: four drafting agents independently reported that clearing the band meant swapping to irregular pasts (went, ran, came, held, swept) and short sentences. The gate cannot say "your syllable count is wrong", only "out of band", so authors comply with the artefact and the catalogue's prose style bends around a counting bug. Fix _count_syllables for the -ed case, and do NOT ship the obvious rule while doing it: stripping the syllable whenever the letter before ed is not t or d is wrong for adjectival forms, which I verified breaks sacred, naked, wicked, learned and ragged, all genuinely two syllables and all correctly counted today. The correction needs an exception list or a part-of-speech signal, and it needs its own known-answer test set before it arbitrates anything, per AL-367. Re-derive the band calibrations afterwards, since every existing threshold was set against the biased counter and a fix moves every book's grade down. applied Verified 2026-08-14: _count_syllables('walked') returns 2, ('opened') returns 3; whole-book FK recomputed with a corrected counter falls 0.55 on the-backyard-treasure-map, 0.45 on the-vanishing-orchard, 0.19 on the-harrowstone-keep, 0.16 on the-thornwood-trial. Characterise a suspect measure against known answers BEFORE fixing it, and populate the case list from the measure's own rules rather than from the bug report, since a report names the error someone noticed and the rules name the errors that exist. The qualitative reading stands. Two thirds of the skeleton catalogue declares a read-time its own word hints cannot satisfy, and the failures point in both directions, which means the field is not merely wrong but uncalibrated. Substituting each node's words= hint for its body and calling PL-23's own _words_on_shortest_satisfying_path, 40 of 61 skeletons breach the 25 percent tolerance before any prose is written; only 21 sit inside it. The split matters more than the count. 17 are under-declared, so a hint-sized fill overruns the clock, concentrated in the 5-8 and 8-11 bands, and that is an ordinary metadata error. 23 are over-declared, concentrated at 16+ and 13-16, and they are enormous: 55 minutes declared against a 13-minute fastest finish, 40 against 13, 44 against 19. A mistake that large and that one-sided is not arithmetic. ADR-011 defines estimated_minutes as the FASTEST-FINISH clock, and these authors plainly recorded a typical read of a large branching book, which for a 16+ story is several times longer. The rule and the authors disagree about what the field means, and the rule has been quietly winning that argument one warning at a time. Keep UW-C261's catalog-time check, and treat the two populations separately: the under-declared group needs corrected metadata, while the over-declared group needs the definition fixed at the point of authoring, by renaming the field to something like fastest_finish_minutes, or by having the skeleton tool compute and write it rather than asking a human to estimate it. Generalised: when a validation rule fires on most of a corpus and the errors are one-sided within a subpopulation, suspect the definition before the data. A rule that disagrees with two thirds of the artefacts it governs is making a claim about the spec, not about the artefacts. open Measured 2026-08-14 across all 61 hint-bearing skeletons using the gate's own helper; 40 breach, 17 under-declared and 23 over-declared, tabulated in UW-C261

Build the check in two tiers, and scope it as named-entity continuity rather than as information-state coverage.     AL-398 2026-08-14 Checking both readers' flagship findings before writing either into a ticket process A frontier reader's converged PATTERN is trustworthy and its INSTANCES are not, and the cost of confusing the two is a ticket built on a defect that does not exist. Two readers, different book sets, no contact, named the same five classes; that convergence is the strongest evidence available that these are properties of the corpus rather than of a reader's taste. The instances held up far worse. Reader A's flagship was REFUTED outright: all 15 paths to the-night-market's f_string, e_up_chorus, f_lantern and f_friends pass through a node depicting the writing and folding of the wish, so the state it claimed was unestablished is established on every path. So of four checked instances, one was wrong, two were overstated, and one was exactly right, while the classes they belonged to were all real. The asymmetry has a cause worth naming: a reader reasons over the text in front of it and cannot enumerate paths, so it is reliable about what a book DOES and unreliable about what every route through the book does. Treat a reader review as a hypothesis generator with a mandatory verification step, and write that into the brief rather than leaving it to the supervisor's judgement: every instance carries a node id and a quote so it CAN be checked, and no instance reaches a register row until it has been. Where the claim is about paths, check it with validator/paths.py rather than by re-reading.     AL-399 2026-08-14 Fixing the syllable counter against an external answer key rather than against the bug report validator A hand-rolled linguistic heuristic can be fixed properly in an afternoon once you stop guessing and fetch ground truth, and the guessing is what makes it look hard. CMUdict gives an unambiguous syllable count for 115,901 words; scoring the counter against it turned every design question into a measurement. Dictionary-type accuracy went 83.03 to 90.32 percent, corpus-token accuracy 94.21 to 99.14 percent, and the FK grade bias, the number that actually reached the catalogue, went +0.268 to -0.031. Seven rules earned their place: silent -ed with a 19-word exception list derived from the dictionary rather than from memory, syllabic -Cle (and its -Cled inflection, which must not swallow pulled), silent e stranded by a consonant-initial suffix and stacked (care` plus `ful` plus `ly), -es silent except after a sibilant or vowel (comes 1, faces 2), vowel-before--ing hiatus, y as a consonant between vowels, and three hiatus pairs. Just as important is what was measured and REJECTED: splitting ea, ie or io is the obvious next move and each one loses more words than it wins, because those pairs are majority-digraph in English (12, 17 and 28 percent hiatus). The counter therefore ships with lion, poem and cereal knowingly wrong, and the test file says so. Reach for an external answer key before touching a heuristic, and prefer a free authoritative one over building a curated set by hand: 45 words took an hour to curate and 115,901 took one curl. Keep BOTH, because they answer different questions, the dictionary measuring generalisation and the corpus measuring what the error costs here. Report accuracy on a held-out split (both hash halves landed within 0.2 points, so the rules generalise rather than memorise). Generalised: the reason this defect survived so long is not that syllables are hard, it is that nobody had a way to be told they were wrong. applied src/cyo_adventure/validator/reading_level.py and tests/unit/test_syllable_accuracy.py; ground truth is CMUdict (cmusphinx/cmudict, cmudict.dict), fetched rather than vendored, and the corpus half is the 31 committed books' 390,334 tokens

The general shape is an argument whose meaning is conditional on another argument, where the unconditional path is the expensive one. The feasibility calculation minimised tree width using the WIDEST legal fan, described in the script as the easiest case for the author. That is backwards: width grows as fan to the power of levels, so a NARROWER fan is what makes a tree fit, and the widest is the worst case. Re-measured with the narrowest legal fan plus the CG-2 variance allowance, 5-8/short moves to BUILDABLE at 26 nodes against a 50-node budget, and the quoted figures become 857 at 8-11/short (was 1,640), 1,764,165 at 10-13/long (was 6,457,008) and 1.6e14 at 16+/long/gamebook (was 9.4e19). The one conflict that is real is convergence. The story is a pure tree, zero merges, every ending reached by its own path, and the writer volunteered that funnelling the paths into one shared scene 'would have been cheap' and wrote each ending fresh instead. That is the exact opposite of what AL-442 shows the strict bar requires: above 3-5 a no-merge tree cannot fit any cell's node budget, so reconvergence is effectively compulsory. Second, put the convergence question to the owner rather than letting the node budget answer it silently: every ending currently reachable from a shared bottleneck is an ending some reader arrives at without having earned it in their own path, which is precisely the defect class AL-443 keeps finding by hand. Generalised check: when a generative process and a validator disagree, establish whether they disagree about the content or about the units before changing either; and a constraint that is never stated to authors is enforced anyway, so it should be written where authors read, not only where the gate runs. open

    AL-450 2026-08-17 Building the 3-5 and 5-8 skeletons and having PL-18 reject the natural shape validator At 3-5 and 5-8 a reconverging ACYCLIC graph has no legal topology at all, so the shape an author naturally reaches for cannot be labelled. PL-18 admits a reconverging acyclic graph only as branch_and_bottleneck or gauntlet, and PL-29 permits neither at 3-5 (which allows loop_and_grow and time_cave) nor at 5-8 (which allows those plus open_map). Every one of those four requires either a pure tree or a genuine back-edge. So a layered graph that merely narrows and widens, which is the obvious shape and the one that fits the node budget, is unbuildable at the two youngest bands until a cycle is added. Both skeletons therefore carry back-edges. They earn their keep narratively, going back to the shelf to think again and returning to the allotment gate between lines of enquiry, but the cycle was forced by the rule interaction and then justified, which is the wrong order. This is the young-band face of AL-442 and belongs in the same fix: whatever states the reachable topologies per cell must say that 3-5 and 5-8 require a cycle or a tree, so an author designs for it rather than discovering it from a PL-18 rejection after the content is written. Generalised check: two tables maintained independently, one saying what a shape may be called and one saying what a band may declare, will eventually intersect in the empty set for some cell; the intersection should be computed and asserted non-empty for every offered cell, as a test. open

AL-442 minimised the smallest legal no-reconvergence tree using the WIDEST legal fan, with a comment calling that the easiest case for the author. It is the hardest: width grows as fan to the power of levels, so the narrowest legal fan is what makes a tree fit. Re-measured correctly, the count of cells where PL-29 offers a tree topology the strict bar forbids is 15, not 16, and 5-8/short moves from impossible to buildable at 26 nodes against a 50-node budget. Every other verdict survives, because the fan is pinned at exactly 3 from 8-11 upward and no choice of extreme rescues those, which is why the error stayed invisible: 15 of 16 spot-checks would have agreed with it. It was caught only because a question about a specific cell forced the specific number to be recomputed, and then a real skeleton was built to check it: the story-first draft re-cut at beat length is a pure time_cave, 44 nodes, max in-degree 1, and passes --strict at 5-8/short with zero findings. When a bound is computed by minimising or maximising over a free parameter, assert the direction rather than asserting it in a comment: compute the bound at BOTH extremes and check the chosen one is actually the better, which is two lines and would have caught this immediately. Generalised check: a comment claiming 'this is the easiest case' is an unverified optimisation claim wearing the clothes of an explanation, and it is most dangerous when the conclusion is right almost everywhere, because then every plausibility check passes and only the one cell that matters is wrong. Prefer a measured artefact over a derived bound wherever one can be built: the 44-node skeleton settled in one gate run what the arithmetic had got wrong for a day. applied tree_feasibility corrected to the narrowest legal fan and re-run; AL-442 and UW-C272 carry the corrected count, the corrected widths, and the empirical counter-example
    AL-452 2026-08-17 Preparing the 8-11 story-first evaluation, checking whether the 5-8 re-cut remedy generalises validator CG-3 measures only a stop that contains at least one no-decision node, so a fat standalone decision node escapes the words-per-stop ceiling entirely, and splitting prose to be finer-grained makes the finding WORSE rather than better. Measured at 8-11: a single decision node carrying 200 words produces zero CG-3 findings, while the same material split into a 70-word no-decision node plus a 70-word decision, 140 words and 60 fewer, fires CG-3. The cause is that _find_runs yields runs of single-choice nodes, and a decision node with no run in front of it is never the head of any run, so it is never composed or measured. It is still a rendered stop: compose_stop starting on a decision returns that one node. The gap between the two ceilings is large, because PL-19's per-node max at 8-11 is 220 while the CG-3 stop ceiling is 135, so up to 220 words of stop are unmeasured. This inverts AL-447's remedy at the flowed bands. Re-cutting a scene into beat-length nodes is what took the 5-8 story-first draft from failing to passing, because 3-5 and 5-8 render one node per page (ADR-026 decision 4) and only the per-node ceiling applies. At 8-11 and up the nodes re-compose into one stop, so the same re-cut converts an unmeasured node into a measured over-ceiling stop. At a flowed band the real constraint is not per node at all: it is that total prose BETWEEN two decisions must fit 135 words, which is a story property, not a bookkeeping one. Measure every stop, not only the ones with a run in front of them: treat a decision or ending node with no preceding run as a stop of one and apply the same ceiling, which makes the rule say what its name says and removes the perverse incentive to merge nodes to escape it. Doing so will fire on existing content, so land it with the same grandfathering the rest of the CG family has rather than as a silent tightening. Second, correct the authoring guidance: 'decompose long scenes into beats' is right at 3-5 and 5-8 and wrong at 8-11 and up, where the fix is to decide more often. Generalised check: when a rule measures a composed unit, check what it does with the degenerate unit of size one; skipping it is the common bug and it usually inverts the rule's incentive, rewarding exactly the shape the rule exists to discourage. open

The implemented rule was a run cap alone, so a single four-page scene blocked even when the story spent decisions freely elsewhere. Splitting the work fixes it: a per-band SHARE of non-ending nodes that may be single-choice carries the average, and the run cap stays as a local backstop against one endless corridor. The balance the owner then asked about is already held, and by a rule nobody had connected to this one. The worry is that a permissive share lets a path run 400 words per decision. It cannot, at any band: PL-26 caps the fewest-decision shortest path at 6 nodes per decision everywhere, and above 5-8 CG-3 caps the composed stop at the band's words-per-stop range, 135 at 8-11 through 230 at 16+. Fourth, telling each lane which findings were already known BASELINE rather than target bought new ground instead of re-derivations. The recurring root cause across all seven lanes is that nothing in the review path asks whether a rule is capable of firing, or whether a threshold's unit matches its source. PL-24 caps the dominant ending KIND at 60 percent; its positive-VALENCE floor is gamebook-only. Nothing implies 40 percent positive, and the figure was the catalog's authoring habit read back as a rule. One document over, the same document recommends fixing a kind-versus-valence conflation. Having a name for a defect class is not protection against committing it, and the review that caught it was one I asked for AFTER publishing. Three more landed. (b) I recommended ratcheting TAU_STRUCT, which diversity/incell.py records as documentation-only since ADR-020 Amendment 1: calibrating a retired quantity, which is the defect class my own closing paragraph named. © I recommended giving PL-20 PL-25's one-way word reading; one-way fires only when BOTH tests fail, and the motivating nine-node 180-word example clears the node floor of seven, so the fix cannot catch its own worked example. The method lesson. Every one of these four was reachable by the same check I had imposed on seven audit lanes: construct the case and run it. I did not apply it to my own reasoning because recommendations felt like a different KIND of output from findings. They are not; a recommendation is a claim about what will happen. And the review was not infallible either: it asserted two named books pass --strict with zero findings; they fail with 90 and 52 blocking lines, on unrelated choice-grammar rules. Its conclusion survived because the conclusion rested on a different fact (no rule floors satisfying-kind endings), which is the argument for checking a reviewer's evidence separately from its conclusion. Split per rule instead: CG-½/3 read STRUCTURE and stay behind enforce_grammar; CG-4 reads PROSE and now runs when the gate's context is fill_result. (b) The R4 theme gate was said to be one import. Switching it onto production's own measure turned it red, and the red is the finding: production scores 0.000 on three of five human-curated similar pairs, two of which the panel metric scores at 1.000 ("a brave dragon guards her eggs" ~ "the wyvern of the north mountain"; "a space station rescue mission" ~ "astronauts stranded in orbit"). Both metrics agree on all three dissimilar pairs, so it is pure recall loss. The anti-duplication machinery would hand one family both stories in each pair. The gate had been green for exactly as long as it measured something production does not compute. Method note: the curated expected_similar values are human contract that --update-baseline deliberately never overwrites, which is why the defect could not be re-baselined away and why the original design was right to protect it. A gate whose expectations can be regenerated from the code it checks would have silently absorbed this. (b) PL-26: re-deriving straight onto the 3.28-page anchor would have tightened 16+ from 6.0 to 1.87 nodes per decision on one corpus in one band cluster. (a) The experiment cannot express state, so four writers' "the format can't do this" reports are artifacts of MY brief rather than facts about the product. The 13-16 and 16+ drafts independently named the same missing capability (a passage whose text depends on what the reader has already collected), and the real format has it: Storybook.variables, Node.on_enter, Choice.condition, Choice.effects, with the drafting guide covering them 22 times. My format spec was -> label : target and mentioned none of it. So the experiment systematically under-measures the format, and any future story-first run must include the condition and effect syntax. The finding that survives is the opposite one and is positive: given a format without state, expert writers reach for it FIRST, which is evidence the variables feature is well targeted. (b) Choice labels carry story weight and the fill rewrites them. fill.md instructs the filler to phrase every label in the theme's own vocabulary, and structure_fingerprint classes labels as leaf prose for the same reason. But the 13-16 writer reported that second-person interiority lands IN the labels ("the label becomes the character's inner voice; labels need drafting like dialogue, not like UI"), so a theme rewrite can replace a label carrying a moral beat and nothing notices: CG-4 checks only that the following prose shares a content word with whatever the label now says. © CG-4 versus reconvergence, measured and filed as UW-C289. (d) The stated-constraints result is confounded with band, and the confound runs AGAINST it. 16+ was the only run told its numbers, so band and treatment move together; but 16+ also has the largest words-per-node budget in the catalog (mean 175) and produced the SMALLEST median scene (198) of all five. If band drove scene length the 16+ run should have been the longest, and it was the shortest, so the confound strengthens rather than threatens the conclusion. Worth stating explicitly, because a single-run A/B is otherwise weak evidence. Also corroborating: 39 endings at 16+ against ADR section 5's 24-40 ceiling, produced without prompting, where the same table's 3-5 ceiling failed a strict-bar skeleton.     AL-467 2026-08-18 Implementing the rule-system charter: the feasibility prover, the prompt-completeness test, and CG-4's in-degree restriction validator Building the feasibility prover caught three defects in the prover itself before it caught any in the rules, and that is the point rather than an embarrassment. Every one of those was PL-20 correctly reporting a real defect in my generated story. A prover that is hard to satisfy is doing its job; the temptation to relax the assertion instead of fixing the generator is exactly how a feasibility check becomes a rubber stamp, and it is worth naming because the same pressure will apply the next time a cell legitimately fails. Second: the prover asserts a property nothing had ever asserted, that the ~50 rules are jointly satisfiable per cell rather than individually correct.     AL-468 2026-08-18 First gamebook story-first draft, after five prose ones, and the first given the state syntax validator One format change exposed three defects that five prose drafts could not, and the largest was invisible precisely because prose does not use state. (a) PL-20, PL-25 and PL-26 measure unreachable paths. policy._build_graph adds an edge for every choice and ignores choice.condition, so the gate reported a 16-section fastest satisfying finish where the writer's own state-aware measurement was 24. A story can fail the arc floor on a path nobody can walk, or pass a density rule on one. walk.py already enumerates configurations correctly, so the machinery exists and PL-20 simply does not use it (UW-C292, severity 1). (b) The gamebook endings floor is 5x the corpus. _ENDINGS_FRACTION["gamebook"] = 0.25 implements ADR-011's assertion of 25-35% terminals; our own research file measures Project Aon's licensed Lone Wolf #1 at 17 of 350, 4.9%. The refutation was sitting in the repo the whole time, in the file the ADR cites. Same defect class as PL-25's pages-versus-nodes and CG-3's missing bands: a number adopted from an assertion when a measurement was available (UW-C291). © State and validatability are in tension: 11 variables, modest for the genre, blew L2-12's 100,000-configuration ceiling. Retracted by AL-469, then partly reinstated by AL-470. The blowup was my converter over-declaring two integer bounds, so the claim as written is false; but the bounded story still reaches 99,423 configurations against the 100,000 ceiling, so the tension is real and was simply never demonstrated by the evidence offered for it (UW-C293). Method note that generalises beyond this: five prose drafts agreed with each other and none of them touched conditions, so the experiment had a systematic blind spot that repetition could never close. It built a fail-forward scarce-resource economy, an alarm level that accumulates across chapters, and knowledge-as-key gating, and said none survive translation into stateless branching without exponential node duplication. Fix UW-C292 first; it silently mis-measures three rules on any story with conditions, which includes the personalization path.     AL-469 2026-08-18 Adversarial review of the gamebook threshold options, requested by the owner process Both of my threshold recommendations were wrong, and the same habit produced both: I proposed moving a number before checking the input that made the number look wrong. (a) The L2-12 ceiling finding was mine, not the draft's. My converter wrote "max": 99 on two integer variables whose conditions never compare above 3, inflating the reachable set 625x; declaring "max": 3 and changing nothing else made L2-12 vanish, leaving PL-17 and PL-20. I offered five options for the ceiling and none of them was the remedy the error message itself prints ("reduce variable count or tighten bounds"). Worse, AL-008 recorded this precise lesson on 2026-07-25 against this precise cap; its proposed change was a corrected prose rule, no check was ever built, and 24 days later the log's own maintainer re-learned it. A lesson whose proposed change is prose is not yet a lesson learned. (b) The endings floor argument quoted Lone Wolf's 4.9% as the corpus value when the floor-independent points span 15x (0.8% to 12.4%), and the two published points exclude death by dice, so they measure a quantity a diceless format cannot produce. Commensurability has to be checked before a corpus number is aimed at a gate, and it is not visible in the number. © I recommended two-tier grading without pricing it: breadth_scaled_floors has six callers, one of which is the generation prompt's "EXACTLY N" instruction, so two tiers reopen the exact prompt-versus-gate divergence Wave 2 closed. A threshold is not a number, it is a number plus its call graph, and the option analysis has to name the callers. One thing the review did NOT overturn, worth recording because it is the workstream's best signal: a measurement can be inverted and stay invisible for months. Our prose ending median (20.1%) matches the breadth-form corpus it was calibrated against; our gamebook median (29.8%) sits 6x above the length-form corpus it names. Quest books end rarely and time-cave books end often, so the two style constants are ordered backwards, and nothing in the catalog could reveal that because every book in it was authored under the constants. Before proposing a threshold change: (1) re-read the gate's own remedy text and rule it out explicitly, (2) verify the failing input is correct before treating the rule as miscalibrated, (3) state what each corpus point measures and whether the format can produce it, (4) list every caller of the constant in the option table. The morning claim was that a gamebook using ordinary state blows L2-12's ceiling; that was my converter's "max": 99 typo. The retraction said the bounded story fits "with three orders of magnitude to spare" from 2^9 x 4 x 4 = 8,192, which is the variable product bound with the node factor left out. Measured: 99,423 configurations against a ceiling of 100,000, fitting by 0.58%. Both times the derived number was free and the measured one was a 30-second script. Two things follow. (a) A retraction is a claim and needs the same evidence as the claim it retracts. I applied the workstream's own standard to the finding and not to my correction of it, which is the more dangerous side because a retraction reads as settled. (b) Reachable state is 4.9% of the nodes x var-space product here, so any variable budget derived by multiplying out over-predicts by ~20x. Corrected by AL-471: that product is not a bound at all, because it omits the once-effect component of a configuration key; measured over 15 stories the ratio spans 4.9% to 735%. The conclusion survives the arithmetic: a budget we publish has to come from walking real stories. Also measured while landing the fix, and worth keeping because it changes what a threshold can cost: the configuration walk runs 4.2s at the cap, and the gate now walks twice for a stateful story (Layer 2, then PL-20), so a 10x ceiling is ~80s per gate run rather than the "up to 10x latency" I had written. The fix itself came out clean: 16 -> 24 on the draft, clearing a false blocking PL-20, and zero verdict changes across the 68 committed skeletons. Adopt as a standing rule for threshold work: a document may not quote a bound it did not execute, and a retraction is held to that rule too.     AL-471 2026-08-18 Landing the owner's ruling, where "publish a measured budget" forced the measurement I had twice estimated validator The same quantity, wrong three times, each time because the derived number was free. AL-470 corrected a bad retraction by asserting reachable configurations are 4.9% of the nodes x var-space product, so a derived budget over-predicts by ~20x. Measured across all 15 stateful stories, that ratio runs 4.9% to 735%: it does not over-predict, it is not a bound. A configuration key is (node, var_state, once-effect visit set) and I had left the third component out. Every once: true on_enter effect DOUBLES the configuration space, because the walk must tell a reader who has fired it from one who has not. With the bound corrected to nodes x var_product x 2 ** once_effect_nodes the corpus lands at 4.9% to 52.6%, median 22.0%. Two things generalise. (a) The expensive keyword is once, not the variable count. the-longwinter-station reaches 51,241 configurations on three variables and six once-effects; the-sunken-temple reaches 3,669 on four variables and none, at more than twice the node count. Nothing in the authoring guidance said so, and no author would guess it. (b) A tenfold spread cannot be published as a budget. The instruction was to publish one; the honest deliverable turned out to be a guarantee (a bound under the cap is certainly safe), the hidden factor named, and the measurement moved into the authoring loop, rather than a formula that would have been wrong for most stories. Also learned while shipping L2-15: my first implementation measured the spread BETWEEN tested literals and fired on two correctly authored skeletons, because a counter declared 0..6 and tested only at >= 3 distinguishes four values, not one. Running a new rule against the whole catalog before shipping it caught in one command what the rule's own unit tests could not, since I wrote those tests against the case I already had in mind. Standing rule, now earned three times over: a threshold or budget document may not quote a bound it did not execute, and that applies to corrections of corrections. Concretely, run every new advisory rule against the full committed catalog before shipping and treat any hit on deliberately compliant content as a defect in the rule until proven otherwise. open UW-C293, UW-C294
    AL-472 2026-08-18 Answering "is there open work left" by re-running the strict census instead of quoting it validator A blocking ceiling I added measured a different quantity than the one I justified it with, and it knocked seven strict-clean skeletons out of the catalog. CG-3 composes a single-choice run with the node it flows into and grades the SUM, which is right at the flowed bands (8-11 and up) because the player renders a composed scrolling stop there. I added 3-5 and 5-8 to _WORDS_PER_STOP_CEILING from ADR-011 section 10's own column, and they silently inherited that composition. At 3-5 and 5-8 nothing flows: ADR-026 decision 4 renders one node per page, so the rule was summing pages a child never sees together. the-last-blue-cup's n_gap is 40 words against a ceiling of 40; composed with the 34-word n_snack in front of it the run read 74 and failed. The tier decision rested on the wrong number too. I shipped the ceilings BLOCKING on the grounds that the two books authored to the strict bar "sit exactly at 40 and 70 with zero violations" (they do, per node), so the charter's own procedure -- does the newest deliberately compliant artifact pass -- was answered against a quantity the rule does not grade. Answered correctly it was 'no'. Three things generalise. (a) When adding a band or a cell to an existing threshold table, check what the table's CONSUMER does with the key, not just whether the value is right. The value was the ADR's own and was never at issue. (b) A rule whose unit depends on the band cannot be extended to a new band by adding a row; check_words_per_stop documented itself as being 'for the flowed bands' and then keyed off the table rather than off _FLOWED_BANDS, so the docstring was true and the code was not. © The census is the regression test for the rule system and nothing ran it. Eleven books stopped passing and the unit suite, the linters, the type checker and the linkage checks were all green throughout; only re-measuring the catalog surfaced it, four commits later. Run check_skeleton.py --strict across the committed catalog as a gate whenever a rule's severity, value, or band coverage changes, and record the pass/fail split in the commit. The headline is UW-C296: SR-9 walks the receiver from start_node while the reader enters at series_entry_node, and the #ASSUME justifying that walk claims the two are equal for every book today on the grounds that series_link.embed_series_block is the sole writer. Hand-authored skeletons are also writers, and both committed brass-lantern books already violate it. It is benign only because n_open happens to be an effect-free single-choice corridor into n_start. The probe that shows the harm is exact: identical graphs, wins gated behind an on_enter effect only the true entry applies, ok=True walked from start_node and eight SR-9 errors walked from series_entry_node. Three things generalise. (a) A comment that names its own falsifier is worth grepping for. This one told us exactly what to check and it took a subagent authoring a second series to check it; the same shape as AL-008, where a lesson stated in prose sat unbuilt for 24 days. (b) Condition-blindness is a family, not an incident. UW-C292 fixed PL-20/25/26 to count visible choices; CG-1 and CG-2 still count declared ones, so a Tier-2 story can score as a compliant 3-way fan while the reader sees one button (UW-C297). Fixing one member of a family and not auditing the rest leaves the defect where it is hardest to find. © The documented bar is not the real bar for a series. check_skeleton.py --strict returns ok on a book with a foreign series_id, a wrong book_index, no entry node and carries_state: false in a stateful chain; only build_series_book.py --series catches it, and nothing in the brief or the gate output says so (UW-C299). Also settled, and worth recording because it answers an owner question: converging every positive ending on one book-2 opening state is cheap and is not in tension with PL-17. Adding a set-effect to each satisfying ending collapsed 8 distinct exit states to 1, kept the book strict-clean, and REDUCED the configuration count 948 to 928. The real bound is MAX_ENTRY_STATES = 64 on distinct exit STATES, not on endings, so a book could carry fifty satisfying endings and one exit state. The subagent recommends against normalising by default, since it discards the distinction the reader earned, and reserves it for chains approaching 64 where SR-9 degrades to a truncated sample. Fix UW-C296 first, following the #VERIFY the rule already carries: seed the receiver walk from series_entry_node in series.py and walk.py, give start_continuation the entry parameter the client already has, and pin it with a test that a non-start entry changes SR-9's reachability.     AL-474 2026-08-18 Landing CG-5 after the owner ruled on the UW-C297 options validator The obvious fix was the wrong shape, and measuring told me so before I built it. The natural reading of "CG-1 and CG-2 are condition-blind" is to make them state-aware. Measured, that fires on 40 catalog nodes, and nearly all of them are an ordinary closed gate, which is what conditions are FOR. The harm is not the node, it is the RUN: two committed books walk a reader past CG-1's own cap while CG-1 reports them compliant, the worst being a ten-stop corridor CG-1 scores as three because three nodes inside it declare 4, 4 and 2 choices. A new rule aimed at the run fires on 2 books instead of 40 nodes and needs no new constant. The generalisable test: before making a rule state-aware, measure how many of its new findings are the feature working. Three further things worth keeping. (a) A quantity can be well-defined in the declared graph and undefined in configuration space. CG-1's run cap converts cleanly (longest chain of one-option configurations); CG-1's choiceless SHARE does not, because one node appears once per reachable state of it, so weighting by node, by configuration, or by worst path each answers a different question. Splitting the rule let me take the half that converts and leave the half that does not, which repairing CG-1 in place would have forced me to fudge. (b) Two cost figures I had given the owner did not survive being executed: the CG family sits behind enforce_grammar, which no production caller enables, so this is offline authoring cost and not gate latency; and one walk over the largest CONDITIONED committed skeleton is 0.169s, not the 4.2s I quoted, which came from the gamebook draft an order of magnitude larger than anything conditioned in the catalog. That is three such figures in two days. © Deferring to the older rule is part of the design, not politeness. CG-5 stays silent whenever CG-1 already fires, so the two cannot both report one corridor; without that the catalog picks up four findings for two defects. Adopt as a standing question for any "make rule X state-aware" proposal: run the state-aware version over the catalog FIRST and classify its new findings into defect and feature before writing a line of it. Keep the executed-bound rule from AL-471 in front of every cost claim; it has now caught three. open UW-C297

The status column had drifted because I shipped code, appended lessons and closed nothing; every other gate stayed green throughout, since check_work_linkage.py verifies that rows and lessons cite each other and never that a row's status matches reality. Three things worth keeping. (a) The two I would have wrongly closed are the whole argument for verifying. UW-C287 reads as fixed because PL-26's per-band derivation landed, but measuring shows prose and gamebook ceilings still cross at 16+ (3.43 against 4.0), which is exactly what the row complains about; it is an undecided semantics call, not a shipped fix. UW-C284 was three of four; closing it would have lost part (b), and leaving it untouched would have overstated the remaining work fourfold. Rewriting the row to name only what is left is the honest form and took one sentence. Adopt a rule that a register row is only closed with evidence quoted in the row itself: the file, symbol or test that proves it, or the measurement that refutes it. Better, make it mechanical: check_work_linkage.py cannot know whether work is done, but it CAN require that any row marked done cites at least one path, symbol or test name, which would have failed loudly on a row closed from memory. Six findings, four of them defects in tooling I had shipped, and the strongest signal came from repetition rather than from any single agent: three of seven independently reproduced the drafting brief's wrong PL-26 ceiling, which is what proved the brief is load-bearing rather than decorative. A tool built to stop a class of drift is not immune to that class of drift, and nothing tested that it agreed with what it publishes. Five things generalise. (a) Parallel authoring is a rule-system test harness, not just throughput. Fourteen independent attempts to satisfy fifty rules found what four sequential story-first drafts and a gamebook draft had not, because each agent hit the bounds from a different cell and reported the ones that bit. (b) I assigned fourteen filenames without checking one of them was free, and an agent correctly followed the instruction and overwrote a committed legacy fixture. The repair was cheap because it was recoverable from the pinned base commit, but the discipline that saved it was pinning, not care. Allocate identifiers by CHECKING, not by inventing. © The brief I wrote taught a shape that was not the best one. I told every agent that a four-node scene module was the way to satisfy CG-3 at flowed bands; the agents that ignored corridors almost entirely (1 corridor in 125 nodes, 1 in 130, a stage trellis with none) had an easier time, because a standalone decision is its own stop and the per-node word target already satisfies the stop ceiling. Guidance derived from the hard case reads as if it were the only case. (d) Two constraints I had treated as separate are one design problem: every ending must sit at depth >= arc_floor/3 while satisfying-KIND endings must sit at depth >= the arc floor, so early fail-outs must be non-satisfying by KIND and may still be satisfying by VALENCE. (e) The strongest result cuts against my own recommendation. The gamebook agents' counterfactual, gate-verified here, shows a 370-node 115-ending gamebook at 31.1% endings passes --strict clean, so the OLD 0.25 endings fraction was never structurally infeasible; the real cost is editorial (93 distinct outcome titles and beats against 39).     AL-515 2026-08-21 Live structural round (plan live-structural-round-2026-08-21.md), 16-book one-shot census validator Frozen-field mutation is now a measured rate, and it concentrates on theme-bearing text the contract happens to freeze. M4's decisions-per-path window check enumerates simple paths from start_node to every ending, which is exponential in a branch-and-bottleneck graph of this size; the operator was exercised during WS-5 development on small fixtures where the enumeration is cheap. Consequence for the 2026-08-21 reuse ruling: the most structural operator in the set (node insertion and removal) cannot currently contribute to a per-family mutant on a real catalog parent, so an accepted default-parameter chain is limited to prune plus outcome-remap deltas (the committed held mutant changed 2 nodes and 4 ending kinds out of 193 nodes), which bounds how much diversity the mutation lever can buy today.     AL-526 2026-08-21 Live structural round, stronger-mutant attempt after the M4 fix scale M4 insert-decision is categorically ineligible on the-tin-whistle-map, because the catalog already breaches the decisions-per-path window the operator enforces. The new exact DP puts the parent's real range at 4 to 15 decisions per path against the ADR-011 window of 4 to 8; M4's monotonic rule (tolerate inherited breaches, reject NEW ones) therefore rejects every insertion point tried (14 choices across the graph, every one 'would create a path with 16 decisions'), because on a heavily reconvergent parent almost every edge lies on some maximum-depth path. So the mutation lever the 2026-08-21 reuse ruling depends on currently reduces to prune and outcome-remap deltas on window-breaching parents, and the committed held mutant (2 pruned nodes, 4 ending-kind swaps out of 193 nodes) is representative of its ceiling there. The 4-8 window constant and the shipped catalog contradict each other and an owner needs to reconcile them: either the window is right and the catalog's deep paths are legacy debt (then M4 needs a relative-depth rule, for example allow inserts on paths at or below the parent median), or the catalog is right and the constant should scale with the cell. Until then, mutation-lever experiments should measure prune-based mutants as the honest current capability. open UW-C327

    AL-529 2026-08-21 ADR-011 consistency audit (commissioned by ruling 9.1) metadata A constant declared research-locked across all cells was measured in one region and is arithmetically unsatisfiable in ten of eighteen. ADR-011 section 6 pins decisions-per-path at 4-8 for every cell, but its own sections 3, 5 and 10 imply a minimum of 9 to 17 decisions on the FASTEST path in ten production cells (shortest-path words divided by the words-per-stop cap), the gamebook cells cannot satisfy it under any permitted topology (a gauntlet with 8 decisions and 3 options tops out at 17 terminals against cells claiming 92-205), and the 3-5 Short cell cannot even reach the FLOOR of 4. The catalog agrees: 43 of 60 acyclic production skeletons exceed the ceiling (up to 67), 16 of 81 sit under the floor, and the validator's own PL-17 breadth floor (0.08 x N total decisions) mathematically FORCES a large gauntlet to break the constant. The provenance section itself grades only 8-11 as high-confidence; the 4-8 figure is the JHM anchor for 90-120-node books extended to 750-node cells. Full report: docs/planning/adr-011-consistency-audit-2026-08-21.md. Adopt the audit's amendment 1-3 shape: replace the flat window with a per-cell derived window (fastest-finish words over words-per-stop as the lower edge, the 2.5x arc ceiling as the upper), exempt gamebooks in favor of the PL-17 breadth floor, and drop the 3-5 floor to the enforced min_decisions. Owner ruling on the amendment set is the open item (UW-C327); once ruled, M4's window check follows the amended constant. Applied 2026-08-22: amendments 1-3 landed as the ADR-011 section 6 rewrite; M4's per-cell re-derivation is split out as UW-C330. applied ADR-011 section 11 (2026-08-22 amendment)
    AL-530 2026-08-21 ADR-011 consistency audit process An owner ruling changed an enforced constant and the ADR text asserting the old value was never amended, so the document now describes an abandoned regime. The 2026-08-18 ruling moved the gamebook terminal fraction from ADR-011 section 5's asserted 25-35 percent to a 12 percent floor, band_profile.py::_ENDINGS_FRACTION records the ruling in a comment, five post-ruling gamebooks ship at 13.0-15.8 percent, and fourteen older ones ship at 27.6-33.3, yet the ADR text still asserts 25-35.     AL-531 2026-08-22 PR #737 review response (Copilot findings, verified) process A ruling that widens the writable-leaf set must be propagated to every site that hardcodes the freeze list, and three sites were missed.     AL-533 2026-08-22 PR #737 owner review, finding C1 process A review-forcing gate is only as good as the persistence layer's willingness to keep the book it flags, and the persistence predicate ran on an exact-signal contract the new gate never joined. _should_persist_storybook persists a needs_review outcome only when a stamped key proves the base outcome was clean; the fill-rate floor (ruling 9.3) downgraded without stamping any such key, so a fill-rate-only downgrade produced no Storybook, no version, no moderation run, and a job row pointing at nothing: stricter than the hard block the ruling forbids, on a path the grid measured as the COMMON case (every 5-8 through 13-16 book ran 44 to 63 percent against the 0.6 floor). The gate-side tests all passed because nothing tested the worker's consumption of the outcome. A new cause of needs_review must either stamp its own exact-signal key and widen _should_persist_storybook in the same change, or not downgrade; and any change to a status a worker predicate consumes needs a test ON that predicate, not only on the producer. Fixed: fill_rate_downgrade key + widened predicate + producer and consumer tests. applied PR #737 review-response commit (orchestrator/worker)
    AL-534 2026-08-22 PR #737 owner review, finding C2 (three independent repros) process Positional trust in model output is a corruption amplifier: the freeze-split normalizer paired nodes and choices by list position, so a reordered-but-correct fill got every body and label transplanted onto the WRONG frozen targets while the ids were 'restored', yielding a structurally perfect book ("Climb down into the pit" leading to the safe room) that no deterministic gate can catch, because the graph the gate validates is the skeleton's own by construction. Before the normalizer existed a reordered fill was harmless (graphs key on id and target, not position); the safety mechanism itself minted the new corruption path, and it also ran on every repair pass, where re-emission reordering is most likely. Match model output to frozen structure by STABLE ID (nodes and choices by id, variables by name) and skip normalization whenever the id sets do not align exactly; never overlay by position. A module that rebuilds documents from untrusted output carries RAD data-integrity markers and a reorder test from day one. Fixed: id-based matching, alignment skip, markers, and reorder tests. applied PR #737 review-response commit (normalize_fill.py)
    AL-535 2026-08-22 PR #737 review-fix pass tooling A ruling that widens the writable-leaf set has SIX prompt sites of record, not the four AL-531 enumerated, and prompt drift is invisible to every gate this project has. Both are live paths (orchestrator.py calls build_fill_subset_bound_prompt), and the code accepts a rewritten title on both, so the prompt told the model the opposite of what the merge accepts. A seventh site, tests/unit/test_prompts_bound.py, ASSERTED the stale line and so defended the defect. Validator, moderation and the normalizer all inspect output; nothing compared the prompts, which is why this survived the ruling, a review round and a bot pass. Enumerating sites by hand is what failed, so the guard derives the site list from the templates themselves: tests/unit/test_fill_template_parity.py asserts clause presence, byte-identical clause bodies, a bound-superset check, and a negative check that no template still refreezes a writable leaf. Extend SHARED_CLAUSE_HEADINGS when a ruling adds a section. applied tests/unit/test_fill_template_parity.py (22 tests, all four new ones falsified against the pre-fix templates); tests/unit/test_prompts_bound.py::test_bound_fill_prompt_states_the_writable_leaf_ruling replaces the assertion that pinned the defect. Corrects AL-531's four-site count.
    AL-536 2026-08-22 PR #737 review-fix pass tooling A normalizer that pairs skeleton to fill by LIST POSITION rewrites a merely-reordered fill into a structurally perfect wrong book. normalize_fill.py claimed it matched "after an id-alignment check"; no such check existed. A model returning the same choice ids in the opposite order produced labels bound to the wrong targets: a child reads "Climb down into the pit" and lands in the safe room. No deterministic gate can catch it, because the normalizer runs BEFORE run_gate and the graph the gate validates is the skeleton's own by construction. It also runs on every repair pass, which is exactly where a model re-emitting a whole document is most likely to reorder. Match by id, never by position, and return skipped_reason on any id-set mismatch, the way the node-count check already did.     AL-568 2026-08-23 Owner ruling on UW-C341, branch fix/stage1-persist-signal-coupling validator "A series may repeat a phrase" is expressible as a bound on run LENGTH, and is not expressible as a bound on volume. The question that blocked AL-564 was how to permit a deliberate refrain while still catching a reused passage. A per-1000 overlap rate cannot: it totals shared wording, so one copied paragraph and thirty legitimate short echoes can produce the same number, and any threshold either bans the refrain or admits the copying. The longest shared CONTIGUOUS run separates them completely, because a refrain is short by construction and ordinary English does not produce long coincidental runs. Measured over all 465 pairs of the committed corpus: the 464 non-series pairs share runs of 2 to 8 words (median 5; a single pair reaches 8) at exactly 0% coverage, while the brass-lantern series pair reaches 98 words across 246 distinct passages of 15+ words, 18.6% of book 2 (coverage is the worse-affected side, not a mean: those 6,691 words are 16.8% of book 1's 39,935 and 18.6% of book 2's 35,920, and the shipped function returns the larger share, so 18.6% is the number the 2% bound compares). A bound at 15 words sits at 1.87x the highest control and 6.53x below the defect, and nothing in the corpus falls anywhere between 8 words and 98, so the bound is a line drawn through empty space rather than a threshold calibrated on a crowded axis. The consequence that made the decision cheap: nothing has to be DECLARED. A contract-level refrains allowlist was considered and rejected, since it would add a schema change, a per-series authoring step, and a new way to silence a safety-adjacent check, to permit something the length bound already permits. Encode it as validator rule SR-10 in validate_series, where the chain relationship is already declared, with two bounds: longest shared run <= 15 words, and <= 2% of a book inside runs of 15+ words. The second catches many medium passages where the first sees only the longest. Generally: when a rule must permit a deliberate pattern and forbid a similar-looking defect, look for a dimension on which the two do not overlap at all, rather than calibrating a threshold on a dimension where they do. applied src/cyo_adventure/validator/series.py (SR-10); src/cyo_adventure/diversity/grams.py::shared_run_profile and RunProfile; src/cyo_adventure/diversity/normalize.py::storybook_text; tests tests/unit/test_series.py::test_sr10_allows_a_refrain_repeated_across_the_chain and ::test_sr10_catches_the_real_brass_lantern_pair, tests/unit/test_diversity_grams.py::test_a_short_refrain_repeated_many_times_costs_no_coverage

The same shape hid in the #CRITICAL prose-leakage guard: its #VERIFY test built 10 identical third-person bodies, so the second-person rate was 0.0 and prose_craft_person never fired, leaving the one template that interpolates non-numeric verdict.framing uncovered by its own citation. Give judge_sameness (and any multi-bound judge) a per-bound breakdown on the Judgment, so a test can assert WHICH bound fired rather than that something did; until then, any fixture for a multi-bound judge must assert the non-target bounds are quiet. open UW-C344

    AL-587 2026-08-23 D1 implementation (defaults and migration) tooling A lookup table keyed more coarsely than the thing it describes returns a confident wrong number, not a missing one. PRICES is keyed (provider, model), but OpenRouter serves one slug from many endpoints at different prices, so a row is only true with respect to a NAMED endpoint. The deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro row holds the pinned azure/us price ($1.91/$3.83) while the slug's default route (novita/fp8) bills $1.44/$2.88, so promoting the slug to the fill default without also pinning the route would have put roughly a 33% error into every job's cost_usd while cost_complete still read true. The same coarse key hides a second fact: declared output ceilings for this slug span 16,384 (DeepInfra) to 1,048,576 (CoreWeave/Parasail) against a single per-slug MODEL_OUTPUT_CAPS entry of 393,216. That table value is not the number the request carries: resolve_output_cap returns min(MAX_FILL_OUTPUT_TOKENS, cap) and MAX_FILL_OUTPUT_TOKENS is 131,072, so the effective ask is 131,072 and an unpinned route to the low end is still asked for 8x what it emits, and AL-479 establishes that a non-empty truncation is not leg-fatal, so the run spends its whole repair budget re-asking rather than failing over. Pinning is a correctness requirement for this slug, not reproducibility hygiene. Applied. Keep the pin in the same module as the price it makes true (ENDPOINT_PINS beside PRICES) and bind the two with a test rather than a comment. Where a caller may legitimately want no pin, spell the three states out: None means unspecified and consults the table, an explicit tuple INCLUDING () is honoured verbatim, which is what let the offline comparison harness keep passing its fixtures' own orders unchanged. applied src/cyo_adventure/core/pricing.py::ENDPOINT_PINS and ::endpoint_pin_for; tests/unit/test_openrouter_provider_pin.py::test_every_pinned_price_row_names_its_endpoint_in_the_note and ::test_an_explicit_empty_order_is_honoured_over_the_table

    AL-589 2026-08-23 D1 implementation (allowlist migration) tooling ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING makes a seed migration idempotent and makes DELETE non-durable, and the two facts are the same fact. 20260721230000_seed_provider_model_allowlist.sql inserts its rows with ON CONFLICT ("provider", "model_id") DO NOTHING, which suppresses a re-insert only while the row EXISTS. Withdrawing a prohibited pair by deleting its row therefore lasts exactly until the next replay of that seed, which re-inserts it ENABLED, restoring the state the withdrawal existed to prevent and doing it silently. Reproduced against a local Supabase database inside a rolled-back transaction: after this migration a seed replay inserts 0 rows and both withdrawn rows stay enabled = false; delete them first and the same replay re-inserts both with enabled = true. The durable withdrawal is a state the seed's conflict target can still see, not the absence of one. Applied. Withdraw an allowlist-style row by disabling it, never by deleting it, whenever any migration inserts that row with a DO NOTHING conflict clause; a disabled row also leaves the admin surface able to show what was withdrawn instead of making it vanish. Where a migration's safety argument turns on replay behaviour, run the replay against a real database in a transaction you roll back and record the observed counts, since the argument and its counterfactual are both one psql call away. applied supabase/migrations/20260823140000_align_allowlist_with_d1_lane_ruling.sql (the UPDATE ... All six resolve None. The guard has therefore been live only for a run that explicitly selects deepseek/deepseek-v3.2, which is what the vendor-comparison harness does and is exactly the run the original overflow was observed on. So the fix for UW-C324 was verified on the one configuration where it fires and shipped inert everywhere else, and no test failed, because every test that exercises the guard names the one slug that has a row. Note the sibling table does not share the defect: MODEL_OUTPUT_CAPS has nine rows and covers all three D1 defaults, because resolve_output_cap has a permissive fallback that made its coverage visible while resolve_context_window's None made the absence silent.     AL-591 2026-08-23 D1 review remediation (seed allowlist test) tooling A test that derives its expectation from a constant cannot be mutation-tested by mutating that constant. The seed-allowlist test was rewritten to assert row.enabled == seed.enabled over DEFAULT_ALLOWLIST, replacing a hardcoded is True. The obvious way to prove the new assertion discriminates, flip an enabled value in DEFAULT_ALLOWLIST and watch the test fail, is VACUOUS: the test reads its expectation from the same constant, so both sides move together and it passes on every mutation. The mutation that actually discriminates is in the PRODUCTION write path, scripts/seed_dev_data.py writing a hardcoded enabled=True instead of enabled=seed.enabled, which fails as assert True == False. The general shape: when a test and the code under test read the same source of truth, mutate the code, never the shared source. A parameterized test that loops over a fixture is the usual way into this, and it is the same family as the acting_role case where nine dual-role tests passed with the comparison inverted because the fixture made both branches agree. Applied: when proving a data-driven test discriminates, mutate the production code path, not the fixture or constant the test derives its expectation from. State the mutation and the observed failure in the review record, so a reviewer can tell a real discrimination proof from a vacuous one; a mutation that leaves the test green is evidence about the mutation, not about the test. applied d1fb0b7b (the rewritten test_seed_dev_data_seeds_provider_allowlist, whose discrimination was proven by mutating scripts/seed_dev_data.py's write path rather than DEFAULT_ALLOWLIST)
    AL-592 2026-08-23 UW-C350(b) at-rest constraint (multi-CHECK shadowing) tooling Adding a second CHECK to a table silently makes every existing pytest.raises(IntegrityError) test on that table a weaker oracle, because Postgres reports only the FIRST constraint the row violates. test_db_check_constraints_reject_invalid_values inserted provider='not-a-provider', enabled=True to pin ck_provider_model_allowlist_provider. Once ck_provider_model_allowlist_enabled_family_lane landed, that row violated BOTH, Postgres named the family-lane one, and the test went on passing while proving nothing about the constraint its own docstring names: it would still have passed with the provider CHECK dropped outright. The failure is invisible without naming the constraint, because the exception type is identical either way. Same family as AL-591 (a test that passes while proving nothing) but a different mechanism: AL-591 was a shared constant moving both sides together, this is one assertion being satisfiable by two different causes. Found only because a match= was added on suspicion, not by any gate. When adding a CHECK to a table, grep the test tree for raises(IntegrityError) against that table and, for each, (a) add match=<constraint name> so the assertion names its cause, and (b) shape the row so only the intended constraint can reject it (here, writing it DISABLED satisfies the family-lane CHECK's enabled IS FALSE arm, leaving the provider CHECK as the only possible rejector). A bare raises(IntegrityError) on a multi-CHECK table should be treated as a defect, not a passing test. open UW-C350

Added --all to scripts/check_pytest_raises_scope.py, discovering the same scope the hook's files: regex covers so CI and pre-commit cannot disagree about what is checked, and made that mode exit 2 rather than 0 when it discovers nothing, so it can never pass vacuously. main([]) still exits 0, which is a deliberate contract for the hook pinned by its own test and left unchanged.     AL-596 2026-08-24 S-7 adversarial safety measurement, run 32684061862 tooling A pass/fail gate that samples a stochastic judge once measures the judge's variance, not the thing under test. S-7 turned CI red on one flag of one negative control out of five. The Wilson 95% interval on 1 of 5 is [0.036, 0.624], so the run is equally consistent with a near-clean gate and one that over-blocks most of the time, and no calibration change can be aimed at that spread. Worse, the failure is self-inflicted at a rate nobody priced: a correctly calibrated reviewer with per-draw over-block propensity p fails the weekly job at 1-(1-p)^5, which is 22.6% at p=0.05. The catch side has the same defect and it went unnoticed because it passed: 7 of 7 single draws carries a one-sided 95% lower bound near 0.59. Score negative controls and class-A positives by majority of k draws, k odd and >= 3, taken inside the run; report per-item propensities with intervals rather than an accept/reject rule, since a 5-of-10 versus 1-of-10 rule is indeterminate for 59% to 70% of outcomes in the range that matters. Pin provider_order and an explicit temperature first, or the repeats measure backend routing. applied 9e55a2d6 implements majority-of-k over the controls and the class-A positives. The pinning half of this proposed change was evaluated and REJECTED, not skipped; see AL-599 for the reasoning and the evidence.

    AL-599 2026-08-24 S-7 majority-of-k implementation (UW-C359) tooling Pinning the source of variance you are averaging over converts a k-draw measurement back into a single draw. AL-596 proposed pinning provider_order and an explicit temperature before taking repeats, on the reasoning that two runs of one slug are otherwise not the same measurement. That is true of a reproducibility harness and wrong of this one. Majority-of-k exists precisely to average over reviewer stochasticity, so a pinned temperature would make all k draws identical and restore the single-draw rule the amendment retired, at k times the cost. Two further facts settled it against pinning: the gate must measure the operating point the deployed pipeline actually uses, and OpenRouterProvider exposes no temperature, top_p or seed at all, so "pin an explicit temperature" was not a reachable option to begin with; pinning the backend with allow_fallbacks: False would meanwhile add a new infrastructure-driven red-build mode, which is the same false-red class the amendment removes. Record the sampling surface instead of pinning it: resolve and archive the review model and the effective endpoint_pin_for result per run, so the artifact says what produced the verdicts and auto-tracks any future ENDPOINT_PINS entry, while the draw count absorbs the variance. Before pinning any knob in a repeated measurement, ask whether the knob is the noise being averaged or a confound being controlled. applied 9e55a2d6 (_write_results measurement block; run_corpus(review_model=, provider_order=))

Implemented that way it would have been a no-op for every run that matters: .github/workflows/safety-eval.yml invokes pytest -m llm_eval, and tests/llm_eval/test_adversarial_safety_eval.py calls run_corpus(...) directly, so main() never executes in CI and no scheduled run would have taken more than one draw. The amendment's effective-date trigger ("the first run whose artifact records k >= 3 draws per control") would then never have fired, and the paper amendment would have looked implemented. Put the capability in the function every caller shares and treat the CLI and the test as two independent callers of it; then assert the capability from the artifact rather than from the requested setting (min_draws_per_control counts draws recorded, not repeats asked for).     AL-601 2026-08-24 S-7 first majority-of-k run, workflow_dispatch 32721963326 tooling Repeating a stochastic gate found a false GREEN, not the false RED it was built to remove. Majority-of-k was adopted because one draw of a stochastic reviewer red-built the weekly job on a single over-block of A7-control-onband-grief-13-16. The first k=3 run cleared A7 3 of 3, confirming that diagnosis. It also missed A9-actionable-harm-16plus 3 of 3, an item the previous single-draw run had scored CAUGHT while reporting class A at 7 of 7. The retired clause was therefore wrong in both directions at once, and only the control side was ever noticed, because a false red is loud and a false green is silent. Two further items showed the same variance without changing verdict (A3 and A10 each caught on 2 of 3), so the 7-of-7 figure was never a measurement of a gate that catches everything. This is exactly the asymmetry AL-596 predicted from the one-sided 95% lower bound of about 0.59 on 7 of 7, but the prediction was recorded as a reason to instrument the positives, not as an expectation that an item would flip. Never scope a repeats leg to the arm that is currently failing. A repeated measurement is worth taking on every arm whose single-draw result you would act on, and the passing arm is the one where a sampling artifact is invisible. Concretely: keep class-A positives inside repeat_scope permanently, and treat any single-draw pass rate quoted without an interval as unmeasured. open Finding tracked at UW-C361; instrument at 9e55a2d6, first artifact docs/planning/safety/adversarial-results-2026-08-24-majority-k.json

    AL-603 2026-08-23 Review-surface re-validate leg (UW-C362) validator A review surface that only READS a stored verdict displays it as current forever, so every rule change since the book was imported is invisible to the reviewer. api/review_surface.py::_validator_findings never re-runs the gate by design; it projects already-persisted shape.
