    AL-605 2026-08-24 Production schema-drift recovery (UW-C363) tooling Every automated health signal stayed green while production 500'd on every authenticated adult request, because the readiness probe is a connectivity probe and nothing in the stack validates the schema. /api/v1/health/ready's database check opens a session and confirms the connection; it asserts nothing about columns. SQLAlchemy validates no mapping at import or at startup either, so a column present in db/models.py and absent from the live table is not an error until the first query that selects it, and it is then a 500 rather than a startup failure. Eighteen migrations sat unapplied behind that green probe. The concrete symptom was select(User) failing on user.consent_verification_id, which is on the path of every adult request, so the app was serving / and /api/v1/health/ready with 200 while doing nothing useful. A probe that returns 200 for a database the app cannot query is worse than no probe: it is an anti-oracle, and it was consulted and believed. Wanted: a schema-parity check that compares Base.metadata against information_schema.columns and fails loudly, either as a deep-health endpoint distinct from the liveness/readiness pair or as a startup assertion. The ad-hoc version used in the recovery is the specification: generate every (table, column) pair from Base.metadata.sorted_tables, and assert none is missing from the live catalog (31 tables, 304 columns, ran in one query). Decide startup-fail versus report-only first: a startup assertion turns drift into a refusal to boot, which is the right control for schema but would have taken the app down rather than degrading it. open
    AL-606 2026-08-24 Production schema-drift recovery (UW-C363) process App deploy and schema deploy are decoupled and nothing compares them, so the gap can only grow and only a human noticing closes it. The application image auto-deploys on merge to main; supabase-production.yml is workflow_dispatch only, gated by the production environment's required reviewer. Both halves are individually correct: schema changes to a children's-data database SHOULD need a human, and app deploys SHOULD be automatic. What is missing is the comparator. Code that requires a migration ships the moment it merges, the migration waits for someone to remember, and no check anywhere reports the difference. Eighteen migrations accumulated that way. Detection is cheap and was available the whole time: supabase migration list --linked against git ls-tree --name-only origin/main supabase/migrations/ is a set difference, and it is exactly what the recovery ran first. Wanted: run that set difference on a schedule against production and staging and open a ci-failure issue when it is non-empty, so a pending migration is announced rather than discovered. Two design points to settle before building it: the check needs a production DB credential in CI, which is the same credential gap AL-607 records, and a non-empty pending set is normal for the minutes between merge and dispatch, so the alert needs an age threshold rather than firing on any difference. Section 2.5 of the operations runbook now documents the manual form. open
    AL-607 2026-08-24 Production schema-drift recovery (UW-C363) process The runbook's own pre-flight restore-point step was not executable at the moment it was needed, and the obvious way to automate it would have been a data breach. Taking a dump before applying migrations is step 1 of the documented procedure. In practice the local checkout was supabase linked to staging, no operator held SUPABASE_DB_PASSWORD for production, and gh secret list --env backups returned nothing at all, which means supabase-backup.yml could not have produced an artifact on any night it has ever run. The tempting fix, adding a dump-and-upload step to the production migration workflow, is disqualified for a reason unrelated to backups: this repository is public, so GitHub workflow artifacts are readable by anyone with repo read access, and a supabase db dump is the entire production dataset including children's profile data. A documented control that cannot be executed is not a control, and the shortest path to making it executable was the wrong one. APPLIED to the runbook: section 2.5 now records the credential gap, states plainly that a restore point must land in access-controlled storage (the R2 backup bucket or Supabase managed backups) and never in CI artifact storage, and documents the substitute used when no dump is possible, scan the pending set for destructive verbs and snapshot exactly what they touch. On this apply that scan found every DROP to be a drop-then-recreate of a constraint, policy, or index and only three data-touching statements, none against child, family, story, or reading data, so a five-row provider_model_allowlist snapshot rendered as a replayable INSERT was proportionate. The general rule: a restore-point step must be rehearsed, because the first time you find out it does not run is the moment you need it. applied docs/operations/runbook.md
    AL-608 2026-08-24 In-review re-moderation widening (UW-C364) tooling A pytest.raises assertion is satisfied by ANY raise from ANY code path, so a guard test can pass with its guard deleted. The new status guard in scripts/remoderate_books.py::_resolve_book_id_targets was covered by a test that named a draft book and expected ResourceNotFoundError. Replacing the guard with if False: left the test GREEN: the fixture also had current_published_version=None, so the pre-existing pointer check raised the same exception type for an entirely unrelated reason. The test proved only that the function raises on that fixture, never that the status mattered. This is the same shape as the sibling defect where a fixture makes both branches agree, but reached through the exception TYPE rather than through the return value, so a reviewer reading the assertion sees nothing wrong. Fixed by giving every fixture a RESOLVABLE version (a live publish pointer and a live max(version)) so only the status can cause the raise, parametrizing over archived/needs_revision/draft, and adding match=. archived is the case that matters: an archived book keeps its publish pointer, so nothing but the status guard stops it being swept. Make match= mandatory on pytest.raises wherever the assertion is about WHICH guard fired rather than merely that the call failed, and add it to the mutation-proof checklist that a raise-assertion is the weakest oracle in the suite: mutate the guard, not just the happy path. A pytest.raises(X) with no match= in a module that can raise X from more than one place is a lint-able shape. open UW-C364
    AL-609 2026-08-24 In-review re-moderation widening (UW-C364) tooling Widening an endpoint's admitted statuses left every ops path to the new population unreachable, because each selector resolved a pointer only the OLD status has. api/remoderate.py accepted in_review books three commits before anything could name one: both selectors in scripts/remoderate_books.py resolve storybook.current_published_version, which is NULL for an in_review book, so --mock-moderated could not see one and --book-id raised a 404 on one. The capability was real and the reviewable path to it did not exist, which would have been discovered at the moment of running it against production. The pointer is the tell: a status-specific column (current_published_version) silently encodes a status assumption that no type and no test mentions. When widening an admission set, grep for the pointer column the old population used (current_published_version here) and treat every hit as a caller that cannot reach the new population until it is given a resolution rule. Prefer resolving 'the version under review' from ONE shared helper rather than restating max(version), which now appears in api/approval.py twice and scripts/remoderate_books.py twice. open UW-C364
    AL-610 2026-08-24 In-review re-moderation widening (UW-C364) tooling A two-flag mutual-exclusion guard written as an equality silently stops being one when a third flag lands. sweep() enforced 'exactly one selector' with if bool(book_ids) == mock_moderated: raise, which is a correct XOR for two flags and reads as intentional. Adding in_review made it accept --mock-moderated --in-review together and then run whichever branch the if/elif chain reached first, silently sweeping the wrong population. Argparse's mutually-exclusive group catches this at the CLI, so the defect is only reachable through the library entry point that tests and future callers use. Replaced with sum([...]) != 1, which stays correct at any arity. Write n-way exclusivity as a count from the start, never as an equality or a chain of pairwise checks: the equality form is correct exactly at n=2 and its failure at n=3 is silent and selects behaviour rather than erroring. Worth a grep for == applied between two booleans across the repo. open UW-C364
    AL-611 2026-08-24 ADR-023 catalog migration, scripts/promote_personalizable_slots.py tooling A three-field edit to every theme contract came out as 1,739 inserted lines, because json.dumps(..., indent=2) cannot preserve an author's inlined arrays. The catalog's sidecars inline short arrays ("forbid": ["weapon"]); Python's encoder always expands them. Ten contracts reformatted wholesale, worst case the-tide-pool-rescue at 389 insertions and 102 deletions for what is semantically three lines. Nothing in the repo formats skeletons/ (prettier is scoped to frontend/src, check-json is syntax-only), so the churn would have been permanent and no later pass would normalize it away. A reviewer cannot see a semantic change through that. Any tool that edits a catalog JSON sidecar in place must edit the bytes around the target, not re-serialize the document. The pattern that worked: locate the target with a regex, find its enclosing object with a string-aware brace scan so a brace inside a quoted value cannot move the span, splice the new properties in at the object's existing indent, then round-trip the result against the intended document before returning. Diff shape confirms it: 4 insertions and 1 deletion per contract, the 1 deletion being a line that only gained a trailing comma. applied ce3d9d9c, insert_promotion_fields plus tests/unit/test_promote_personalizable_slots.py::test_insert_promotion_fields_inline_array_preserves_surrounding_bytes
    AL-612 2026-08-24 ADR-023 catalog migration, mutation check on the promotion gate's tests tooling A test that reads its exclusion roster from the tool under test cannot notice the roster shrinking. test_main_excluded_slug_is_never_promoted iterated NOT_PERSONALIZABLE and asserted each entry was unpromoted on disk. Deleting an entry left the test GREEN, because the deleted slug simply stopped being iterated. The safety claim the test was cited for (a #CRITICAL tag: personalizing an animal protagonist renders a real child's name attached to a body they do not have) was therefore unguarded in the one direction that matters. Only test_main_check_mode_over_catalog_exits_zero caught the mutation, and only by luck of ordering: drop an exclusion AND re-run --apply and every gate goes green with the defect shipped. State the roster independently in the test rather than importing it, so adding or removing an entry is a deliberate two-file edit. More generally: when a test's subject is a policy LIST, iterating that list is a vacuity trap, and the test must pin the expected set. Prove it by mutation before believing it, which is how this was found. applied ce3d9d9c, _ANIMAL_PROTAGONIST_SLUGS in tests/unit/test_promote_personalizable_slots.py
    AL-613 2026-08-24 ADR-023 content retrofit, scripts/retrofit_personalization.py metadata No column records the theme binding a stored book was generated with, so any later transform that needs it has to guess from the contract and can be silently wrong. storybook_version carries skeleton_slug but nothing that says which binding was applied, and re-themed books exist: the-cave-of-echoes produced three books whose heroes are Theo and Priya rather than the contract's pinned name. Reinserting the contract's default_binding into such a book does not corrupt prose (it matches nothing), which is precisely the hazard: it would report 0% coverage and still stamp personalization_eligible, promising the reader a personalization that never resolves. The retrofit works around this by requiring the pinned value to be present in the stored blob, which is a precondition rather than a fix, and which permanently excludes those books from personalization because their real binding is unrecoverable. Persist the applied binding at generation time, alongside skeleton_slug and sentinel_manifest, so a later transform reads a fact instead of re-deriving an assumption. Until then, every consumer of default_binding against stored content must verify presence before acting, and no consumer may infer absence to mean "this book has no such slot". open Workaround at 72624fb1 (plan_retrofit precondition); tracked at UW-C370
    AL-614 2026-08-24 ADR-023 content retrofit, dry run over all 31 tracked fills in out/ process Personalization coverage is bimodal, so a mean describes no book in the corpus.     AL-615 2026-08-25 ADR-023 catalog promotion, PR #759 CI (test_skeleton_mutation_contract_gate_coverage.py) tooling A test that reaches into a catalog fixture by POSITION silently encodes an assumption about the catalog's shape, and a catalog-wide change invalidates it without touching the test.     AL-616 2026-08-25 ADR-023 personalization, PR #759 review round tooling An idempotence guard that normalizes only one side of the comparison asserts the opposite of what it means to. _assert_only_wrappers_added stripped sentinels from the retrofitted document but compared against the raw stored text, so re-running the sweep over an already-retrofitted book compared stripped text to wrapped text and raised.     AL-617 2026-08-25 ADR-023 personalization, PR #759 review round tooling A rollback() inside a per-item loop poisons every later item, and the traceback names a greenlet, not the rollback. The sweep caught a per-book ValidationError and called await session.rollback(). That expires every non-expunged object in the session, so the next iteration's first attribute access issued a lazy refresh SELECT, which under AsyncSession raises MissingGreenlet. One bad book therefore aborted the whole run, and the error pointed at the innocent book. Do not roll back a session that outlives the failing item; a handler that only records an outcome has nothing to roll back. Make the constraint executable rather than documented: the test double's rollback now raises, so reintroducing the call fails at the call site instead of at a later victim. Applied. applied a705ece1
    AL-618 2026-08-25 ADR-023 personalization, PR #759 review round tooling A changed-file filter that drops sidecars turns the gate green having proved nothing, and the skip is indistinguishable from a pass. skeleton-promotion.yml filtered *.contract.json out before counting changed files, then gated both downstream steps on that count. Starlette's call runs once per response and failing there is correct; the digest's runs once per book inside a listing, so a single blob carrying NaN 500s every book on the shelf. _library_item is explicitly built to tolerate that input, defaulting the field and logging a warning.     AL-622 2026-08-25 ADR-023 personalization, PR #759 review round process A gapless id sequence is a global invariant enforced per file, so two branches can each be internally valid and jointly invalid, and neither branch's CI can see it. check_lessons_log.py requires ids to be exactly consecutive from 001. PR #753 and PR #759 both branched from a main at AL-601; #753 claimed AL-602 through AL-610 and #759 claimed AL-602 through AL-613, so they overlapped on nine rows while each file passed its own branch's gate. A union resolution would have produced duplicate ids that fail the same check. #753 merged first, so #759's twelve rows renumbered to AL-611 through AL-622 during the rebase. The register avoided this only because it tolerates gaps, so its ids can move before merge. Treat the collision as an id-set diff and renumber plus merge as one commit, never as a text conflict resolution. The shift cannot be applied blindly to every row: a row whose own subject is the contested ids reads as a true statement about the wrong range afterwards, so this row had to be rewritten by hand rather than shifted.     AL-623 2026-08-25 PR #760 review fixes (three independent reviews) validator A tri-state whose fail-closed arm and whose benign arm are both falsy cannot be read with a truthiness test, and strict typing does not catch the one shape that gets it wrong. personalizable_slot_ids_for_* answers three things about a story's declared personalizable slots: a populated frozenset (these are declared), an EMPTY frozenset (none could legitimately exist, so any sentinel present is FORGED), and, spelled None, "the contract could not be recovered, fail closed". The last two are opposites and both falsy, so a single if not slots: collapsed the fail-closed arm into the benign one with nothing left to notice. BasedPyright strict already caught the OTHER way to mishandle it (passing frozenset \| None where a plain frozenset was wanted has always been an error), so a truthiness test was the single shape that type-checked perfectly and still routed a security control the wrong way. Giving the fail-closed arm its own marker type whose __bool__ returns NoReturn closes it twice over: the type gate rejects if, if not, while, assert, ternary conditions and comprehension guards, and a value reaching an untyped path still raises. Two residues the fix does NOT close, and they are the reusable part. First, bool(x), x or y and x and y type-check CLEAN and raise only at runtime, and generation/persistence.py prescribed bool(...) in prose as the house recipe until this PR corrected it. Second, the marker's SIBLING ("the caller passed no override") stayed truthy, so the residual union after narrowing the fail-closed arm away was truthiness-testable again, safe only by the order in which pipeline.py happened to narrow the two. When a union carries a fail-closed member, no arm may share falsiness with a benign arm: give the fail-closed arm a marker type whose __bool__ returns NoReturn, and give EVERY marker in that union the same treatment, because narrowing one re-opens the hole on the next. Add a repo check that greps unions carrying a fail-closed member for if not x, bool(x), x or and x and, since the type gate cannot see the last three. Fourth occurrence of this shape after AL-306, AL-582 and AL-583. open UW-C376
    AL-624 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, Tasks 1, 2, 4, 6, 11 validator A write-once report store needs a report-health predicate evaluated at every consumer, because render-time defenses keyed on fields newer than the stored rows structurally miss legacy data. moderation_report is write-once JSONB (immutable at rest absent an explicit pipeline re-run); 12 in-review production books carry a 100 percent fail-safe report from the 2026-07-21 mock-reviewer incident, unchanged since. Newer logic added to the review surface (tiered severity counts, a structural collapse row) reads the SAME fields a real report would carry, so it cannot tell a report that found nothing from a report that never ran a real classifier: both look like zero findings on any field newer code checks. The distinguishing signal has to come from the report's own content (the fail-safe/mock-reviewer marker literals in moderation/stages.py and moderation/insights.py), not from field presence or recency. Built moderation_report_unusable() as one shared predicate and threaded it through every consumer that makes a decision or renders a count from a stored report, rather than letting each consumer re-derive freshness independently: the approval gate (publishing/service.py::approve, blocks approving an unusable report), the review surface (api/review_surface.py, collapses it to one structural row instead of counting fail-safe artifacts as findings, and carries the same flag onto the queue item's badge), and the weekly unusable-report detector (scripts/check_moderation_report_health.py). The ops sweep script (scripts/remoderate_books.py) deliberately does NOT call this predicate: its _is_mock_moderated() selection function is a separate ANY-match test over the same underlying constants (FAIL_SAFE_MESSAGE_SUBSTRING, MOCK_MODERATED_CONCERNS), since a re-moderation candidate needs only one fail-safe finding while approval-blocking requires every finding to be a fail-safe artifact. Any future decision/count consumer of moderation_report must call the shared predicate rather than inferring health from which fields are populated. open UW-C377
    AL-625 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, Task 10 floor calibration (gate D3) validator A single global advisory-persistence floor cannot separate clean-prose noise from adversarial signal, because the categories that carry the noise are disjoint from the categories the adversarial corpus needs kept sensitive. Measured candidate floors {0.01, 0.02, 0.05, 0.10} against the 2026-08-01 Stage-0 baseline (120 clean records, 13 adversarial records with OpenAI scores): clean-prose persistence falls from 0.83 to 0.18 advisories per node as the floor rises from 0.01 to 0.10, driven almost entirely by violence and violence/graphic (p95 0.25 and 0.09 on clean prose against every other category's p95 under 0.015); but raising the floor enough to clear the 0.2 advisories/node clean target (0.10 is the only candidate that does) also crosses the score of 10 of the 14 adversarial (passage, attribute) pairs that persisted under the old floor, including one of the two sexual/sexual-minors-shaped probes. No candidate in the set satisfies both "clean prose stays quiet" and "no adversarial attribute already caught goes silent"; the two goals move in strictly opposite directions across the whole range measured.     AL-626 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, Task 3 controller ruling process A plan can specify a persistence detail that conflicts with an existing shipped data contract elsewhere in the codebase, and only reading the contract, not the plan, surfaces it.     AL-627 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, PR #764 docs pass validator Retiring a classifier's call site can silently orphan the standalone baseline script's copy of that classifier's threshold, because the two live far enough apart that nothing forces them to change together. a5abb2b4 retired Perspective as a Stage-0 signal source, deleting _run_perspective/_perspective_attribute_finding and unwiring the pipeline call site. scripts/capture_stage0_baseline.py's _PERSPECTIVE_BRIGHTLINE_MIN_SCORE = 0.8 was never itself wrong, but its only pinning test (test_recorded_perspective_brightline_matches_the_live_classifier) imported the now-deleted function directly and had to be deleted to clear an ImportError, rather than rewritten against a replacement, because there is no replacement to pin against.     AL-628 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, PR #764 docs pass tooling A frontend gate that re-derives a backend security predicate in a second language has no mechanism forcing the two implementations to change together, and a comment asking a future editor to remember is not that mechanism. frontend/src/admin/ReviewDetailPage.tsx's needsOverride recomputes, in TypeScript, the same severe-finding condition the backend's severe_finding_counts() computes in Python, guarded only by a #CRITICAL: security comment asking future edits to keep the two in lockstep.     AL-629 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, PR #764 docs pass validator A pipeline-artifact finding built for one purpose (collapsing a per-node outage into one story-level row) can silently satisfy the trigger condition of a second, unrelated gate that was never designed with it in mind. moderation/stages.py collapses a per-node moderation-reviewer outage into a single Finding(verdict=Verdict.FLAG, severity=FindingSeverity.HIGH, structural=True, concern="reviewer_unavailable"), a fix this same PR makes for the write-once-report problem AL-624 describes. severe_finding_counts(), which feeds the admin override-reason requirement, counts BLOCK/high-FLAG verdicts with no check of the structural field, unlike its siblings (api/review_surface.py's tiered counts, moderation/repair.py), both of which explicitly exclude structural findings.     AL-630 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, PR #764 docs pass (coordinator-supplied, independently verified) validator An "unusable report" predicate built as existence-of-one-genuine-finding, rather than coverage-of-nodes, clears a report the moment a single node was judged, and a same-PR rendering rule can make the remaining unjudged nodes actively invisible rather than merely uncounted. moderation_report_unusable()'s per-finding loop returns False (usable) at the first entry carrying a non-empty verdict, with no comparison of judged-node count against total nodes. The two mechanisms compound: a book can clear the mandatory-human-approval gate this PR hardens while most of its nodes were never judged by anything, and the reviewer sees no visual cue that coverage was incomplete. Reported (not independently re-measured by this author; attribute to whoever ran the census): sk_clocktower_cipher at 22 of 25 nodes with no readability verdict, sk_hollow_lighthouse at 24 of 148. Make the unusable-report predicate (or a sibling coverage check) compare judged-node count against total node count rather than testing for the existence of one genuine finding, and/or stop collapsing a soft-stage fail-safe into Verdict.PASS so it stays distinguishable from a real pass on the review surface.     AL-631 2026-08-25 moderation-review-hardening plan, PR #764 docs pass (coordinator-supplied, independently verified) validator When a detection predicate has multiple arms meant to catch the same population, an arm gated on infrastructure introduced after the population existed is dead against that population from the moment it ships, leaving only the arms that key on content. moderation_report_unusable()'s reviewer_independent is False arm is written only by moderation/pipeline.py::_stamp_mock_reviewer, gated on the mock provider being active outside local and introduced in 8ca8d1b3 (2026-07-30, PR #496); the mock reviewer's own provider-level independence flag is separately hardcoded True (moderation/review_provider.py), so neither mechanism can retroactively mark a pre-existing row. The 12 in-review production books this PR's moderation_report_unusable() exists to find (AL-624) came from an incident on 2026-07-21, nine days before the stamp existed, and moderation_report is write-once JSONB, so none of the 12 carry the stamp or its concern. Only the FAIL_SAFE_MESSAGE_SUBSTRING message-literal arm reaches this population, making one string constant the sole detector for the exact rows this predicate was built to catch. AL-624 already states the general principle (the signal must come from the report's own content, not from field presence or recency); this lesson is the residual single-point-of-failure that principle leaves in place. Treat the message-literal arm as safety-critical and add a regression test pinning it against the legacy corpus's exact shape, so a future rename or rewording of the fail-safe message cannot silently un-detect the 12 books with no other arm able to catch the regression. open UW-C384
    AL-632 2026-08-25 PR #764 review-fix coordination (FixBackend test rename during commit staging) tooling Renaming or deleting a test file orphans every #VERIFY citation that names it, anywhere in the tree, and check-rad-citations does not surface that at the time of the rename because the rename never touches a path the pre-commit hook is scoped to. FixBackend renamed test_approve_over_block_with_whitespace_only_reason_returns_400 to ..._returns_422 in tests/integration/test_approval_api.py. That orphaned a pre-existing citation at src/cyo_adventure/publishing/service.py:489, written in commit 94c54c77 naming the old _400 suffix. The hook's files: filter covers only src/, scripts/, frontend/src/, and the baseline file, excluding tests/ entirely; a commit staging service.py alone passed clean, because the citation's own line was unchanged and the hook only re-resolves citations within the files it is handed. The mismatch surfaced only once a second, unrelated commit happened to stage tests/integration/test_approval_api.py itself. So the blast radius of a rename stays invisible at commit time until some other commit incidentally touches the citing file, and in between, a green local hook reads as proof nothing is wrong when the tree-wide picture is already broken. Verified before proposing, per the script's own module docstring: --all mode already performs exactly this tree-wide resolution, and the rad-citations CI job already runs --all on every push, pull_request, and merge_group, so CI is already the authoritative full-tree gate and cannot miss this case; the gap is local timing, not a missing mode. Teach the pre-commit hook to detect a staged rename or deletion of a tests/**/test_*.py file (git diff --cached --diff-filter=RD) and escalate only that case to a full --all resolution, so the developer's own commit catches an orphaned citation immediately rather than waiting for CI or an incidental later commit to the citing file. open UW-C385
    AL-633 2026-08-25 PR #764 review-fix coordination (coordinator's blocked first commit attempt, verbatim hook output) tooling check-rad-citations caught three of the four stale citations from this branch's session exactly as designed, and the shape that evaded it (AL-632) is genuinely distinct from the shapes it caught. The coordinator's first commit attempt was blocked with: src/cyo_adventure/api/node_edit.py:741: tests/unit/test_node_edit.py::test_missing_openai_key_outside_local_is_recorded_as_degraded: tests/unit/test_node_edit.py defines no such test and src/cyo_adventure/moderation/rescreen.py:662: tests/unit/test_rescreen_unit.py::test_missing_openai_key_outside_local_does_not_pass_clean: tests/unit/test_rescreen_unit.py defines no such test, exiting with 2 stale RAD #VERIFY citation(s). Both named tests FixBackend wrote afterward; commit d7fb8b67 is the first commit where each citation and its test co-occur, consistent with the blocked attempt never becoming a git object. A third shape, reported firsthand by the coordinator and unfalsifiable from git history for the same reason: schemas.py briefly carried a same-file rename orphan after FixBackend's ..._returns_400 to ..._returns_422 rename, hand-fixed before the first commit attempt. My own initial check (a live --all run plus existence checks against the current tree) could only see the post-repair state and wrongly concluded the claim did not hold; a clean check AFTER a same-session repair cannot see the defect that preceded the repair, so 'currently clean' and 'was stale mid-session' are both true and not in tension. Two citations naming tests that do not yet exist, and a same-file rename orphan, are both already caught by the existing hook at commit time because the citing file is within its src:-scoped files: filter; no gate change is proposed for either shape. When a #VERIFY citation is checked only after a repair, on request, whether from a live run or a working copy, that check answers the CURRENT state and cannot refute a claim about a PRIOR, already-repaired state; verifying a historical claim requires the pre-repair evidence (hook output, or a commit before the repair), not a fresh run. open UW-C386
